events.event_narrative: Arctic air came over the Divide on the morning of the 20th with snow and wind resulting in low visibility at Marias Pass and Essex. The snow and wind impact spread westward on US Highway 2 reaching Bad Rock Canyon by early afternoon with wind gusts to 50 miles per hour and heavy snow. Total snow amounts of 6 to 9 inches were common. Snow drifts to 4 feet were reported at Hungry Horse with a few power outages between West Glacier and Essex.

Arctic winds blasted into the Flathead Valley during the early afternoon accompanied by snow. Glacier Park International Airport reported a peak gust to 47 miles per hour and blowing snow for 7 hours. Most areas only received an inch or two of new snow but the town of Whitefish picked up 9 inches of snow.

Arctic air rushed over the Divide in the early afternoon of the 20th with wind and snow causing difficult travel. Most areas received between 1 and 3 inches of snow with wind gusts to 40 miles per hour.
Snowfall rates up to 1 inch per hour fell during the morning hours, but limited travel impacts were noted. Pierce received 7.4 inches of snow.

High elevations above 6000 feet observed wind chills to -63 degrees and wind gusts to 60  miles per hour. Lower elevations experienced wind chills of -25 to -35 degrees with wind gusts to 35 miles per hour. Big Mountain Ski Area didn't open the summit chair lift on the 22nd due to the extreme cold.

High elevations above 6000 feet observed wind chills to -60 degrees and wind gusts to 60  miles per hour. Lower elevations experienced wind chills of -25 to -35 degrees with wind gusts to 30 miles per hour. Montana Snowbowl Ski Area closed on the 22nd due to the extreme cold.
Wind chills of -25 to -35 degrees with wind gusts to 40 miles per hour were common. Discovery Ski Area closed on the 22nd due to the extreme cold.

The Grangeville and Cottonwood areas had received 15 to 17 inches of snow with off and on periods of blowing and drifting by the end of December 2021. Southerly winds ramped up by the beginning of the new year, and reached a climax from the late morning to the afternoon on the 3rd as sustained winds between 40 and 50 mph and gusts nearing 70 mph occurred. Initially severe drifting was reported on Whitebird Grade and vicinity, where a spotter reported 2 to 3 foot drifts over their country road by the morning of the 2nd. When the winds ramped up by 4 am on the 3rd, severe drifting up to 4 feet high shut down Idaho 64. By 10 am on the 3rd, the 50 to 60+ mph winds and severe drifting shut down US-95 between Cottonwood and Grangeville until 2 am on the 4th. Other impacts include: Idaho 162 and many other prairie roads were shut down due to drifting snow, spotty power outages, schools were closed, roads stayed icy and intense drifting snow with wind gusts to 61 mph were reported on top of Greer Grade on the 3rd.

SNOW SQUALL Snowfall rates between 2 and 3 inches per hour were reported in Missoula. Severe driving conditions were hoisted by Montana Department of Transportation between Tarkio and Frenchtown from 16:47 to 18:26 MST.

SNOW SQUALL Dual pol radar confirmed similar heavy snowfall rates were possible with the band over Interstate 90. Severe driving conditions were hoisted by the MDT on Highway 12 between Garrison and Avon.

Freezing rain led to severe driving conditions and school closures from Troy to Libby to Marion on US-2. Periods of moderate to heavy snowfall occurred with amounts ranging from 9 inches in Marion, 10 inches Bull Lake, over a foot of snow between Troy and Libby and a whopping 18.5 inches at Troy. Gusty winds between Dickey Lake and Fortine caused drifting snow on US-93. One spotter located in higher terrain above and south of Rexford reported a total snowfall amount of 24 inches.

Moderate amounts of snow fell within two days and brought 8 to 12 inches of snow from West Glacier to Marias Pass. Montana Department of Transportation hoisted severe driving conditions on US-2 from 5 miles west of Marias Pass to Browning due to blowing and drifting snow from strong southwest winds gusting to 36 mph on the morning of the 7th.
An arctic weather system brought 4 to 8 inches of snow from the Flathead Valley to Polson and 2 to 4 inches of snow in the Mission Valley. This resulted in snow-covered roads and slick travel.

Periods of moderate to heavy snow fell early on the 6th which resulted in multiple school closures from St. Regis to Alberton. Heavy snow kept falling in the mountains but changed to freezing rain in the valleys by daybreak on the 7th. Severe driving conditions were reported on Highway 200. Power outages were reported between Thompson Falls and Trout Creek. Snow amounts ranged from 6 to 12 inches in the valleys, 12 inches Haugan, 16 inches Heron and over 2 feet in the mountains.

Multiple avalanches occurred on Interstate 90 with full blockage of the driving lane on the westbound side from mile-markers 7.5 to 10, situated west of Saltese. Estimating from the MDT photo, the largest slide was 5 feet tall and between 100 to 300 feet wide. The westbound lanes were closed the following night due to further avalanche risk.

Moderate to heavy snow, amounting between 5 and 10 inches fell initially before changing to freezing rain. Roads became very icy which resulted in multiple vehicle crashes, school closures and delays.

Over 2 feet of heavy, wet snow fell at both Lolo Pass, and south of Conner to Lost Trail Pass, and caused hazardous road conditions. Heavy snowfall increased the avalanche risk which resulted in the closure of US-12 west of Lolo Pass for a total of 3 days. Severe driving conditions were reported on US-12 between Lolo and Lolo Pass for 3 hours on the morning of the 8th.

In the first part of the storm, 9 to 15 inches of heavy snow fell, and disrupted travel. The snow changed to freezing rain by the 7th which created icy, and severe driving conditions. Facebook reports mentioned that a multi-vehicle pile-up stopped traffic near Clinton on Interstate 90 during the morning of the 7th.
Highway 200 was blocked by an avalanche just east of Bonner at mile marker 3. The dimensions were approximately 100 feet wide by 5 feet high.

Periods of moderate to heavy snow fell, ranging from near 8 inches at both Philipsburg and Butte, to 14 inches at both 7 miles west of Anaconda, and in Ovando. Severe driving conditions were hoisted near daybreak on the 5th between Anaconda and Warm Springs. Interstate 90 was closed for a period between Butte and Whitehall on the morning of the 6th due to several tractor trailers that had slid off the road. Road conditions were very slick between Garrison and MacDonald Pass where a plow slid off the roadway during the storm.

Heavy snowfall totals amounted to around 2 feet in the area which resulted in poor driving conditions and a few power outages. Pierce received a 3 day snowfall total of 20.6 inches through the 7th, which was the 7th highest snowfall during any time of the year since 1963.

More than 2 feet of heavy snow fell across the region with the Idaho Department of Transportation stating that the snow rates were up to 3 inches per hour at times. US-12 between Kooskia and Powell was closed from 2 pm PST Jan. 6 through 4 pm Jan. 9 due to avalanche and treefall danger. It was estimated that 150 trees fell due to the weight of the snow along the highway. Also a large avalanche occurred at milepost 136. Power outages were reported east of Kooskia and also in the Elk City area.

A large avalanche, more than 10 feet deep and up to 40 feet wide was triggered by heavy snow near milepost 136 on US-12. This along with treefall caused the highway to be closed for 3 days. The last time an avalanche crossed US-12 was in 2008. The date and time of the avalanche is a coarse estimate.

Heavy snow amounts during this event included 10 inches on the Camas Prairie, 12.5 inches in Orofino, 14.8 inches located west-northwest of Orofino, and 18.5 inches in Woodland. Multiple trees fell onto US-12 between Orofino and Kamiah which halted plowing operations and damaged power lines. Besides a plethora of power outages, there were area-wide school closures and delays.

events.cz_name: LOWER HELLS CANYON / SALMON RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: A CoCoRaHS spotter located 3 miles southwest of Riggins reported 10.4 inches of snow in 3 days ending on the 7th. When compared to the longer Riggins climate record, this is within the top 10 highest snowfall for that area. The Riggins school closed due to heavy snow.
Heavy snow fell, ranging from 16 inches in Salmon to 22 inches in Gibbonsville over a 3 day period, and caused difficult travel in Lemhi County.

Severe driving conditions were hoisted by 8 am on the 12th in Bull Lake, Troy to the Lincoln County Airport. One Facebook report mentioned that four wheel drive vehicles with studded tires would slide sideways due to the standing water on top of ice on the country roads in Trego.

Periods of wet snow and rain brought slick roads. A park ranger said that the conditions were more of a wet slush. A spotter in Coram reported that sidewalks were slick from freezing rain during the evening of the 11th.

Rain developed during the late evening hours and caused slick roads across the western Flathead Valley. Ponding of water was common, especially on Farm to Market Road where a couple of cars slid off the road by 8 am on the 12th.

Multiple people reported very slick conditions due to the freezing rain. One person on Facebook reported that Blue Slide Road in Thompson Falls was the worst ice they had ever experienced since 1982. Another mentioned that they were going 10 mph and lost control. The slick roads continued through the 12th as someone from Sanders County reported that the roads were a sheet of ice. Several schools were delayed and two jackknifed trucks were reported on I-90 west of Alberton.
Roads and sidewalks became a sheet of ice from the freezing rain and caused: dozens of accidents with some injuries, several people fell on the ice and several school delays and closures.
Black ice was reported by Montana Department of Transportation on US-12 between Lolo and Lolo Pass. Chains were required at Lolo Pass.

Several intense rain showers moved over Interstate 90 between Alberton and Superior,  and caused ice accretion and slick conditions. The eastbound lane was closed for several hours due to an overturned truck and two jackknifed tractor trailers.

Showers brought around a tenth of an inch of ice accretion to the Missoula area which caused several vehicle crashes, an ambulance to slide off the road and a vehicle with a trailer to get jackknifed on I-90.
Showers caused I-90 to become slick and caused two jackknifes and a slide-off between Clinton and Bearmouth. Black ice was also reported between Bonner and Potomac.
Williams Creek Summit received between 18 and 24 inches of snowfall.

A spotter in Colombia Falls, MT measured 4 inches of snow that fell in 3 hours. Additionally, weather stations around the area measured wind chills in the negative single digits throughout the day on the 8th.

Very low visibilities along with several inches of snow could be seen at the Hungry Horse bridge on a Montana DOT camera around 8:30 pm. Throughout the day of the 8th, multiple reporting stations measured wind chills in the negative 20s.

There was a report of 6 inches plus of snow in Connor, MT and snow covered road surfaces in the vicinity of Connor, near US-93. Additionally, weather stations measured wind chills in the negative single digits.
There was a report of 4.5 inches of snow near Clinton, MT and Potomac schools had a 2-hour delay due to icy roads.

The Idaho Department of Transportation weather and webcam sensors indicated visibility below a quarter of a mile along with wind gusts up to 25 mph at Lost Trail Pass. Road temperatures during the snow squall dropped from 35 to 29 degrees Fahrenheit, indicating the likelihood of a flash freeze.

A snow squall produced snowfall rates of 3 inches per hour. Visibility of one quarter mile or less and frequent wind gusts of 30 to 40 mph was observed. 1.4 inches of wet snow was observed at the Missoula Weather Forecast Office between 8:00 pm and 830 pm MDT.

Downed trees damaged utility infrastructure along SR 508, in Libby, and in the Ashley Lake area. At least 1,500 customers were without power across the zone. In the Ashley Lake area, a few broken power poles were observed along with damage to a large main feeder.
Wind gusts of 70 to 80 mph were observed above 6,000 feet. High winds downed trees in Essex and Hungry Horse leading to power outages.

High winds damaged utility infrastructure and downed trees across the Flathead Valley. Farm to Market Road in Whitefish closed due to downed trees and power lines. Downed trees and power lines were also observed in Columbia Falls, where a spotter recorded a wind gust of 55 mph.
High winds knocked down trees in Thompson Falls; 500 customers lost power. In St. Regis, high winds downed a ponderosa pine tree, injuring and hospitalizing a local resident.

A peak wind gust of 67 mph was reported at the Missoula International Airport at 11:40 pm MST on April 4th. High winds and strong low level wind shear diverted two flights on approach to KMSO. Power outages were observed in Missoula, Frenchtown, and Hamilton.
A peak wind gust of 59 mph was observed on Mt. Sentinel outside of Missoula.

A peak wind gust of 67 mph was observed at Point Six northeast of Missoula. The Montana Department of Transportation reported down trees in southbound lane on Montana State Highway 83 at milepost 34. The Seeley Lake Ranger Station reported two live trees, 25 to 30 inches in diameter, were snapped about four feet off the ground. Downed trees were also reported in the Big Larch Campground.

Widespread wind gusts of 50 to 70 mph were observed across the Orofino and Grangeville region. High winds in Orofino downed trees and damaged utility infrastructure, leading to power outages. A downed tree totaled an RV trailer in a park west of Orofino.
Two teenager kayakers drowned on Swan Lake following the development of strong offshore winds.

The Lincoln Electric COOP reported 1700 customers without power, with specific impacts in Olney, Dickey Lake, Wolf Prairie, Burma, the Indian Creek area, and Lupfer. Utility crews reported numerous downed and/or damaged trees. Furthermore, 15 to 20 trees fell onto power lines.
Over 100 customers lost power in the Swan Lake area as a tree fell onto a powerline.

Mission Valley Power reported downed trees on Finley Point and in the Synder Hill and Addy Lane areas. Utility crews reported two broken power poles and multiple downed lines. Downed trees in Bigfork and Ferndale led to power outages.
A minor power outage was reported in Greenough Park. A large fir tree was downed in McCormick Park. A poorly maintained building experienced shingle damage off 14th Street and Russel Street.
A cluster of convective snow showers impacted the Flathead Valley, where 4 to 8 inches of snow was observed. Icy roads led to school delays.

Department of Transportation webcams at Lolo and Lost Trail Passes indicate several hours of heavy snow and blowing snow occurred. Trained spotters reported 8 inches of snow in Sula. At least 14 inches of snow was reported in the Lost Trail Pass area. The Montana Department of Transportation declared severe driving conditions on US Highway 12 over Lolo Pass.

Heavy snow and icy conditions led to numerous accidents along the I-90 and I-15 corridors in the Butte region. The Basin Creek SNOTEL in the Highland Mountains south of Butte, reported a 26 inch snow depth increase in 13 hours. A foot or more of snow was reported in Butte's Terra Verde Heights.

events.cz_name: LOWER HELLS CANYON / SALMON RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: The Idaho County Sherriff's Office reported low visibility in heavy snow and blowing snow on US 95 over Whitebird Hill and advised citizens to stay home if possible. US 95 was closed over Whitebird Hill due to an accident.
Heavy snow in Salmon led to school closures on April 12th. Five inches of snow was reported in nearby Carmen.

The Idaho County Sherriff's Office reported low visibility in snow and blowing snow in the Grangeville area and encouraged citizens to avoid unnecessary travel. Chains were recommended for travelers heading for Whitebird Hill. Six inches of snow was observed in Grangeville.
Heavy snow was observed across the southern Clearwater Mountains, with 9.4 inches of snow being reported in Dixie.

Four to eight inches of snow was observed. Mild temperatures limited travel impacts. The Montana Department of Transported required chains for towing units during the early morning hours of April 29th as two semis spun out.
Thunderstorm wind caused trees and power lines to be down near the intersection of Caribel and Glenwood in northeast Kamiah. Power outages were reported from Orofino to Woodland and Kamiah.
A person on Facebook reported large hail south of Weippe.
Facebook report showed jagged hail stone next to a ruler. They reported that their car windshield was damaged and there were dents. A neighbor's car windshield was also damaged.

A person on Facebook reported golf ball sized hail that dented their vehicle and killed one of their chickens. Another person in the area reported minor damage to a chicken coop, damage to gardens and minor damage to vehicles.

Two to three feet of new snow was observed at the Noisy Basin and Stahl Peak SNOTELs. Noisy Basin reported a snow water equivalent increase of 9.70 inches with 7.80 inches at Stahl Peak. The Glacier National Park plow crew reported 18 to 24 inches of new snow on the Going-to-the-Sun Road at 6250 feet elevation.  Slushy road conditions were even reported at Marias Pass on Highway 2. Whitefish Ski Resort had to cancel all activities because of the late season snowfall.

Multiple large, mature Colorado spruce and ponderosa pine trees were blown down along with smaller deciduous trees across the Mission Valley. Shingle damage also occurred on several homes with power outages in Pablo.
Several reports of 1.00 inch hail.
A Facebook report of 1.00 inch hail in Arlee.
A Facebook report of half dollar size hail just west of Potomac.
Quarter size hail in the Rattlesnake area to the northeast of Missoula.

The South Fork of the Clearwater River went into minor flood stage leading to flooding of low-lying areas and adjacent roads. Johnston Cutoff Road and Tolo Lake Road west of Grangeville also experienced road closures because of water flowing across the roadway.

The Yaak River near Troy reached minor flood stage with limited impact noted. More significant impacts occurred along Hwy 508 between US Highway 2 and Yaak, as debris and water across the road resulted in a closure for much of June 14.

Several areas of flooding and debris flows occurred, mainly on June 15. Trumbull Creek west of Columbia Falls, flooded a dozen homes near Highway 2 with water on to the highway. Flooding also occurred on North Hilltop Road along Garnier Creek and Blankenship Road near Columbia Falls with water running across Highway 2 from nearby hillsides. Debris flows occurred on the west side of Hungry Horse Reservoir forcing the closure of West Side Road in the Graves Creek area.

The Flathead River at Columbia Falls reached minor flood stage on June 12 as Flathead Lake reached full pool, and continued at minor flood stage until June 26. Impacts included groundwater flooding agricultural fields along the Steel Bridge Road. Also water flooded recreational vehicle sites and surrounded some trailer homes just northwest of the Highway 35 bridge over the Flathead River. This event did prompt Flathead County to spin up an Emergency Operations Center with the Sheriff as the IC.
The Clark Fork River above Missoula briefly reached minor flood stage with limited impacts of water into low lying areas adjacent to the river.
The Bitterroot River near Missoula briefly reached minor flood stage with limited impacts of water into low lying areas adjacent to the river.

Plugged culverts and heavy rainfall contributed to flooding on Main Street in Grangeville and also in Cottonwood. Rock slides and mud slides were reported along Highway 95 between Riggins and White Bird and also along Big Salmon Road east of Riggins. Rock slides, mud slides and fallen trees occurred on Highway 12 between Kooskia and Jerry Johnson Hot Springs. Water from Sevenmile Creek also flowed over Highway 162 at milepost 20. Debris flow caused the Lolo Creek bridge along the Clearwater and Idaho County line to wash out. The Clearwater River at Stites briefly spiked up to 8.86 feet in the minor flood category, but no major impacts were noted.
A person from Conner mentioned that quarter size hail ruined their garden.
A report of 1 diameter hail was received just east of Sula, MT.
An owner of a general store reported large hail causing dented vehicles and trailers, holes in window screens, and damaged field crops.
One inch hail was reported from a storm that had a relatively small core of 55-60 dbz returns. There were no damage reports from this event.

Radar indicated 60 dbz reflectivity to 30k feet MSL, and there was evidence of meso-cyclone rotation in velocity products. A spotter reported 0.88 hail with no reports of damage in Georgetown Lake. Another member of the public reported seeing a funnel cloud from the storm south of Phillipsburg.
Both the Flathead Bio Station and a spotter 13 mi northeast of Polson reported 1/2 inch hail, resulting in unknown quantity of plant and leaf damage.

A spotter in Bigfork, MT sent in a photo showing 1 1/2 inch hail. Near Lakeside on Flathead Lake a cherry orchard reported a total loss of their cherry and apple crop from 125 trees, and they had to replace all their screens on one side of the house and a larger cherry producer in Bigfork reported a total loss.
A trained spotter reported 1 1/2 inch hail along with near continuous lighting. She also reported minor damage to trees with a few leaves shredded.

Local reports between Stevensville and Florence, MT varied between 1 to 1.50 for hail size, with damage to cars, trees, and at least one garden. Damage to trees, and a barn blown over in Stevensville, suggested estimated wind gusts to near 70 mph emanating from the storm.

This storm that moved generally from Lakeside northeast to the Flathead Valley just north of Echo Lake produced two reports of 1 inch hail. One of those reports was from Somers and the other along HWY-35 just north of Bigfork, MT.

There were multiple reports from Kalispell, MT of 1.75 to 2.5 hail which caused extensive  body and windshield damage to vehicles. Additionally, multiple homes sustained damage, especially roofs that needed to be replaced. One homeowner spent $80,000 US dollars to replace their roof. A patio umbrella in Evergreen, MT was shredded. The property damage estimate could be underdone.
One inch hail was reported on the 'eastside' of Florence, MT.

There was a report of 1.25 hail from a storm that traversed the southern portions of Flathead Lake. Two greenhouse businesses in Jette, MT reported nickel size hail, or 7/8. A greenhouse received significant damage.
A photo on Twitter depicted 1 hail in Seeley Lake, MT.
One inch hail was reported south of Grangeville, ID.
One inch hail was reported in Charlo, MT.
Although the largest public report of hail was 3/4 on Deer Mountain east of Darby, MT, radar did estimate 1.25 hail with a reflectivity core of 70 dbz at 33,000 feet.
A member of the public sent in a photo demonstrating 1.25 hail. Hail around 2.5 was reported by an employee of the NWS near Wye, MT.
Two reports of large hail were received, one of .88 around Ravalli ,MT and the second of 1 just south of Ninepipes Reservoir.
A member of the public sent in a photo of 2 hail that fell near Seeley Lake.
A member of the public reported 1 inch hail near Corvalis.
There were two reports of 1 hail near Clinton, followed by another near US-200 2 miles from Potomac, MT.
There were two reports of large hail near Salmon Lake; a Forest Service employee reported 1.5 hail south of the lake, while there was a report of 1.75 hail just east of the lake.
A weather station near I-90, just east of Anaconda measured a wind gust of 64 mph from a thunderstorm.

A RAWS station above the city of Salmon recorded a wind gust to 66 mph. There was extensive damage within Salmon, mainly centered on the southern side of the city. Damage included damage to roofs, RVs blown over, and high school bleachers blown over.
Sporadic power outages were reported around Drummond and Butte, MT as winds gusted from the mid 40s to the mid 50s mph.

Highs temperatures reached from 100 to 108 degrees Fahrenheit with overnight lows in the upper 60s to lower 70s. Pierce ID set record high temperatures on July 29 and August 1, and also remained above 95F for 6 straight days from July 29 to August 3.  This was its 2nd longest such streak.

With high temperatures ranging from 95 to 104F over 5 days, this was the hottest period of the summer. Missoula set record high temperatures 4 straight days from July 29 through Aug 1, and remained 100F or warmer for high temperatures for 5 consecutive days.  This tied the longest streak of 100F days ever.

events.cz_name: LOWER HELLS CANYON / SALMON RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Highs temperatures reached from 105 to 113 degrees Fahrenheit, with overnight lows in the upper 60s to lower 70s.
The hail accumulated to a depth of 2 feet.

Significant hail damage to multiple residences was observed, including broken windows, damaged siding, and crop losses. Wind driven hail broke through windows. Canola and wheat crops were flattened. A vineyard near Cottonwood was stripped by hail.
Numerous trees were downed by strong winds in the east Kamiah area. Idaho Power and Light reported outages lasting 16 to 24 hours. In Kamiah, wind lifted a 40-foot wide roof into a neighbors yard.
Strong winds downed trees, leading to an extended power outage in the Glenwood area.
Tree damage reported due to strong winds.
Minor damage to vegetation was reported, with lots of leaves down.
A tree was downed on US Highway 12 near mile post 143.
Strong winds damaged trees which led to a power outage in the Elk City area.
Strong winds snapped large limbs, estimated near 4 inches in diameter, off trees.
Ping pong size hail, very heavy rain, and gusty winds were reported at the National Bison Range. A hay crop was destroyed near St. Ignatius. Hail damaged an RV roof.

A person from Hamilton remarked on Facebook that they had downed trees. A driver on Highway 93 saw 3 different trees split and fall between Lolo and Florence. A tree fell on Lost Horse Road with a power line down. Four cottonwood trees were blown down between Lolo and Florence.
General snow amounts of 5-10 inches were reported above 5000 feet with 12-18 inches above 6000 feet on the Darby Ranger District. Roadways over Lost Trail and Lolo passes were snow covered at times.
Up to 12 inches of snow was reported above 6000 feet with significant impacts to backcountry users.

Snow amounts were highly variable but SNOTELs above 6000 feet reported 8-16 inches of new snow. Philipsburg reported 12 inches of snow as well. Interstate 90 at Homestake Pass was closed for 7 hours due to icy conditions and semi-truck slide offs on the evening of the 23rd. Chains were also required for a time on MacDonald Pass.
Up to a foot of snow was observed above 6000 feet, impacting backcountry users. Highway 93 was also slick and snow covered at Lost Trail Pass multiple times.
Snow amounts of 5-10 inches were observed above 5000 feet, impacting backcountry users. Highway 12 was also slick and snow covered at Lolo Pass multiple times.

Between 5 and 7 inches of snow fell between Marion and Kila during the event. There were a few power outages reported in these areas due to tree damage from the heavy weight of the snow. The higher elevation SNOTEL stations picked up 6 to 12 inches of snow.

Over 1600 people were without power in the Swan Lake region due to the heavy snow damage to trees and power lines. The weather observer at the Hungry Horse Dam reported 13 inches of snow from this event while there was a report of near 10 inches in Ferndale.

A utility company in the Flathead Valley reported that this storm caused the most number of individual outages in its history as countless branches and trees fell on the power infrastrucure. Almost 57 percent of the meters on their power lines experienced at least one outage during the event which took 6 days to restore power. More than one thousand customers were without power in the Mission Valley. The city of Kalispell Public Works reported that they had so many trees and branches down everywhere that it took 2 days to clean up the driving lanes. A semi pile-up occurred on Jette Hill, located northwest of Polson. Schools in Lakeside and Somers called off classes for the day. Snow amounts ranged from 4 inches in Polson to 7 inches in Whitefish, and to 10 inches just northwest of Kalispell. The Ferndale are saw 9 to 10 inches of snow.
The Pierce observer reported 5.2 inches of snow while the ITD Grangemont webcam on Highway 11 showed snow-covered roads through mid-morning on the 2nd.
The observer in Dixie reported 3.9 inches of snow while the Lolo Pass SNOTEL recorded a snow depth increase of 3 inches.
The cold front passage brought up to 3.9 inches of snow in the Grangeville area, 3.5 inches in Woodland and 2 inches to Cottonwood.

events.cz_name: LOWER HELLS CANYON / SALMON RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Roads were snow-covered on Whitebird Hill, and the grip level revealed potentially slick conditions during this time.

Very heavy snow caused difficult travel along Interstate 90 and Thompson Pass. Multiple semitrucks became stuck near Lookout Pass because of the deep snow. The Lookout Pass SNOTEL recorded 16 inches of snow depth increase with 2.70 inches of snow water equivalent during this event. The Haugan COOP reported 5 inches of snow. A 39 year old woman passed away after hitting a semitruck head-on near Evaro Hill as road conditions were wet and slick.

Between 16 and 24 inches of heavy snow fell in the mountains across west-central Montana. Chains were required for Lolo Pass during the event. Very high winds in excess of 50 and 60 mph were reported in the higher elevations behind the cold front on the morning of the 5th.

Between 10 and 20 inches of heavy snow fell in the mountains while 8 inches fell at Seeley Lake. After the passage of the cold front, winds gusted as high as 83 mph on the peak of Point 6 Mountain, and to 53 mph in both Clinton and Bearmouth on the morning of the 5th. A tree was reported down on Highway 83 near mile-marker 21, north of Seeley Lake.

SNOTEL stations reported between 2 and 4 inches of snow water equivalent which was mostly in the form of 1 to 2 feet of snow in the mountains. Pierce reported 6.2 inches of snow. Strong gusty winds near 40 mph occurred during and after the heavy snowfall.

The Idaho County Sheriff reported numerous slide-offs and accidents because of the snow-covered roads. Webcams showed heavy wet snow in the lower elevations weighing the trees down and subsequently a power outage occurred thereafter in the Pete King area. SNOTEL stations reported 12 to 16 inches of snow during the event. Strong winds gusting over 50 mph and trees down near Lolo Pass were reported towards the end of the storm.

Heavy wet snow caused power outages on the Camas Prairie and over 1100 customers were without power on the benches above Orofino and Greer Grade. Cottonwood received 5.5 inches while Woodland received 3.5 inches. Winds gusted to 56 mph around daybreak on the 5th in Syringa as a strong cold front pushed through.

events.cz_name: LOWER HELLS CANYON / SALMON RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: The weather sensor at Whitebird Hill reported moderate to heavy snow and slick conditions, along with gusty south winds to 30 mph.
Roughly 20 medium size trees were down with debris along Interstate 90 near Lookout Pass. Several power outages were reported including in the Thompson Falls area, and between Alberton and Superior.

An electric company reported 2,300 members were without power because of the high winds. A weather station northeast of Hot Springs recorded a peak wind gust of 61 mph. Another company reported a power outage along Highway 35 north of Finley Point.

Weather stations in the Whitefish Range reported up to 85 mph wind gusts while lower elevation stations had gusts near 50 mph. Due to the concern for hunters being in the backcountry, the danger for treefall was very high.
A power company reported 402 customers without power due to wind damage in Lincoln County.
Widespread gusts between 50 and 60 mph were recorded in both the Missoula and Bitterroot Valleys. Power outages were reported in both the Missoula and Hamilton areas.

A strong cold front brought wind gusts between 50 and 60 mph across southwest Montana. Trees were observed falling down in the higher elevations just south of Nevada Lake due to the strong winds. A few roadways were covered with a little bit of snow from the the cold front passage. The Bert Mooney Airport south of Butte saw gusts to 55 mph and light snow. The Wise River RAWS reported a wind gust to 61 mph and the sensor north of Avon recorded a peak wind of 60 mph.
Between 2 and 4 inches of snow fell between the Happy's Inn and Marion.

The observer in Alberton reported 1.6 inches of snow, but the main snow band made a direct hit to the Petty Creek and Fish Creek areas where radar estimated precipitation could deduce snow amounts closer to 4 inches.

A snow band produced 1.5 inch per hour rates across the South Hills of Missoula where a total of 4 inches fell. Other location snowfall totals include 2.3 inches in Florence, and 1.6 inches in Hamilton.

The ITD sensor and webcams at Lolo Pass reported heavy snow, with rates potentially as highs as 2 inches per hour (as snow water equivalent hourly values were 0.20 inches). An accident blocked the pass for a few hours. Another location that received heavy snow showers was just northwest of Charlo where 4 inches of snow fell later in the evening.
Two to four inches of snow fell between Swan Lake and Seeley Lake. While only 1.2 fell just southeast of Bonner, radar estimates would suggest that heavier amounts likely occurred towards Clinton.

Snow showers brought several inches of snow to the region, including 3.1 inches in Kila and 2.1 inches in Marion. The slick roads contributed to two fatalities on US-2 west of Libby at 1423MST in the afternoon.

Wind chills fell as low as 16 below zero at Marias Pass, but in the higher elevations wind chill values were as low as 43 below in Glacier National Park. Strong wind gusts close to 50 mph caused tree damage and power outages in the northern Whitefish Lake area and also near Big Mountain. Mountain top easterly arctic winds were very strong over the Whitefish and Swan Ranges and also in Glacier. Garden Wall saw gusts to 72 mph while the top of Mount Aeneas at 7,120 feet, gusted as high as 73 mph during the event.

Strong gusty northeast winds between 40 and 50 mph and wind chills down to 3 below occurred between Glacier Park Int. Airport and Badrock Canyon. The winds limited the snowfall in the eastern Flathead Valley, but up to 2.5 inches fell northwest of the City of Kalispell. Between 2 and 4 inches of snow fell in the Mission Valley, causing slick roads. Sustained northeast winds of 41 mph occurred at Yellow Bay Point. Power outages from the strong winds occurred in the northern Flathead Valley.

Between 1 to 3 inches of snow caused slick conditions along Highway 200 and Interstate 90. Heavy snow showers brought low visibility from 1000 to 1300MST to Evaro Hill and I-90 between Tarkio and Missoula.

Between 2 and 4 inches of snow fell in the Bitterroot Valley and to 1.5 inches in the southern Missoula Valley. The snow fell at moderate to heavy rates at times with showers and squalls. The snow caused slick roads with a few accidents in the region.

Snow Squall Heavy snow combined with gusty east winds sustained at 20 mph with gusts to 30 mph caused low visibility, and slick roads which contributed to several accidents in the Missoula and Bitterroot Valleys. The Missoula Police department issued a MEANS alert due to icy roads and multiple crashes at 1227MST.
Between 1 and 3 inches of snow fell from Clinton to Seeley Lake and Lindbergh Lake which caused slick roads. Heavy snow showers impacted the region from 1040MST to 1500MST.

The arctic cold front pushed west over the Divide by late morning on the 6th, and the east winds became very strong with frequent gusts over 50 mph in the Helmville area from 1800MST Nov. 6 to 1200MST Nov. 7 (Peak gust was 59 mph). Snow showers brought slick roads to the region with snow amounts ranging from a 1 to to 4 inches.

The Shanghi Summit SNOTEL received 5 inches of snow and it also reported heavy snow rates during the event. Other snow amounts ranged from 2 to 4 inches. The Grangemont webcam revealed snow-covered roads during the morning commute.
Between 4 and 6 inches of snow fell in the higher terrain of the Bitterroot and Clearwater Mountains. The snow rates were moderate to heavy at times and brought slick conditions at Lolo Pass.

The Greer Grade webcam showed heavy snow with snow-covered roads and trucks pulled over to the side of the road. A power outage occurred by mid-morning in the region. Snow amounts ranged from 2 to 4 inches including the Camas Prairie.

events.cz_name: LOWER HELLS CANYON / SALMON RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Slick conditions were observed at Whitebird Hill on US-95.

Slick conditions were observed at Lost Trail Pass and Gilmore Summit due to moderate to heavy snow. Drifting at Gilmore due to southerly winds to 26 mph made it difficult to mitigate the snow-covered Highway 28. A weather spotter in Salmon reported 1.5 inches of snow while the Saddle Mountain SNOTEL near Lost Trail reported 5 inches.

The Morgan Creek SNOTEL at 7600 feet reported a snow depth increase of 10 inches with 0.80 inches of snow water equivalent. An estimated foot of snow fell at Williams Creek Summit by a county official.
MDT road crews reported an estimated 8 to 14 inches of heavy snow between Somers and Polson. It was snowing hard enough that they had a hard time keeping up with limited crew early in the season.
Severe driving conditions were hoisted by MDT for US-93 between Evaro and Evaro Hill during the event.  Snow amounts ranged from 5 to 6 inches.

Slick conditions with semi's spinning out led the MDT to issue severe driving conditions on Interstate 90 and also Brooks Street in Missoula. Corvallis schools were delayed. Snowfall totals ranged from 2.4 inches in Stevensville up to 7 inches in southern Missoula, Lolo and Hamilton. Three midday commercial flights to the Missoula International Airport were diverted to Spokane because of the snow.

The SNOTEL at Lolo Pass recorded a snow water equivalent of 0.40 which could equate to around 6 inches while the Black Pine SNOTEL potentially received around 8 inches of snow. Highway 12 was snow-covered and using the swath of snow as a guide, the Rock Creek area could have received 4 or more inches of snow.

Heavy snow brought low visibility and snow-covered roads. Multiple accidents were reported on both Highway 200 and I-90 east of East Missoula. Snow totals include: 11 inches Seeley Lake, 10 inches Bearmouth, 8 inches East Missoula and 7 inches in Potomac.

Heavy snow fell across northern Powell County with snow amounts reported up to 12 inches 3 miles southwest of Ovando. Gusty easterly winds between 10 and 17 mph with gusts to 30 mph were reported at Garrison Junction which caused blowing snow and lower visibility. Other snow amounts include: 4 to 5 inches from Philipsburg to Anaconda and 2.8 inches at Montana Tech in Butte.
Generally 3 to 6 inches of snow fell across the central and eastern parts of Clearwater County.

Between 6 and 12 inches of heavy snow fell across the mountains of Idaho County, especially towards the Montana border. The Dixie COOP reported 9.6 inches and the Mountain Meadows SNOTEL reported close to a foot of snow. Hunters and recreationists were likely negatively impacted due to impassable backcountry roads.

Heavy snow brought slick conditions and low visibility to the region. Snow amounts include: 7 in Kooskia and 6 Grangeville. Moderate to heavy snow brought a brief period of snow-covered conditions at Whitebird Hill on US-95 between 0700 and 0900PST.

The Schwartz Lake SNOTEL received 0.60 inches of snow water equivalent which could equate to around 10 inches. The Leadore COOP reported 3 inches of snow and the ITD webcam at Gilmore Summit showed snow-covered roads.
There were multiple reports of icy roads with a report of freezing rain on US-93 north of Whitefish to the Canadian border on Facebook.
Lookout Pass received close to 6 inches of snow with 0.50 inches of snow water equivalent. Interstate 90 at the pass was snow-covered during the morning hours.
The Grangemont ITD webcam showed heavy snow and snow-covered conditions. Total snow amounts during the event include: 7 inches in 5 hours at the Shanghi Summit and 2.5 inches at Pierce.
The Lolo Pass SNOTEL recorded heavy snow with 3 inches falling from 1400 to 1500PST. Other snow amounts include: 5.6 inches at Dixie and 8 inches at the Twin Lakes SNOTEL.

Snow Squall A heavy burst of snow deposited 2 inches of snow in the Grangeville region that melted and froze on the roadways. A weather spotter reported that the vehicles on US-95 and Johnson Cutoff were bumper to bumper for hours because of icy conditions. The Idaho County sheriff issued a road advisory stating that the US-95 was backed up due to multiple slide offs and accidents. They also stated that Harpster Grade was extremely slick and snow-covered.
Snow Squall A snow band brought heavy snow that melted and refroze onto US-95 towards Frei Hill and Cottonwood, and created icy conditions.
MDT reported that there were low hanging power lines in the vicinity of Essex. At the time, winds were gusting to 76 mph at the Snowslip station which is situated at 7,020 feet in the mountains.

Snow Squall Heavy snow, gusty winds to 37 mph with blowing snow brought whiteout conditions to the Highway 1 and Georgetown Lake area. A person on Facebook remarked that the roads were icing up and there was poor visibility.  A second snow squall brought heavy snow, winds gusting to 42 mph, blowing snow and flash freeze to Highway 12 from Garrison Junction to MacDonald Pass and also to Highway 141 north of Avon.

Snow Squall Severe driving conditions were hoisted by MDT due to whiteout conditions from winds gusting to 46 mph and heavy snow from Garrison Junction to Warm Springs. The low visibility and roads icing up contributed to several vehicle accidents.

Snow Squall Winds gusting between 30 and 40 mph combined with heavy snow caused blowing snow with whiteout conditions and icy roads. Reports from Facebook stated that Homestake Pass was really bad and also at least 2 dozen people were in ditches along Interstate 90 between Missoula and Butte because of icy roads.

Snow Squall Strong wind gusting to 35 mph with blizzard conditions were reported in Salmon. Observations showed that temperatures dropped from near 40 degrees to the upper 20s with the squall which likely contributed to icy conditions. Estimated total snowfall in Salmon was 1 inch while near 8 inches fell at Williams Creek Summit.

The Montana Department of Transportation estimated that around 6 inches fell at Polson and near to over a foot of snow fell between Big Arm and Jette. Mesonet stations in the region were reporting wind gusts 20 to 30 mph out of the northeast which implies blowing and drifting snow occurred in this region. Reports on social media reported slick roadways in the Flathead Valley. Other snow amounts include: 3.8 inches in Kila, 2.5 inches in Ronan and 1.7 inches in the City of Kalispell.
Light to moderate snow showers brought 5 to 6 inches of total snow to Lookout Pass and also along Highway 200 northwest of Thompson Falls.
Pierce received 3.5 inches of snow while the mountains received 4 to 6 inches.
The Dixie observer reported 3.8 inches of snow and webcams revealed periods of light to moderate snowfall down to the valley locations.

Moderate to heavy snow rates from showers produced snow-covered roads. Snow amounts included: 6 inches two miles west of Grangeville, 4.5 inches in Grangeville, 2.7 inches Cottonwood and 1.3 inches in Orofino.

events.cz_name: LOWER HELLS CANYON / SALMON RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Periods of light to moderate snow, with amounts ranging from 1 inch in Riggins to 5 inches at Whitebird, caused slippery roads in the region.

Heavy snow, along with blowing and drifting snow, caused very tough driving conditions across the area. Total snowfall amounts include: 22 inches Bull Lake, 12 to 18 inches Libby and Eureka, 7 to 10 inches in both Yaak and Trout Creek. Snow bands brought periods of moderate to heavy snow to US-93 between Olney and Whitefish during the evening of Dec. 1.

Heavy snow, blowing and drifting snow caused very tough driving conditions across the area. Total snowfall amounts include: 22 inches Bull Lake, 12 to 18 inches Libby and Eureka, 7 to 10 inches in both Yaak and Trout Creek. Snow bands brought periods of moderate to heavy snow to US-93 between Olney and Whitefish during the evening of Dec. 1.

A moist Pacific front, followed by an arctic front initiated very heavy snow rates between 1 to 2 inches per hour, gusty winds to 25 mph with blowing and drifting snow, and very low visibility along US-2 between Hungry Horse and Marias Pass. Heavy snow showers enhanced by the existing arctic air mass caused more accumulation during the later period through early Dec. 2. Total snowfall included: 30 inches Pinnacle, 29.9 inches Essex, 17 inches West Glacier, 16 inches Coram and over 12 inches at Marias Pass.

A moist Pacific front, then arctic front passage initiated very heavy snow rates between 1 to 2 inches per hour, gusty winds to 25 mph with blowing and drifting snow, and very low visibility along US-2 between Hungry Horse and Marias Pass. Heavy snow showers enhanced by the existing arctic airmass caused more accumulation during the later period through early Dec. 2. Total snowfall included: 30 inches Pinnacle, 29.9 inches Essex, 17 inches West Glacier, 16 inches Coram and over 12 inches at Marias Pass.

Moderate snowfall brought snow-covered roads to the Flathead and Mission Valleys. Snowfall amounts include: 6.8 inches east of Pablo, 6 inches Creston, 5.5 inches Glacier Park International, and 3.3 inches in Ronan.

Moderate snowfall brought snow-covered roads to the Flathead and Mission Valleys. Snowfall amounts include: 6.8 inches east of Pablo, 6 inches Creston, 5.5 inches Glacier Park International, and 3.3 inches in Ronan.

Heavy snow fell with total amounts up to 18 inches in Heron, 10 inches in Superior, 8 to 10 inches between Dixon and Trout Creek and 5.6 inches in Alberton. Severe driving conditions were hoisted during the early morning hours of Dec. 1 on I-90 from Lookout Pass to milepost 33. Schools in the region were either delayed or closed because of the snow. Black ice with snow showers caused slick conditions and several semi rollovers during the evening of Dec. 1.

Heavy snow fell with total amounts up to 18 inches in Heron, 10 inches in Superior, 8 to 10 inches between Dixon and Trout Creek and 5.6 inches in Alberton. Severe driving conditions were hoisted during the early morning hours of Dec. 1 on I-90 from Lookout Pass to milepost 33. Schools in the region were either delayed or closed because of the snow. Black ice with snow showers caused slick conditions and several semi rollovers during the evening of Dec. 1.

Snow brought black ice and slick conditions both evenings of Nov. 30 and Dec. 1. A weak arctic front from the north produced gusty north winds to 26 mph and falling temperatures, which in turn caused the wet roads to ice up during the late afternoon and evening of Dec. 1 in the Missoula Valley. Multiple vehicle accidents were reported via social media. Total snowfall includes: 4.7 inches four miles west of Missoula, 3.8 inches at the Missoula International Airport, and 1 inch east of Florence.

Snow brought black ice and slick conditions both evenings of the 30th and Dec. 1. A weak arctic front from the north caused gusty north winds to 26 mph and falling temperatures which caused the wet roads to ice up during the late afternoon and evening of Dec. 1 in the Missoula Valley. Multiple vehicle accidents were reported via social media. Total snowfall includes: 4.7 inches four miles west of Missoula, 3.8 inches at the Missoula International Airport, and 1 inch east of Florence.

Periods of moderate to heavy snow fell in the  mountains. Total snow from the two day event included 12 inches at Lolo Pass and 9 inches at Lost Trail Pass. Chains were required at Lolo Pass during the day on Nov. 30.
Periods of moderate to heavy snow fell in the  mountains. Total snow from the two day event included 12 inches at Lolo Pass and 9 inches at Lost Trail Pass.
Periods of moderate to heavy snow through Dec. 1 brought up to 10 inches of snow four mile north of Seeley Lake, and 6 inches in both Clinton and Condon.
Periods of moderate to heavy snow through Dec. 1 brought up to 10 inches of snow four miles north of Seeley Lake, and 6 inches in both Clinton and Condon.

Snow Squall Heavy snow with strong winds gusting to 30 mph produced widespread blowing snow and whiteout conditions and a dramatic drop in temperatures and icy roads across both Deer Lodge and Silver Bow counties. A weather spotter located seven miles south-southwest of Butte measured 2.5 inches of snow in 1.2 hours. They also recorded a total snowfall of 4.5 inches.
Moderate to heavy snow fell across the region with amounts ranging from 5 to 8 inches.
Very heavy snow rates were observed by SNOTEL stations and the webcam at Grangemont corroborated this. The Hemlock Butte SNOTEL picked up close to 10 inches of snow in 9 hours.
Light to moderate snow showers brought 1 to 4 inches of total snow. The highest amounts were observed along eastern sections of Flathead Lake and the Flathead and Mission Valleys.
Snow showers brought 1 to 2 inches of snow along the Highway 200 corridor from Plains to the Idaho border.
Lindbergh Lake received 7.2 inches of snow with other areas in the Swan Valley seeing 4 to 6 inches. Lesser amounts of 1 to 3 inches were observed along Highway 200 and in Seeley Lake.
Butte and Homestake Pass webcams showed periods of moderate snowfall and winter driving conditions. 2 inches of snow was measured in Butte.
Snow showers led to 1 to 4 inches of accumulation and snow covered roadways across the Missoula and Bitterroot Valleys.

events.cz_name: LOWER HELLS CANYON / SALMON RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: IDT road crews reported 2 inches of snow on US Highway 95 over Whitebird Hill.
Grangeville received 1.5 inches of snow.

MDT webcams highlighted winter driving conditions from snowfall along the I-90 and Highway 200 corridors near the Idaho and Montana border. 3 to 4 inches of snow was reported in the Trout Creek and Noxon areas, where school was delayed 2 hours on December 19th.

Between 2 and 4 inches of snow caused slick road conditions across the US-93 corridor. Snow and blowing snow was observed across northeast portions of the Flathead Valley, where wind chills reached 10 below zero as the arctic front passed.
Pierce received 4.4 inches of snow while the mountains received 5 to 7 inches.

Heavy snow, along with blowing and drifting snow caused very tough driving conditions across the area, particularly from Essex to Marias Pass on US Highway 2. Wind chills fell to 30 to 35 below zero between Essex and Marias Pass and reached as low as 55 below in the mountains of Glacier National Park. Snow totals include: 15 inches in West Glacier and 15.9 inches in Essex.
Temperatures fell between 20 and 41 below. Notable observations include: 41 below Olney, 39 below Yaak, and 31 below in Libby.

Widespread wind chills of 40 to 55 below zero were observed. Snowslip Mountain in Glacier National Park recorded a wind chill of 70 below zero. Temperatures fell to 49 below at Marias Pass, 47 below in Polebridge, 36 below in Hungry Horse, and 34 below in West Glacier.
Wind chills reached 31 below in Thompson Falls and as low as 41 below in the mountains (Mullan Pass). Temperatures fell between 15 and 27 below.

MDT declared severe driving conditions on Interstate 90 from Tarkio to Lookout Pass as snowfall rates up to 2 inches per hour were observed. Wind gusts of 30 to 35 mph led to areas of blowing and drifting snow in the mountains. Between 8 to 14 inches of snow fell along the Highway 200 corridor, which led to cancellations of area schools on December 22.

MDT reported snowfall rates in excess of 1 inch per hour in Libby for 9 consecutive hours. Trained spotters in Libby reported 14 inches of snow. Snow, blowing and drifting snow led to whiteout conditions on US Highway 2 and 93.

Heavy snow and east-northeast winds of 20-30 mph with gusts to 45 mph led to periods of whiteout conditions on US Highway 2 east of West Glacier. MDT and the Essex COOP reported 29 inches of snowfall. 14 inches of snow was measured in West Glacier.

Widespread heavy snowfall, with rates up 2 inches per hour, was observed on December 20th. Snowfall accumulations of 5 to 12 inches was reported, with Bigfork receiving 14 inches. Arctic north-northeast winds of 30 to 50 mph led to widespread blowing and drifting snow on December 21st. Lake County officials declared emergency travel as area roadways became impassable. Flathead County closed Hodgson Road due to drifting snow. Numerous schools announced closures on December 21st.

Wind chills dropped to 30 to 40 below zero across the Flathead Valley and to 30 below in the Mission Valley on the December 21st. Temperatures dropped to 34 below in Kalispell (7th coldest on record) and Hot Springs. Creston dropped to 35 below zero. Several thousand people lost power during the morning of December 21st across the Flathead Valley.

Roadways experienced a flash freeze, and blowing and drifting snow as the arctic front arrived, which led to MDT declaring severe driving conditions. Numerous schools closed due to weather on December 21st.

Wind chills fell to 38 below zero in Missoula as sustained east winds of 15 to 25 mph were observed. Notable low temperatures include: 27 below Frenchtown, 26 below Stevensville, 24 below Hamilton, and 19 below Missoula.

MDT reported a flash freeze, blowing and drifting snow, as the arctic front arrived on December 21st. 12 inches of snow was reported at Lost Trail Pass, with at least 13 inches accumulating at Lolo Pass.

Lost Trail Ski Area closed on December 22 as wind chills dropped to 47 below zero. Widespread wind chills of 40 below or colder were observed across mountain sites. Temperatures dropped between 20 and 30 below, with the Skalkaho summit Snotel hitting 34 below.
Low temperatures on December 22nd reached 49 below in Potomac, and 41 below in Seeley Lake and in Clearwater Junction. Extreme cold closed Snowbowl Ski Area.

Snow, blowing and drifting snow, and dangerous wind chills impacted areas along US Highway 12 and Interstate 90, prompting MDT to declare severe driving conditions. Numerous slide offs occurred between Garrison Junction and Deer Lodge, where visibility below one quarter of a mile was observed by area spotters and mesonets. Wind chills dropped between 30 and 50 below as north-northeast winds reached 20 to 30 mph and temperatures dropped in the teens to low 20s below zero. MacDonald Pass reported a wind chill of 60 below zero.
Temperatures fell between 35 and 43 below zero. Butte dropped to 40 below zero. Discovery Ski Area closed due to extreme cold.

Clearwater County road officials reported 18 inches of snow in Cardiff, with snowfall rates exceeding one inch per hour. Elk River received around 10 inches of snow, with mountain sites, such as Elk Butte Snotel picking up at least 12 inches.
Dixie received 5.8 inches of snow. Snotel sites along US Highway 2 reported 8 to 13 inches.

South wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph led to areas of blowing snow in Grangeville and vicinity. Two hours of heavy snow was observed in Grangeville, with 4 inches of snow being reported. Other sites picked up 1 to 3 inches of accumulation, including Orofino.

MDT declared severe driving conditions across US and State Highways 2, 37, 56, and 93 as rain and freezing rain led to extremely slick road conditions. Water ponded onto roadways between Troy and Libby as temperatures reached into the mid-30s.
MDT declared severe driving on US Highway 2 between Columbia Falls and Marias Pass as freezing rain led to extremely slick conditions.
Freezing rain impacted the Flathead Valley, particularly in Whitefish, where roadways became extremely slick.

A CWOP station a few miles northwest of Grangeville measured a peak wind gust of 71 mph. The Grangeville Idaho County Airport recorded a wind gust of 61 mph. No significant power outages were observed.

The Lolo Pass sensor recorded 0.80 inches of snow water equivalent which could equate to 8 to 10 inches of snow with temps in the upper 20s.  Dixie only received 1.1 inches and Mountain Meadows SNOTEL received 2 inches of snow depth increase.

The ITD snow depth sensor at Powell on US-12 reported very heavy snow, 4.4 inches in 3 hours, during the morning hours associated with the passage of the cold front. Other snow amounts include around 7 inches Lolo Pass and Mountain Meadows. The Elk City sensor reported heavy snow throughout the day.

An observer in Grangeville reported close to a foot of heavy snow that fell in 10 hours.  A spotter located 5 miles southwest of Grangeville received 14 inches. Another spotter located 7.3 miles southeast of Kooskia received 12.5 inches. Spotters mentioned that the driving conditions were scary with vehicles getting stuck during the storm. Power outages were reported south of Grangeville.

Strong downslope winds gusted between 50 and 65 mph and caused blowing and drifting snow that reduced visibility west and southwest of Grangeville. The 65 mph gust was reported via Facebook from Tolo Lake.

events.cz_name: LOWER HELLS CANYON / SALMON RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Whitebird Hill on US-95 received heavy snow with ITD mentioning that snow chains were recommended. A spotter located on a bench at 4150 feet, 9 miles southwest of Whitebird Hill received around 7 inches of snow. Power outages were reported south of Grangeville.
The Gibbonsville COOP reported 5.2 inches of snow while Leadore only received 0.4 inches. The Saddle Mountain SNOTEL above Lost Trail Ski Resort reported 9 inches of snow.

MDT declared severe driving conditions on US Highway 2 as freezing rain lead to extremely slick conditions. Two tenths of an inch of freezing rain was reported in Essex. A downed tree caused 378 customers to lose power.

Widespread freezing rain impacted the Interstate 90 and Highway 200 corridors, where up to a quarter inch of ice accretion was reported. MDT declared severe driving for Interstate 90 between Frenchtown and Lookout Pass.
The Missoula International Airport briefly closed due to freezing rain during the morning hours of December 25th. A light glaze of ice was reported on area roadways.
A glaze of ice on roadways from freezing rain caused MDT to declare severe driving conditions on US 12.
Widespread freezing rain led to dangerous driving conditions and several slide offs on area roadways.

Widespread freezing rain led to extremely difficult travel along Interstate 90 and US Highway 12 from Bearmouth to Garrison Junction to MacDonald Pass. Numerous slide offs occurred. A glaze of ice also was reported along Highway 200.

Severe driving conditions on Highway 93 from mile marker 56 to 75 and on Highway 35 from mile marker 0 to 18. KGPI closed from 14:12 to 23:50 MST on 12-25, due to freezing rain. Many reports of dangerous driving conditions and ice accumulations up to one quarter inch.
Areas of snow and blowing snow impacted travel on US 93 between Eureka and Fortine. 4 to 6 inches of snowfall was widespread across valley areas.
Ice jam related flooding damaged 3 homes and properties and flooded driveways of 10-12 additional homes. Hay fields were covered with 3 feet of ice with damage to stored hay.
Morning lows of -15F to -25F were common in Southwest Montana. More extreme cold of -36F was felt at Butte with -39F at Georgetown Lake.
Morning lows of -15F to -25F were common in Southwest Montana. More extreme cold of -38F occurred at Potomac.
Morning lows of -15F to -25F were common in eastern Lemhi County. An extreme cold value of -33F occurred at Leadore.
Isolated extreme cold occurred with a low of -31F in Dixie and a low of  -33F at Elk City.
The greatest impact was icy conditions in the Mission Valley on the morning of the 28th. General snowfall of 1 to 3 inches occurred.
Periods of severe driving conditions led to multiple accidents on I-90, especially during the early morning hours of the 28th. General snowfall ranged from 1 to 5 inches.

Severe driving conditions and dangerously icy conditions led to multiple accidents. General snowfall of 3 to 6 inches occurred with blowing snow and reduced visibility, especially in the Bitterroot Valley the morning of the 28th.
Icy conditions resulted in a two car accident on Highway 93.

Prolonged periods of severe driving conditions occurred on US 12 due to ice and snow from Lolo to Lolo Pass. Chains were required on Lolo Pass multiple times as well. There were multiple accidents related to road conditions.

At least 5 hours of severe driving conditions occurred on I-90 with multiple accidents. Loss of power at Montana Snowbowl. Six inches of snow was reported at Seeley Lake with 24 inches at the Stuart Mountain SNOTEL.

Black ice and reduced visibility in blowing snow were problematic on I-90 and I-15, along with secondary roads. Snow amounts of 5 to 10 inches were common with gusts of 30-40 mph. Significant drifting with plows unable to keep up occurred on I-15 south of Butte.

A fatal crash occurred on US-93 at mile marker 87. The call for the crash was dispatched at 19:47 MST. This crash on the S-curves, south of Missoula, occurred as snow showers were impacting the area. Roads had become snow-covered. Observations from near the area show temperatures dropping from just above freezing to just below around the time of the crash.
Montana Department of Transportation road map showed a stretch of US-2 from West Glacier to Marias Pass with black ice from freezing rain that had fallen.
A report was received from Big Fork of 0.2 of ice accumulation as of 05:19 MST on January 14th. Also, there was a freezing rain report from Columbia Falls at 07:00 MST on 1-14.

Montana Department of Transportation road conditions the morning of January 14th showed black ice and scattered ice on many area roads and highways, including I-90 both east and west of Missoula. Also ice was reported on highways 12, 93, and 200. At 07:58 MST, crashes with injuries reported on I-90 east (mile marker 89) and US-93 (mile marker 70). There were reports from the public throughout the morning indicated slick conditions on both highways and side streets.
At 06:09 MST, severe driving conditions were reported on highway 12 from Lolo Pass to Missoula.
Snow totals included 5 at Blankenship Bridge, 10-12 in the Swan Mountains, 9 in the mountains NW of Essex, 4 at Stahl Peak, and 6 at Big Mountain.
Snow totals ranged from 5-6 between Whitefish and Kalispell, 6-10 from Swan Range to Ferndale, 4-5 in the Mission Valley. Big Fork had reported totals ranging from 6 to 9.4.
Multiple crashes were reported on I-90 east, including a commercial vehicle crash at 06:45 MST (mile marker 135) and a multi-car crash at 05:22 MST (mile marker 137).

Reports indicated widespread black ice formation. Multiple crashes were reported, including a non-injury slide off on MT-141 (mile marker 27) at 08:17 MST and a crash with unknown injury on I-90 west (mile marker 165). At 09:44 MST severe driving conditions were declared on MT-141 between MM19 and MM33 and S-271 MM17 to MM22.

A snow total of 7.4 was reported in Condon as of 9:00 MST on February 1st. Snow led to widespread impacts on area roads, especially I-90. There was a multiple vehicle crash with multiple injuries on I-90 near Drummond during the afternoon of January 31st. A news report stated six people were transported to hospitals with serious injuries. The accident resulted in closure of I-90 west of Drummond for several hours. There were also multiple reports from the public of slick road conditions on stretches of I-90.

The Idaho Department of Transportation closed Idaho 29 between Leadore and Bannock Pass due to the combination of heavy snow and blowing and drifting snow. A period of intense snowfall, with wind gusts of 30 to 35 mph associated with snow squalls, was observed, particularly on Idaho State Highway 28 south of Salmon to Gilmore Summit.

A snow squall was observed in Anaconda and along the Interstate 90 corridor west of Butte. Anaconda's Bowman Airfield reported visibility below one quarter of a mile along with wind gusts to 44 mph during the squall. As the snow squall passed through Butte, a wind gust of 53 mph was recorded.
Snow totals include: 6 to 8 inches at Williams Creek Summit and 15 inches in Cobalt.
Snow totals include: 8 to 12 inches above 5,000 feet, with 2 inches in Salmon.

A snow squall produced snowfall rates of 2 to 3 inches per hour and wind gusts of 30 to 35 mph. One inch of snow was measured in a 20 min period at several sites across the Missoula valley. A fatal crash occurred on Interstate 90 at mile marker 97 during the snow squall. The call for the crash was dispatched at 20:12 MST.
Intense bursts of snow and wind associated with a snow squall impacted travel on US Highway 2 west of Kalispell to Happys Inn. Area webcams in the area showed extremely poor visibility.

Intense bursts of snow and wind associated with a snow squall impacted travel across southern portions of the Flathead Valley, including Kalispell. Snow covered roadways led to slick travel conditions following the squall, with two accidents occurring in Big Fork.
There were multiple nights of low temperatures between -5F and -15F, with wind chills between -15F and -30F.
Wind chills across the Mission and Flathead Valleys were between -10F and -20F for multiple overnight periods.
Wind chills across the Lower Clark Fork Region were consistently between -10F and -25F for multiple overnight periods.
The Missoula and Bitterroot Valleys experienced multiple nights of wind chills between -10F and -20F.

Wind chill readings of -10F to -20F for multiple nights prompted a wind chill advisory. While there was not evidence of widespread wind chill warning criteria being met, Deer Mountain did record wind chills as low as -35F. Due to the bitter cold and wind chills, Montana Snowbowl ski area closed on 2/22 and 2/23.
There were multiple nights with wind chills between -15F and -25F for the Potomac and Seeley Lake region.
Wind chills dropped down between -10F and -20F for the Butte/Blackfoot region on the morning of 2/22.

As the coldest temperatures of this Arctic air outbreak were experienced on the morning of 2/23, wind chills across southwest Montana were between -30F and -40F. MacDonald Pass saw the coldest reading of -44F.
The lowest wind chill values observed ranged between -20F and -30F.

Reports of heavy snow started to come in before daybreak along US-93 between Eureka and Whitefish. Near Stryker there was an estimated 4 inches of snow on the road that fell in only 3 hours and by 0727, the wind picked up and caused near whiteout conditions. By the afternoon a traveler reported there were drifts on Highway 37, and it took them an hour to go from the Koocanusa Bridge to Eureka.

A weak arctic push brought heavy snow to Marias Pass between 6 and 9 am on the 20th, then ramped up again by the evening including Essex. Points north and west received a mixture of rain and snow before the arctic push westward overnight. Severe driving conditions were reported for US-2 between West Glacier and Columbia Falls and also at Marias Pass. Total snows included 17 inches at Marias Pass, 11.2 inches at Essex and 6 inches at West Glacier.

High winds at least to 54 mph at the Glacier Park International airport were reported and could have been higher closer to Columbia Falls. A utility company experienced power outages with at least 4 of them caused by trees falling into electrical equipment. The wind damage locations included between Whitefish Lake and Columbia Falls, east side of Flathead Lake, east of Creston, and the area south of Beaver Lake. Heavy snow with 2 inch per hour rates was reported from Bigfork to Yellow Bay for at least 3 hours. Hodgson Road was closed the following night due to severe drifting and severe driving conditions were hoisted by MDT  on Highway 206 and 406. Severe drifting was reported on Mud Lake Road due to strong northeast winds coming down off the Swan Range.
Heavy snow showers with the Pacific cold front impacted Lookout Pass where chains were required for a period. Heavy snow showers also impacted Evaro Hill and brought low visibility.

There were multiple reports of flash freeze in Missoula as the cold arctic air moved in and froze the wet roads. Cars were sliding off the roads and the Missoula Police issued a Emergency Travel Only alert due to whiteout conditions. A report from the public south of Hamilton reported 6 inches of heavy snow.

Heavy snow occurred at Lolo Pass with the Pacific cold front in the early morning hours and then heavy showers during the day. Overall it recorded a snow depth increase of 9 inches. The arctic cold front was mostly a dry front, but temperatures dropped to the single digits by late evening.

The Lindbergh Lake observer reported 10.6 inches of snow, and 8.3 inches fell in Seeley Lake during this event. The arctic cold front brought plummeting temperatures, with gusty east winds to 35 mph, and caused a flash freeze and slick roads.

Snow bands behind the Pacific cold front brought periods of heavy snow and slick conditions in the morning with multiple vehicle wrecks as a result. A weather spotter reported whiteout conditions in Drummond around 1330 as the arctic cold front pushed westward with plummeting temperatures and strong gusty east winds.

Across the West Glacier Region, the wind chills ranged from -30 to -45F between West Glacier and Marias Pass,  in the -15 to -20F range between Columbia Falls and West Glacier and -50 to -60F in the mountains.

Heavy rain from thunderstorm caused a 36 inch culvert to plug on Big Canyon Creek at Milepost 4.9 on road #309. This blockage diverted water into the ditchline on Road #309 downgrade to MP 3.9. The existing cross drains were unable to handle the excess flow. Water draining off the road caused three large debris slides to occur. Much of Mill Creek flooded road #309.

There were two periods of impact for this storm system. During the morning and early afternoon, 06:00 MDT-15:00 MDT, snowfall rates were between 0.25 per hour and 0.50 per hour. Chains were required at Lookout Pass around 08:00 MDT. Another round of snow occurred between 16:30 MDT-18:30 MDT. Snow rates climbed to near 1 inch per hour during the evening hours. The evening snow led to chains being required at Lookout Pass around 17:45 MDT. There were also two separate vehicle accidents that led to lanes of west-bound Interstate 90 being blocked.

Snow bands brought brief heavy snow late on the afternoon of the 12th around Butte. Widespread moderate snow led to chains being required at MacDonald Pass and Homestake Pass late evening on the 12th into early on the 13th. General snow amounts of 2 to 6 inches were observed.

Slick conditions caused by moderate snow and gusty winds resulted in multiple semis spinning out on Homestake Pass on the evening of the 18th. This blockage led to I-90 being closed about 4 hours into the early morning hours on the 19th. General snow amounts of 2 to 4 inches were observed.

Minor flooding occurred along Landing Road, near Elk River. Flowing water came out of the banks of Elk Creek and covered some roadways. The main impact areas were rural and recreational, including near an RV park. Water damaged parts of the road, as confirmed by social media pictures.

The Clark Fork River above Missoula reached minor flood stage of 7.5 feet by 1100MST on May 3rd. The river remained above minor flood stage through 1900MST on May 11th. The river crested at 9.5 feet around 0400MST on May 7th. This did cause sandbagging efforts in the frequently flooded area of Tower and Kehrwald streets in the Orchard Homes neighborhood of Missoula.

A thunderstorm moved through the Mission Valley, near St. Ignatius and produced a tornado as confirmed by multiple public reports and social media pictures. It briefly touched down and caused some minor property damage. Metal roofing was torn off a farm outbuilding, and minor shingle damage occurred at a house.

A few thunderstorm cells formed in northwest Montana, producing gusty outflow winds. There were multiple reports of trees down northwest of Troy along US Highway 2, near mile marker 5, including a large tree that blocked the highway. Around 2300MST, a car ran into a tree blocking part of Highway 2.

A thunderstorm containing very heavy rain moved directly over the Thorne Creek burn scar. Radar estimated 30 minute rainfall totals between 0.55 to 0.90 inches. A report was received from the forest service that a debris flow went over the Thompson River Road.
A strong thunderstorm formed and moved toward Grangeville. Radar estimated maximum size hail was a little over an inch. The public reported nickel size hail with the storm.

A thunderstorm went through Syringa and the Apgar Campground, northeast of Lowell. A weather spotter reported trees down along US Highway-12 from Apgar Campground to just downstream of Swan Creek. The spotter also mentioned roof damage in Syringa and a power outage from Syringa to the Selway River.
Radar signatures suggested the presence of severe hail. A report was received from a trained weather spotter of quarter size hail 5 miles west northwest of Helmville.

A thunderstorm near Ovando showed a bowing structure, indicative of strong outflow winds. Velocity on the lowest radar tilt showed winds near 50 knots. Mid-altitude radial convergence was also present, adding confidence to severe wind gust potential. A report was received that the sign to the Ovando Store was blown over.
The Idaho Transportation Department reported that a major landslide occurred which covered US-93 in both directions near Warm Springs Road at milepost 282 near Elk Bend.
The Salmon-Challis National Forest reported that a landslide had fully blocked the Salmon River Road, one mile southwest of Pine Creek.

The Beartrack Mine reported significant runoff on several of the nearby drainages, and the flood waters including soot from the 2022 Moose Creek wildfire overflowed several structures with no significant damage.
A dispatcher reported flooding with mud and rocks across the north bound lane of US-93 near Twelve Mile County Road. The location was near milepost 292.9 north of Elk Bend.

The Bert Mooney Airport recorded 1.65 inches of rain in an hour. The 911 dispatch reported manholes being blown from deep water rushing down the streets, a motorhome was pushed into a ditch, and there were multiple reports of water in people's homes.
Fields were flooded east of Victor near the Home Acres Road area. The radar estimated rainfall showed 2.60 inches fell in only 1.5 hours.
A layer of mud was found caked over the Drummond Frontage Road the day after the rainfall which depicted that a debris flow had occurred.
There were two reports of quarter sized hail, one on the west side of Anaconda and another 2 miles north of Warm Springs as the storm moved northeastward.

A fast moving grass fire was reported in a neighborhood just southwest of the town of Lolo. At the time of the fire, a nearby RAWS station reported southwest winds around 10 mph gusting between 25-30 MPH. Relative humidity ranged from 10 to 15 percent. Loss estimates include one mobile home lost and one damaged, 16 outbuildings/sheds lost, and 11 vehicles/RV���s were lost or damaged. Three civilians were treated for smoke inhalation and one firefighter suffered a knee injury.

A lightning caused fire consumed hay stored for winter cattle feeding at the Double K Ranch. More than 400 bales each weighting 1000 pounds were lost, which is a year's worth of feed for this ranch. Fencing was also lost in the fire.
The Flathead County dispatch reported 7 inches of new snowfall in Marion, MT. Tree damage and power outages were also reported.

Various heavy snow reports were taken across the West Glacier Region from trained spotters, the general public, the Montana Department of Transportation and automated observing stations. Snowfall amounts ranged from 4.5 inches in Hungry Horse to 10 inches at Essex and Swan Lake at the lower elevations. In the mountains, snowfall ranged from 12 inches at Moss Peak, 24 inches above the Loop to 40 inches at Badger Pass. The heavy snow brought down trees on the Sun Road and other routes in Glacier National Park.

A spotter reported numerous small trees down due to heavy snow falling on them along highway 83, 5 miles south of Swan Lake. Storm total snow accumulations ranged from 4 inches in Condon to 14 inches at Stuart Mountain.

Trained spotters and law enforcement reported snow accumulations ranging from 5 inches in Round Butte to 9 inches on Jette Hill. Law enforcement also reported a power outage in Polson due to a tree down over a power line. Tree branches were reported snapped around Flathead Lake, Big Fork, Ferndale and in Kalispell.
Lookout Pass Ski Resort reported 6 inches and Evaro Hill 4 inches of  new snowfall. Evaro Hill also experienced tree damage from the heavy snow.
Lolo Pass Visitor Center reported 6 inches of new snowfall.
Heavy snow was reported at the Smith Creek automated observing station totaling 8 inches. Heavy snow damaged trees and knocked down numerous tree branches in the Greenough Park area near Missoula.

Heavy snow was reported from various sources including automated observing stations and trained spotters. Storm total snow accumulations ranged from 4 inches in Philipsburg to 22 inches in Warm Springs.
Automated observation stations in this area reported storm total snowfall accumulations ranging from 4 inches at Elk Butte to 14 inches at Crater Meadows.
Automated observation stations in this areas reported heavy snowfall accumulations of 10 inches at Mountain Meadows and 12 inches at Savage Pass.

There were reports received that multiple large debris slides occurred between Pine Creek and Panther Creek along the Salmon River Road, leading to rescue operations to free stranded motorists. There were also reports of large boulders on the road between Indianola and Spring Creek Campground.
High temperatures reached 105-110 degrees each afternoon for several days. Overnight lows in the low to middle 60s provided minimal relief from the daytime heat.

events.cz_name: LOWER HELLS CANYON / SALMON RIVER REGION
