Nine to twelve inches of snow accumulations were reported between Haugan and Heron.
Six to eight inches of new snow was reported in the Seeley Lake area.
Twelve to fourteen inches of snow were reported by spotters in the area.
Thirteen to fiftenn inches of new snow accumulations was reported by COOP observers within the area.  This included Dixie, ID which measured 15 inches during the period.

Heavy snow and blowing snow caused local whiteout conditions on area roads.  Quite a few accidents were reported on US Highway 12, as well as US Highway 95 between Whitebird and Cottonwood. Spotters and COOP observer reported new snow amounts between 7 and 12 inches.

Six inches of snow was reported over Lolo Pass with 16 inches of new snow over Lost Trail Pass.

Spotters reported 6 to 8 inches of new snow.  In addition, strong westerly winds gusted up to 50 mph.  Strong winds caused areas of blowing and drifting snow with local whiteout conditions reported by|Montana DOT on area roads including Interstate 90 and MT Highway 1.
Spotters reported 6 to 13 inches of new snow.
Spotters reported 7 to 8 inches of new snow with the Idaho DOT reporting severe driving conditions along Highway 12 between mile post 169 to the Montana state line.

Snow amounts of 8 to 16 inches were reported by spotters across the region.  Additionally, winds in the forecast zone were sustained anywhere from 13 to 20 mph with gusts up 30 mph.  This created blowing and drifting snow over area roads, causing severe driving conditions on area roads.

Spotters in the region reported 9 to 12 inches of new snow with weather stations measuring sustained winds up to 20 mph. Blowing and drifting snow caused reduced visibility on area roads, leading the Montana DOT to report severe driving conditions on roads across the area.

The Firehall at Glacier Park International measured a total of 25 inches of new snow by the end of this event.  Other spotters in the region reported anywhere from 12 to 18 inches.  In addition, strong winds sustained at 15 to 20 mph with gusts to 30 mph caused reduced visibility in blowing and drifting snow. The Montana DOT reported severe driving conditions on area roads, with the Flathead County Sheriff declaring emergency travel only through the Kalispell area.  A couple power lines were brought down from the heavy snow, causing power outages in the Whitefish area.  The Kalispell airport was shut down for several hours the morning of January 2nd due to snow on the runway.

Spotters in the region reported snow amounts anywhere from 7 to 14 inches.  Winds gusted up to 30 mph creating blowing and drifting snow.  The Montana DOT reported severe driving conditions on area roads, including Interstate 90.

Spotters over Lolo pass reported 15 inches of new snow.  Another spotter in the region reported 12 inches of snow in a 24 hour period.  Lolo Pass was closed due to the heavy snow, winds reducing visibility, and the threat of avalanches along Highway 12 crossing into Idaho.
The Missoula ASOS reported freezing rain, with the Montana DOT reporting freezing rain along Interstate 90 from Missoula to Frenchtown.
Snotel sites in the region reported 10 to 12 inches of new snow.

The Idaho DOT closed Highway 12 between Lolo Pass and 14 miles west of Lolo Pass due to severe avalanche danger from heavy snow. Spotters in the region reported snow amounts between 13 to 16 inches. Additionally, the combination of heavy snow and wind gusts up to 30 mph caused downed trees along Highway 12 between Syringa and Lowell.
The COOP observer in Pierce, as well as storm spotters in the area reported snow amounts between 6 to 7 inches in the valley locations.
Local storm spotters reported 12 inches of new snow in Lowell, with up to 16 inches falling in Elk City.  Schools in Elk City were closed for the day to the heavy snow.

Schools along the Camas Prairie were forced to close due to heavy snow.  This included schools in Grangeville, Cottonwood, Kamiah, and Orofino.  Storm spotters in the area reported snow amounts between 7 and 8 inches.
The COOP observer in Swan Lake reported 6 inches of new snow.  Members of the public in Essex reported 6 inches of snow as well.
Storm spotters located between Seeley Lake and Potomac reported new snowfall totals of 6 to 10 inches.
Storm spotters in the region reported around 9 inches of new snow, with Blacktail Ski Area reporting 14 inches of new snow by the end of the event.
Spotters in the area reported new snowfall amounts of 8 to 9 inches between West Glacier and Essex.
Highway 12 going over Lolo Pass was closed due to the heavy snow and avalanche danger along the road.

The Montana DOT reported severe driving conditions along Highway 200 between Greenough and Lincoln, as well as Highway 141 near Avon, and Highway 12 going over MacDonald Pass. The severe conditions were due to heavy snow and blowing snow reducing visibility.
Trained storm spotters in the area reported new snowfall amounts between 8 and 10 inches.  Trees were reported down in the Seeley Lake area.
The Idaho DOT closed Highway 12 going over Lolo Pass due to the heavy snow causing avalanche danger.  Additionally, storm spotters in Dixie reported new snow accumulations up to 9 inches.
An Idaho DOT camera indicated very poor visibility in extremely heavy snow.

Trained spotters, as well as Idaho DOT cameras, indicated very intense snowfall, reducing visibility considerably.  Although storm total snow amounts only ranged between 3 and 4 inches, this amount fell in less than a 6 hour time frame.
Northeast winds between 30 and 40 mph ushered a secondary push of arctic air into the area.  Wind chill temperatures ranged between 19 and 26 below zero.

Weather observations from the Grangeville airport reported wind gusts as high as 53 mph.  Idaho County Sheriff Dispatch reported zero visibility along Highway 13 due to the blowing and drifting of snow.

events.cz_name: LOWER HELLS CANYON / SALMON RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Slate Creek RAWS observation reported wind gusts up to 44 mph.  Reports were received from Idaho County Sheriff Dispatch of visibility down to zero on area roads.
Storm spotters between Seeley Lake and Swan Lake reported 8 to 12 inches of new snow.

Weather observations between Hamilton and Stevensville recorded wind gusts up to 61 mph.  Storm spotters in the area reported wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph with damage to trees and roofs. A semi-truck was blown over on Highway 93.

Ice accumulations of 0.20 to 0.25 inches built up on surfaces, including roads, in the Flathead valley.  The main location impacted was Kalispell. Numerous area schools were closed due to poor road conditions.

Areas of freezing fog reduced visibility to one quarter mile or less across portions of the Flathead and Mission valley.  Highway 93 near Polson was shut down on the afternoon of the 3rd due to numerous accidents related to the low visibility.
Department of Transportation reported 8 inches of new snow accumulations over Lookout Pass.

Trained spotter at Lookout Pass Visitor Center reported ten inches of snow at 5pm on the 24th.  On the morning of the 25th, they had recieved another fourteen inches of snow.  This made a storm total snow of twenty four inches.

The trained spotter at the Lolo Pass Visitor Center reported ten inches of snow accumulations by 4 pm PST.  An additional fourteen inches was reported by the morning of the 25th, making a storm total snow amount of twenty four inches.
Trained spotters reported seven to eight inches of new snow accumulations in the valley locations.

Department of Transportation issued a report of severe driving conditions for heavy snow and blowing snow, significantly reducing visibility on Highway 2 over Marias Pass. Total snow accumulations were estimated at seven to eight inches, although blowing and drifting made these measurements difficult.

Spotters in the area reported widespread wind gusts to 35 mph with heavy snow and blowing and drifting.  Total snow accumulations ranged between four and eight inches, although the blowing and drifting made snow measurments difficult.
Spotters reported sixteen inches of new snow over Lookout Pass, and seven inches of new snow over Evaro Hill.

The Department of Transportation declared severe driving conditions with near zero visibility in blowing and drifting snow along Highway 12 over Macdonald Pass, as well as Interstate 90 over Homestake Pass.  Snow accumulations ranged between four and eight inches, although the blowing and drifting nature of the snow made for difficult snow measurments.
Storm spotters near Tuscor and Heron each reported 6 of new snow accumulations.

Spotters located in Columbia Falls and West Glacier reported generally one to three inches of snow in combination with strong winds reducing visibility to less than one quarter mile.  Higher elevations received anywhere from six to twelve inches of new snow.

Three to five inches of new snow fell in the lower elevations, with nine to sixteen inches over the higher terrain.  Winds gusting up to 30 mph created blowing and drifting snow with low visibility at times.  Interstate 90 over Lookout Pass was closed due to severe driving conditions.
Lolo Pass reported new snow accumulations of twelve to sixteen inches, while Lost Trail Pass ski area reported fourteen inches of new snow.
The CO-OP in Pierce reported eight inches of snow.  A spotter seven miles north of Pierce reported nine inches of snow.
The storm spotter at Lolo Pass reported twelve to sixteen inches of new snow.  The Dixie CO-OP reported eight inches of new snow.

The combination or snow, blowing snow, lowered visibility, and extreme wind chills lead to the declarations of severe driving conditions along US Highway 2.  Wind chills dropped down to thirty one below for fourteen hours.

The combination or snow, blowing snow, lowered visibility, and extreme wind chills lead to the declarations of severe driving conditions from Kalispell to Columbia Falls to Coram.  Wind chills dropped down to twenty three below for several hours.

The Department of Transportation declared severe driving conditions on Highway 2 over Marias Pass due to blowing and drifting snow limiting visibility.  Estimated snowfall totals ranged between three to seven inches, although such measurements were difficult due to strong winds gusting to near forty mph at times.

Trained spotters in Sula and over Lolo Pass reported nine inches of new snow fall in a twelve hour period. In addition, periodic wind gusts between thirty five and forty five mph caused reduced visibility in blowing and drifting snow.
Storm spotters in Anaconda and around Georgetown Lake reported eight to twelve inches of new snow accumulations over at twelve hour period.
Trained storm spotters in Dixie reported eleven inches of new snow.  Storm spotters in Elk City reported anywhere from fourteen to eighteen inches of new snow.

Trained spotters in Leadore reported six inches of new snow.  In addition, strong winds led to blowing and drifting snow and caused reduced visibility to near zero at times.  Highway 28 near Gilmore Summit and Route 29 to Bannack Pass were closed for some time due to these poor driving conditions.

Trained spotters in Essex reported a storm total snowfall of twelve inches. A spotter in West Glacier measured a total snowfall of eight inches.  On Marias Pass over Highway 2, snow fall amounts ranged between ten to twelve inches.
Trained spotters at Lookout Pass along Interstate 90 reported fourteen inches of new snow.
Trained spotters in Lindbergh Lake reported eleven inches of snow, while spotters in Condon reported seven inches.
A trained spotter in Elk City measured twenty four inches of new snow from the event.  A trained spotter in Dixie measured eight inches of new snow.
Thirteen inches of new snow was reported over Lost Trail Pass on Highway 93.  A storm spotter fourteen miles north of Sula reported twelve inches of new snow accumulations.
A trained spotter in Deerlodge reported nine inches of new snow accumulations.  Philipsburg reported a foot of new snow accumulations.
A trained spotter in Weippe reported seven inches of new snow accumulations.  Pierce reported a storm total snow of five inches.  Higher terrain in the area received up to nine inches of new snow.
A storm spotter in Dixie reported nine inches of new snow fall in twenty four hours.  A spotter seven miles southeast of Grangeville also reported nine inches of new snow.

The Idaho Department of Transportation closed Highway 28 south of Leadore due to snow and blowing snow severely reducing visibility.  Total snow fall amounts ranged from two to four inches in the lower elevations and eight to ten inches over the higher terrain.

The DES in Clearwater County reported seven car accidents due to slick roads in accumulating snow.  The trained spotters in the zone reported about eight inches of new snow accumulations with a report up to fourteen inches twelve miles east of Kooskia.  The power company around this area reported eighty trees down across local roads.  Power and telephone lines were down for a period of time.

A trained spotter near Eureka reported a camper trailer was blown over due to the winds, which were estimated to reach up to 60 mph.  The Forest Service reported forest blowdowns over hundreds of acres on the Kootenai National Forest and neighboring private lands in the Glen Lake and Indian Creek areas.
A trained spotter in the Columbia Falls area measured winds up to seventy five mph. Numerous trees were reported down across the area, causing fairly widespread power outages.

The Department of Transportation declared severe driving conditions on Highway 2 over Marias Pass due to snow and blowing and drifting snow reducing visibility significantly.  Total snow amounts ranged from two to four inches over the valley locations, with up to two feet of snow over the higher terrain.

The Department of Transportation declared severe driving conditions on Interstate 90 from 15 miles west of Butte, to Butte due to reduced visbility in blowing and drifting snow.  Total snow amounts ranged between six to nine inches over the lower elevations.

The few observing stations in the area recorded wind gusts up to 50 mph.  However, the winds were likely much stronger than this as numerous tree blow downs were reported in Yellowpine and at the Whitewater Ranch, including several trees down on nearby roads.
Kriley Creek RAWS reported south winds sustained at 33 mph gusting to 78 mph.  The Salmon RAWS reported south east winds sustained at 19 mph gusting to 59 mph.
Hot Springs RAWS reported 1.36 inches of rainfall in one hour at 3:29 PM MDT. Hot Springs Fire Department reported localized flooding of streets in Hot Springs.
Public reported nickel size hail and heavy rain from thunderstorm over the Irvine Flats area.
Basement flooding was reported by the DES Coordinator in two homes along Fifer Creek on Hemlock Street in Anaconda.

A severe weather spotter reported hearing on a scanner that trees were  blown down onto Highway 12 west of Orofino from gusty winds. A newspaper article confirmed that trees and power lines were blown down onto the highway near the Riverside Motel and Stoddard Electric. Traffic was backed up from the Orofino bridge to the the intersection of 118 Street and Highway 12.
A funnel cloud formed from a thunderstorm south of Gilmore Summit and moved towards Mud Creek before dissipating.

The Nez Perce National Forest closed Road 2009, known locally as Cayuse Connection Raod, due to damage sustained from heavy rain. The Southfork RAWS station recorded 2.4 inches of rain between 10 PM and 2 AM June 5 to June 6 MDT.
Trees were blown down from a severe thunderstorm blocking Highway 12 near milepost 86.
Heavy rain produced rock and debris slides onto Highway 12 near Lowell. An estimated 600 pound rock rolled onto Highway 12 west of Lowell.

Law enforcement reported three to four inches of water on portions of Highway 28 in areas between Lemhi and Leadore, with up to 12 inches of water flowing over Highway 28 near Lemhi.  Precipitation amounts ranged between one to two inches in the area.  Basement flooding and flooding of Macfarland Campground were reported.
Golf ball sized hail accumulated to a 1.5 inch depth on the ground.
Hail up to one inch in diameter reported by a storm spotter.
Report of dime sized hail in Philipsburg.
Weather spotter reported quarter size hail in Philipsburg. Eight miles northwest of Philipsburg, a camper reported half inch diameter hail at 5500 feet.
Weather spotter reported quarter sized hail.

A NWS storm survey revealed flood and debris flows near the Black Cat burn area northeast of Frenchtown.  A basement in the area was flooded with two inches of water.  Another residence had water and debris flows running into their backyard and driveway, which briefly cut off access to the home.
Hail three quarter to one inch in diameter accumulated up to two inches deep on the ground. The hail knocked un-cut hay flat and stripped vegetation from shrubs.

A trained spotter two miles north of Creston reported wind gusts up to 60 mph.  In addition small hail was reported with this storm. The Creston Fire Department reported|extensive damage from numerous trees blown down onto power lines. A sailboat was tipped over on Blaine Lake with four people thrown into the water. A large fir tree was blown down onto a home on Bachelor Grade Road. Up to 100 trees were blown over along Bachelor Grade Road.
Glacier National Park officials reported heavy rain that caused rock and debris flows on the Going to the Sun Road. One rock slide sent a rock through a car window.
Hail caused significant damage to two vehicles and broke small tree limbs off nearby trees 2 miles southeast of Eureka.
Hail up to one inch in diameter was reported with this storm.
Heavy rain caused several Forest Service roads to be flooded.

Flooding was reported on both Elm and Silverbow Street.  A few homes on Silverbow had flooding in their basements.  The Butte Plaza Mall parking lot was flooded, and strong winds caused water to flow into the doorways and walkways of the mall.
Quarter sized hail reported.
A trained spotter reported hail increasing in size.  The windows of the home were damaged. The large hail caused tree branches to be stripped.
A trained spotter reported that the hail caused damage to the windows of his home as well as three vehicles.  Tree branches were stripped from the large hail.
A member of the public reported 2.5 inch hail to the Silver Bow County Sheriff.

Extensive hail damage to homes, roofs, and vehicles reported on Green Acres and Continental Drive near Butte.  Hail size ranged between 1.75 and two inches in diameter.  In addition, wind gusts were estimated up to 70 mph, which caused some tree branches to break.
The Public Works Department reported .75 inch hail and estimated one inch of rain in about 30 minutes in Butte.  Water was flowing down the streets.
Seven thenths of an inch of rain fell in 24 minutes at Bert Mooney Airport.
The Elk Park Department of Transportation weather station measured a thunderstorm wind gust up to 69 mph.
Extensive tree damage was caused by strong thunderstorm winds.  The winds were estimated to be between 55 to 60 mph.
Highway 93 was flooded with a debris flow at Kriley Creek.
A spotter reported 1.75 inch hail on the ground near Highway 93 and Tower Creek.
The wind gust was measured by the Kriley Creek RAWS site.
Large hail up to 1.75 inches was reported by the public in Carmen.  In addition, shingles were blown off a roof.
Quarter sized hail north of Carmen accumulated three to four inches deep.
A motorist traveling over Lost Trail Pass observed nickel and quarter sized hail while traveling over the Montana side of the pass.
VFW Post customers reported having to pull over because of size and intensity of hail along the road between Hall to Maxville.
Hail size was estimated between a walnut and ping pong ball.
Hail lasted about five minutes.
A report of one inch hail received from the VFW Post in Maxville.
The Logan Pass observation site reported sustained winds between 40 and 56 mph with gusts between 86 to 96 mph for a period of about five hours.

Law enforcement relayed reports of mudslides along the Forth of July Creek Road near milemarker 321 on Highway 93.  The combination of mudslides, rocks and boulders made Fourth of July Creek Road impassable.

County officials reported downed trees across area roads, power outages, and phone outages due to trees down on power lines.  The main impact was to areas from Kalispell, to Whitefish, to Polson and Bigfork.  Eleven boats were damaged around Flathead Lake with dock damaged at Lakeside and Finley Point.
Bannock Pass SNOTEL reported twelve inches of snow. Williams Creek SNOTEL reported ten inches of snow.
Barker Lakes SNOTEL reported seventeen inches of snow.  Peterson Meadows SNOTEL reported eleven inches of snow.
Stuart Mountain SNOTEL reported ten inches of snow.  North Fork Jocko SNOTEL reported eleven inches of snow.  Storm spotters in the lower elevations reported between three to eight inches.

Residents in the Quail Ridge subdivision, just south of Lake Blaine Road, endured hail as large as golf balls raining down for up to half an hour, along with very strong winds. Awnings on homes were dented, gardens were flattened, windows broken and basements were flooded from heavy rainfall up to 1 inch with in 30 minutes.

Lightning from a thunderstorm that rolled through Anaconda started a roof on fire that was put out by the fire department before extensive damage occurred. The fire burned though the exterior of the roof and down into the insulation, about 20 square feet of the roof.
A home in St. Ignatius was completely burned down and destroyed by a lightning strike.
Nine to twelve inches of new snow was reported over Marias Pass.  The Fielding RAWS reported eight inches of new snow.
Deer Mountain and Tepee Point RAWS recorded wind gusts between 35 to 40 mph in combination with three to eight inches of new snow.
The COOP observer in Dixie reported seven inches of new snow with this system.  In addition, Mountain Meadows SNOTEL recorded eleven inches of new snow.
SNOTELs in the area reported between five to nine inches of snow above 4000 feet.  In addition gusty west winds up to 40 mph were reported.
SNOTELs in the area reported five to nine inches of new snow.  In addition, wind gusts up to 90 mph were reported over Logan Pass.
SNOTELs in the area reported between five to eleven inches of new snow.

A spotter six miles southeast of Grangeville reported eight inches of snow, with the DOT reporting up to six inches of snow on area roads.  Power went out locally to a few customers in Grangeville due to snowload related problems.  In addition, a few car accidents were reported on area roads.
A spotter 10 ENE of Arlee reported wind chills down to 21 below zero.
Wind chills down to 34 below zero were reported in Essex.
Missoula ASOS reported wind chills down to 20 to 22 below zero.
RAWS/SNOTELs reported wind chills as low as 23 below zero.
Observation site in Avon reported wind chills down to 39 below zero.
An observation site in Greenough reported wind chills down to 21 below zero.

A trained spotter in Swan Lake reported 15 inches of snow.  A trained spotter in Essex reported 14 inches of snow.  In addition, high winds were reported by the DOT along Highway 2 from Marias Pass to Essex, making for low visibility.

A trained spotter in Columbia Falls reported 9 inches of snow.  A trained spotter 10 miles southwest of Kalispell reported 8 inches of snow.  In addition, strong winds with the passing cold front caused a ground blizzard at Glacier International Airport for a period of time overnight on the 12th.
A trained spotter 3 miles east of Lolo reported 8 inches of snow.  A trained spotter in Miller Creek reported 8 inches of snow.
THE DOT over Lolo Pass reported 10 inches of new snow.  Eight inches of new snow was reported over Lost Trail Pass.
A trained spotter 6 miles east of Ovando reported 18 inches of snow.  A trained spotter in Avon reported 8 inches of snow.
A CoCoRaHS observer in Greenough reported 8 inches of snow.  An NWS employee reported 12 inches in Clinton.
The Hemlock Butte SNOTEL reported 8 inches of snow.  A spotter in Pierce reported 10 inches of new snow.
A trained spotter in Elk City reported 14 inches of snow.  The Idaho DOT reported 12 to 16 inches of new snow along Highway 12 between Lowell and Powell.
The Idaho DOT reported 14 inches of snow in Kooskia.  A spotter in Weippe reported 12 inches of new snow.

events.cz_name: LOWER HELLS CANYON / SALMON RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: The entire metal covering over the hamburger stand trailer at the White Bird Arena was blown off by strong gusty southwest winds. The wooden supports and metal posts were yanked upwards, with some of the debris carried 75 feet away. The Slate Creek RAWS weather observation to the south of the site, measured a wind gust up to 47 mph.
Lookout Pass ski area measured 12 inches of new snow in 24 hours.  They reported 14 inches in 48 hours.  A SNOTEL over Lookout Pass reported 9 inches of snow.
The Montana DOT reported 8 to 12 inches of snow over Marias Pass.
The Montana DOT reported 8 to 12 inches of new snow over Marias Pass.
Lookout Pass Ski area reported 12 inches of snow in 24 hours.  They also reported 14 inches of snow fell in 48 hours.  A SNOTEL over Lookout Pass reported 9 inches of snow.
Heavy snow was reported by weather observers ranging from 8 to 11 inches in the valleys. Big Mountain Ski Resort received 13 inches of new snow in a 24 hour period.

Heavy snow and strong gusty north winds impacted Flathead County, where schools were closed in Whitefish, Big Fork and Swan Valley. Local whiteout conditions occurred during the evening in the northern Flathead Valley where wind gusts up to 45 mph were recorded at Glacier International Airport on 1/5/2010. Power outages were reported throughout the county from downed power lines. Total snowfall amounts ranged from 6 to 11 inches.

Heavy snow and local gusty north winds caused blowing and drifting of snow and poor visibility on roadways. Total snowfall amounts ranged from 6 inches near Clinton to 10 to 12 inches from 7 miles north of Seeley Lake to Condon in northern Missoula County. A weather station at Clearwater Junction recorded wind speeds of 37 mph with gusts to 44 mph at 819 PM 1/5/2010.

Montana Department of Transportation declared severe driving conditions on I-90 Deer Lodge to Phosphate, I-90 Deer Lodge to Warm Springs, and US 12 Garrison to Avon due to very strong winds and blowing snow. Chains were required on McDonald Pass from blowing and drifting of snow. Wind speeds at Garrison weather station were recorded at 27 mph with gusts to 35 mph at 716 PM. Wind speeds at Helmville MT-200 weather station were recorded at 33 mph gusting to 43 mph at 756 PM.

Freezing rain caused very slick roadways and closed a portion of I-90 from near Ninemile to the Y. Some Bitterroot and Missoula Valley schools were running two hours late due to bus delays. The Missoula International Airport closed down briefly due to freezing rain on runways. Twenty car crashes were reported along I-90 and in the town of Missoula during the morning hours.
Freezing rain caused very slick roadways and closed the Alberton Schools.

Ice jam buildup on the Salmon River caused waters to rise and flood 4 to 8 miles north of Salmon near the Carmen area and flood homes. A camp ground on a gravel bar near the river was under water; the first time in two decades. The Morgan Bar recreation area was also submerged in water. Local county roads were flooded in the area.
Thunderstorms that moved from the Bitterroot Valley northward to the Missoula Valley, blew down two rotten cottonwood trees in Hamilton, and three trees in the city of Missoula.
Snow amounts up to seven inches reported on the Camas Prairie.  The heavy wet snow caused power outages as well as downed trees.  Gusty winds sombined with the snow to produce whiteout conditions.

The Missoula ASOS reported winds up to 52 mph.  The amateur radio club reported two trees down on Highway 93 near Stevensville, shingles blown off a roof in Florence, and utility poles down in Lolo.  Estimated winds in these areas were 40 to 50 mph sustained with gusts greater than 50 mph.
An observation site 6 miles east of Darby reported a wind gust to 59 mph.  An observation site  4 miles west northwest of Darby reported wind gusts to 54 mph.

A utility company construction site measured winds gusting up to 60 mph.  The same utility company reported scattered power outages from trees down on power lines through Silver Bow County and the Butte area.  Also, a tree fell on a vehicle in the Butte jail parking lot.  A Ford F-150 sustained major damage to its windshield.  Severe driving conditions were reported over MacDonald Pass by the Department of Transportation due to poor visibility in blowing and drifting snow.

Law enforcement reported several large trees down in Kalispell.  Multiple power lines were down across Flathead County.  A billboard was broken in half in Columbia Falls.  A tree fell on a house on Sky Road in Whitefish.  Observations in the area measured winds between 40 to 50 mph sustained with estimated gusts up to 58 mph.
Law enforcement reported trees down on Highway 200 near Bonner. Winds were estimated at 40 to 50 mph with gusts up to 58 mph.
A member of the public reported an old barn was blown down near Eureka.  Also, multiple trees were downed along Highway 37 and Highway 2.

A trained spotter in Georgetown reported six inches of snow.  A trained spotter seven miles south of Butte reported seven inches of heavy snow. The Butte DOT reported six to eight inches of snow over Homestake and MacDonald Passes.
A trained spotter in Essex reported eight inches of snow in 18 hours.  The Montana DOT reported 12 inches of snow over Marias Pass in in 18 hours.
A trained spotter in Seeley Lake reported six inches of snow in less than 12 hours.  A spotter near Linbergh Lake reported seven to eight inches of snow.

Various SNOTELs in the area reported anywhere from seven to 42 inches of snow above 4000 feet.  Severe driving conditions were declared over Marias Pass due to snow and visibility issues by the Montana DOT.
A spotter in Swan Lake reported seven inches of new snow.  A spotter in Essex reported six inches of snow in 12 hours, 13 inches of snow total.
A trained spotter in Pierce reported power outages and numerous trees down due to strong winds.  Winds were measured at 50mph at the Dent RAWS station.
The Red River Ranger Station in Elk City reported trees down along Highway 14 west of Elk City.  The South Fork RAWS station measured a wind gust to 51 mph.

The Grangeville HANDAR reported winds sustained at 43 mph with gusts up to 59 mph.  Multiple trees were reported down near Weippe, including a 16 inch diameter Ponderosa Pine.  Significant damage was caused at the Kooskia National Fish Hatchery due to a 60 ft by 100ft storage building having its roof ripped off.
Salmon RAWS measured a wind gust to 58 mph. Kriley Creek RAWS reported a wind gust to 62 mph.
The Marion RAWS reported a wind gust to 63 mph.
Logan Pass Visitor Center reported a wind gust to 99 mph.  Glacier Park Dispatch in West Glacier reported several trees down, closing the bridge near the park entrance.

A trained spotter reported power poles down along North Echo Lake Road, east of Bigfork.  Numerous trees were downed, some up to one foot in diameter.  A tree was blown over on to a house in Bigfork as well.  Power lines were down all across Flathead County.

A power pole was blown over on to a vehicle at Mullan Road and Grassland Drive in Missoula.  A semi truck was overturned between mile markers 78 and 79 on Highway 93 south.  Several power poles were snapped in that area as well.
Deer Mountain RAWS recorded a wind gust to 59 mph.  Point 119 Weather Station reported a wind gust to 90 mph.

A tree was reported down on a house and in the power lines in Butte.  In Anaconda, a tree broke in half at Main and Front Streets.  The fallen tree broke the top of a light pole and also blocked the street.  In addition, a porch blew off a house in Anaconda sending broken glass on to Chestnut Street.
A trained spotter in Seeley Lake measured wind gusts up to 71 mph.  Numerous trees were reported down, some up to one foot in diameter.  Trees were blown down on to the power lines.
Twelve inches of snow was measured by the Highway Department three miles south-southeast of Leadore.  Six inches of snow was measured in Patterson.

Four inches of snow was observed by the Co-Op observer in May.  Four inches of snow was also reported 9 miles southeast of Salmon by a trained spotter.  Power was out from Barker to Tendoy for twelve hours with broken branches and downed trees  reported due to the heavy, wet snow.
A trained spotter in Divide reported seven inches of new snow.  A trained spotter five miles southwest of Butte reported nine inches of new snow.  Five of those inches fell in about three hours.
The Little Salmon River washed over Highway 95 south of Riggins.  Culvert failure let water and debris flow across Highway 13 near Stites.
A sheriff deputy reported one inch hail at mile marker 56 on Highway 200 that lasted about five minutes.  The sheriff deputy had to pull over because of the intensity of the hail and rain.

Heavy rain fall rates of 0.60 inches in an hour fell near Kooskia, Idaho.  This caused a culvert to be washed out along Battle Ridge Road.  Flash flooding also caused the closure of State Highway 13 between Harpster and Kooskia.
Report of one inch hail on Highway 12 near Kooskia, Idaho.
One inch hail estimated by the COOP observer in Georgetown Lake.
A trained spotter reported quarter sized hail coming down hard.  He also received 0.35 inches of rain in five minutes.
The sheriffs office in Deer Lodge received one inch diameter hail.
An employee at Trixi's Bar in Ovando estimated nickel size hail and heavy rain.
Hail 1.25 inches in diameter was reported at Lindbergh Lake.  Small branches were stripped off pine trees and were covering the ground.
The Swan River Lodge reported periods of one inch sized hail.  This was accompanied by pea sized and marble sized hail as well.
NWS employees measured one inch size hail at the weather forecast office.
A NWS employee measured one inch size hail at his residence north of Missoula in the Prospect Creek neighborhood.
A weather spotter reported  one inch diameter hail near Seeley Lake.
A trained spotter reported a cottonwood tree fallen across the road.
Media shared photos of a backyard trampoline blown up against the side of a home.
Power was out in the Florence area as reported by an NWS employee.
Power lines down near Highway 93 and Carlton Creek Road between Lolo and Florence.
A trained spotter reported estimated wind gusts of 60 MPH.  Smaller tree branches were down with the largest branch estimated at four inches in diameter.
Quarter size hail was reported by the public in Cottonwood, lasting 10 to 15 minutes.
Weather spotter reported hail 1.25 inch in diameter near Fenn.
Weather spotter reported hail one inch in diameter near Kooskia.
A fencing company in Avon reported one inch hail.
Strong winds blew the chimney off of the Syringa Lodge as well as some of the tin on the roof.
A 64 mph wind gust was measured by the salmon RAWS station.
A trained spotter estimated wind gusts up to 65 mph with trees blown down on to roads.
The Lake County Emergency Manager reported trees blown down on Highway 35 near Blue Bay along Flathead Lake.
The public reported four trees blown down from thunderstorm winds at Lake Mary Ronan State Park.
A trained spotter reported a 12 inch diameter tree blown down onto the road.
A trained spotter in the West Valley area reported seeing a funnel cloud near Whitefish.
A member of the public between Darby and Hamilton reported three quarter inch hail.
A trained spotter two miles east of Dixon reported hail to the size of quarters with some larger pieces in the mix.
A trained spotter relayed that their neighbor received golf ball sized hail that left dents in their car and caused damage to their corn crop.
A trained spotter reported quarter sized hail in the Lolo Creek area.
A HAM radio operator reported hail up to one inch in diameter at their residence.
A trained spotter estimated penny to nickel sized hail.
An NWS employee reported one inch in diameter hail north of Florence.
The Sula Lookout station reported 50 mph wind gusts with nickle sized hail.  This observation was taken at an elevation of 6191 feet.
A trained spotter reported heavy rain with hail.
A trained spotter reported several pine trees bent down/over with branches estimated at six inches in diameter broken off of trees from reported thunderstorm winds.
Law enforcement reported golf ball sized hail in the Kamiah city limits.
Law enforcement reports golf ball sized hail in the Whitebird city limits.
A trained spotter reported golf ball sized hail with some larger pieces in the mix east of Kamiah.

A square 16 by 16 cinder block was moved completely off a plywood sheet and the plywood was blown away. Gutters were blown down. Some metal lawn furniture was blown off the porch. Several bails of peat moss were blown around.

A flash flood came out of Edwards Gulch and brought debris, including mud and rocks, as well as water, into buildings on the west side of town.  There was also some basement flooding.
A NWS storm survey of Skalkaho Pass 15 hours after the storm had passed, revealed hail stones of 1.33 inches to 1.5 inches in diameter, with hail accumulations up to four inches deep.
Nickel sized hail was accompanied by heavy rain.
A trained spotter reported a one hour rainfall total of 0.91 inches of rain.
A trained spotter reported that 0.78 inches of precipitation fell in 40 to 50 minutes.
The Deer Lodge County emergency manager reported tin roof and shingle damage in Anaconda.  Storm drains were also having difficulty keeping up with the heavy rainfall amounts.
A spotter at the Deer Mountain lookout reported dime to quarter size hail and heavy rain.
Broadcast media forwarded on a picture they received from a viewer of hail measuring 1.25 inches in diameter.
A US Forest Service trail crew reported hail up to 1.75 inches in diameter.
Law enforcement reported a mudslide over Highway 95 near Slate Creek due to heavy rain.
A 37 year old man riding a horse was struck by lightning and killed.
Severe thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree on to a cabin at Three Rivers Resort in Lowell. Very heavy rain was blowing sideways.
An amateur radio operator reported a wind gust to 58 mph.
Large trees fell across roadways and power lines were knocked down in portions of Butte.  A few small grass fires were reported from the downed power lines.
Brief heavy rain was mixed with hail at Fish Creek and the Clark Fork River.  Precipitation measured in at 0.40 inches in less than 30 minutes.
A spotter reported 0.30 inches of rain in 15 minutes.
A trained spotter reported 0.50 inches of rain in less than 30 minutes.

A slow moving thunderstorm dropped rainfall amounts of 1.59 inches up to an estimated 3.25 inches in a one to two hour period. Twenty five homes were flooded from runoff.  One home owner had half their yard washed away with a shed also flooded.
A car traveling over Logan Pass sustained dents from the hail.
The NWS storm survey team ran across a pile of hail 15 hours after the hail event occured which was still 0.75 inches in diameter.  Hail was likely quite a bit larger when it initially fell.
Wind gust reported from Salmon RAWS.
Wind gust reported from Kriley Creek RAWS.

Numerous blow downs throughout Clearwater County. Spotter reported 18 and 20 inch diameter trees broken at the base and mid-section respectively.  Power and phone service was knocked out. A 26 foot airstream trailer was moved off its jack.  Fire starts from lightning were also reported from this storm.
A trained spotter reported a funnel cloud that was close to the ground.

A US Forest Service employee observed a small tornado that briefly touched the ground west of Greencreek. There was substantial damage to the roof of a barn off New Hope Road, south side of Lawyers Canyon, about 3.5 miles from Ferdinand. There was an incredible amount of topsoil movement and severe erosion down onto a private access road, plugging several culverts.  The sediment was backed up 2 to 3 feet high for 10 to 15 feet behind the culvert.
A home near Corvallis was hit by lightning and burned.
Widespread power outages in the Orofino area. Trees Down near the prison, hospital and hidden valley areas. Storage building blown out on Highway 12 west of Orofino.
Damage to tree due to estimated 60 mph wind gust. Also heard on scanner about other damage around the area. Including trees on cars, roads and structures.
Several trees down across highways 11 and 3, blocking traffic. One trailer park was being evacuated due to tree damage on residences.
Non-thunderstorm wind gusts 3 miles east of Florence in Ravalli county.
Sheriff reported numerous trees blown down and power out throughout Idaho county.

Measured 7 inches of snow 4 miles ne of Ronan.

events.event_narrative: The Idaho county free press reported that a foot and a half of new snow fell on the White Bird grade, making highway 95 nearly impassable. There were 15 slidoffs and 2 crashes.

The Idaho Transportation Department reported a large rock slide that completely blocked U.S. Highway 95 at milepost 188 in the Salmon River canyon. Crews were able to open up one lane by the morning of December 3rd. It had been four to five years since there had been any similar problems in that area.
Slick roads were blamed for a fatal car accident that occurred on highway 12 near mile marker 14 approximately 1.5 miles ESE of Avon, MT.

A trained spotter located in Weippe measured 9 inches of snow.

Law enforcement reported heavy snow at MT-2 near Happy's Inn with 4 to 6 inches on the road surface. They estimated 10 to 12 inches fell there in the last 24 hours.

It can be inferred that there was blowing snow at temperatures between 28 and 32 degrees F. The sensor reported 0.77 of precipitation which can be converted by approximation to 8 and 10 inches of snow.

Numerous pine and cedar trees were blown down by the wind in the Orofino area. The largest tree diameter was 28 inches. Many trees fell onto power lines causing highway 12 and other roads to close for up to 4 hours. Thirty percent of roof shingles were blown off.

A 72 foot, 26 inch diameter Douglas Fir fell down from very strong thunderstorm winds and crashed onto owners' house. Soil moisture was relatively dry, but as seen in photo much of the branches on the trunk except at the top had already been cut off before this event.  A forester examined the tree and found that its roots had been cut on the west side of the tree before the event.

Lookout Pass webcams revealed heavy snow that stuck to the roadway and reduced visibilities to less than one quarter mile from at least 1400 to 1900 MDT. A vehicle spun-out at the pass blocking I-90 east-bound that brought traffic to a standstill.
The Lookout Pass snotel at 5140 feet reported 8 inches of snow that fell in 6 hours.

Ten inches of snow fell in Condon while power outages were reported from Swan Lake to Seeley Lake.  Up to 4 inches of slush made highway 200 slick from Clearwater to just before Potomac while visibilities were reduced to one quarter of a mile due to falling snow.

A weather spotter in Evaro reported 8.2 inches of total snowfall.  Road conditions on US 93 were slick with several inches on the roads from Arlee to Evaro Hill by 6 PM MDT.

An estimated 10 inches of snow fell in Arlee as reported by the public. A NWS employee reported slick and snow-covered road conditions on US-93 from Ninepipes south to Evaro between 6:30 and 7:30 PM MDT.

The Lincoln county emergency manager reported that multiple roofs had been damaged, and trees and power lines were down due to a strong wind gust.  Power was out for several hours from Libby (elevation 2600 ft.) to Happy's Inn on Highway 2.  The nearest observation that reported strong wind gusts was the Zonolite RAWS station at 4200 feet. It reported a gust to 53 mph at 15:06 PM MDT.
The Creston agrimet station measured the strongest wind gust during the event.
The Dent agrimet station recorded a strong wind gust to 58 mph.

The Sheepherder Hill RAWS at 3090 feet reported a gust to 57 mph. Widespread power outages were reported in the Kalispell area due to downed power lines. Flathead Electric reported a total of 3,428 members with outages across northwest Montana.

The Agrimet station in Creston reported wind gusts over 50 mph for a 15 minute period and a temperature drop from 72 to 56 degrees as a strong cold front moved through. There were multiple reports of fallen trees including a Ponderosa Pine with a diameter of 40 inches. Power outages were reported in the Evergreen area due to downed power lines.
High winds caused tree damage and downed power lines to the area causing power outages for 1,367 people in the Swan Lake area.
Strong wind gusts over 50 mph were reported in the Salmon area.
Wind gusts near 50 mph were reported in the Potomac area.
Strong winds between 50 and 60 mph were reported in the Avon area.
A 22 year old male was struck by lightning while changing an irrigation pipe. Injuries were reported as second degree burns.
Scattered power outages were reported from Kalispell to Somers due to lightning strikes.

Power lines were reported down across Mullan Rd.  Large tree branches were reported down at the Missoula Country Club golf course.  Large trees were also reported down in the university district and along Daly Avenue.
Tree branches 2 inches in diameter broken off trees and branches stripped of leaves.

The ASOS at the Kalispell International airport reported a gust to 63 mph. At the time of the gust, temperatures jumped 6 degrees while the relatively humidity values plummeted indicative of a down-slope type wind gust. Flathead Electric reported spotty power outages in Libby, Lakeside, Whitefish and Creston.

The Mid-Lake Flathead buoy located 6.8 miles ESE of Rollins reported sustained winds of 34 mph and gusts up to 51 mph that lasted about 2 hours. A person from the public located near the Flathead Lake West Shore state park near Goose Bay experienced minor beach erosion from 4 foot waves but didn't report any wind.
A forest service employee reported minor flooding on the Yaak River at the Whitetail campground.
Farmer crops adjacent to the Flathead River between Evergreen and Columbia Falls were inundated with water.
Minor flooding occurred to agricultural lands in the low lying areas adjacent to the middle fork of the Flathead River near West Glacier.
Minor flooding occurred across low lying areas adjacent to the north fork of Flathead river.

Flathead county 911 dispatch reported downed power lines and trees with intermittent power outages from Columbia Falls to West Glacier. The Daily Interlake newspaper reported fallen tree branches 2 to 4 inch in diameter due to heavy snow on Dawn Drive in Columbia Falls.
A trained spotter in Condon reported 5 inches of heavy snow weighed down branches and caused power outages.
Seeley Lake ranger station reported multiple Tamarack trees down and power outages due to the weight of new snow.
Granite county dispatch reported slick roads and rock slides at Flint Creek pass between Georgetown lake and Anaconda.  A tree was down at the Georgetown lake dam.
A trained spotter in Anaconda reported 11.5 inches of heavy snow. There were multiple reports of downed trees and branches as well as power outages.

A trained spotter 3 miles WSW of Newcomb reported 4.5 inches of snow. Heavy rain changed to heavy snow by midnight. Multiple 4 to 6 foot in height Aspen trees were bent over while dirt roads were slick and snow-covered.
The first severe thunderstorm developed over the Beaverhead National Forest south of Anaconda before 2pm MDT and tracked northeast over Gregson Hot Springs producing up to one inch hail.

A person from the public reported hail to the estimated size of ping pongs that caused damage to the roof to their house and extensive damage to their camper. The hail lasted for approximately 10 minutes.
The hail began at 11:45 pm MDT and lasted for 10 minutes. The estimated quarter-size hail fell in the last two minutes of the event.

A strong thunderstorm developed just north of Essex and as it moved towards Glacier National Park it released strong gusty winds up to 55 mph. These winds toppled several trees up to 24 inches in diameter in the Apgar Village and Fish Creek campground. A few of the trees fell onto power lines while one large cottonwood branch fell on top of a  Park Service storage building in Apgar Village, causing minor damage.

A strong thunderstorm cell developed 15 miles south of Seeley Lake and by 446 pm MDT it reached its climax in strength reaching up to 44 kft MSL in height. The precipitation core of the thunderstorm dropped after that producing a gust front that reached the Seeley Lake area a little after 5 pm. Multiple Lodgepole pine trees, 50 to 80 feet tall and 8 to 10 inches in diameter, were toppled by strong gusty winds.  The Lodgepole were widely spaced, and with very little root structure on that variety of tree, were particularly susceptible to strong winds.

A thunderstorm cell developed over extreme southeastern Idaho county (over 9 kft terrain) and split into two separate supercells as it moved into Lemhi County. The left-moving supercell tracked across the old Mustang burn scarred Colson Creek drainage basin (Mustang Fire from 2012).  According to Doppler radar estimates, this storm unleashed 0.42 of rainfall in 30 minutes across this drainage basin. At one point the cloud tops reached over 50 kft which meant that the storm had tapped into all the potential instability. These torrential rains produced a debris flow that damaged and made Colson Creek road impassable.  The debris flow traveled over several homeowners' properties and damaged a hydro-electric pump causing power outages.

A high precipitation, left-moving supercell caused very heavy rainfall to fall over the Mustang burn scarred Owl Creek drainage basin inducing a large debris flow. Doppler radar estimates of 0.58 fell 30 minutes ending at 7:28 pm MDT over this basin. The debris flow severely damaged landowners' property including water and fuel barrels, irrigation system and several out-buildings. The debris flow also deposited up to 3 feet of rock and mud plus trees over Salmon River Rd.  A few hours later a spotter in North Fork measured 0.50 of rain in 20 minutes.

A forest service employee reported flash flooding that pushed debris across Salmon River Rd. east of Spring Creek closing one lane. Doppler radar estimated 0.78 of rainfall 30 minutes ending at 4:30 pm MDT across the Spring Creek basin.
A supercell enhanced by the Bitterroot Mountains tracked east-northeast at approximately 43 mph producing 1 inch hail in Victor.

A thunderstorm outflow boundary triggered another cell that grew in strength over higher terrain west of Moiese. This thunderstorm produced hail one inch in diameter, as reported by personnel at the National Bison Range.

A right-moving supercell thunderstorm tracked across the Mission Mountains moving east around 43 mph.  A member from the public 9 miles south of Condon reported golf ball size hail that tore branches and leaves off trees and covered the ground.

As a right-moving supercell approached the Eureka airport, it unleashed severe downdraft winds as reported by the AWOS sensor from the southwest direction for at least 12 minutes. The observer at the airport reported that one airplane flipped over, steel siding was torn off from a hanger, a telephone booth blew over, and an awning structure blew off.

On the afternoon of Wednesday July 17th 2013, a right-moving supercell thunderstorm produced up to one inch hail with estimated winds near 80 mph just north of the Eureka airport in Montana. According to homeowners in the area, the mostly marble-sized hail flew sideways due to the hurricane force wind damaging roof shingles, siding, windows, paint and vehicles, and shredding vegetation. Trees toppled over in a northeast direction implying that winds could have been from the southwest.

On the afternoon of Wednesday July 17th 2013, a right-moving supercell thunderstorm produced up to one inch hail with estimated winds near 80 mph just north of the Eureka airport in Montana. According to homeowners in the area, the mostly marble-sized hail flew sideways due to the hurricane force wind damaging roof shingles, siding, windows, paint and vehicles, and shredding vegetation. Trees toppled over in a northeast direction implying that winds could have been from the southwest.

Local businesses located north of Eureka reported damage to outside equipment due to the wind and hail. Several 4 inch trees broke in half laying down pointing east-northeast. Two fir trees with a base diameter of 16 inches were lost: one fell over while the other broke in half. The wind ripped tin siding off of the buildings.
Local businesses north of Eureka reported damage to outside equipment due to the wind and hail estimated at one inch.

On the afternoon of Wednesday July 17th 2013, a right-moving supercell thunderstorm moved across the region causing severe wind and hail. A local business northwest of Eureka reported at least 30 trees toppled due to the strong wind. Also the combination of wind and hail damaged the greens at a nearby golf course.
A resident reported damage to window screens and 150 fruit trees by the combination of hail and strong wind. They reported that the estimated one inch hail had a disc-shaped appearance.

On the afternoon of Wednesday July 17th 2013, a right-moving supercell thunderstorm developed near Troy and tracked north and east across Rexford. A local business in Rexford reported structure and vehicle damage due to the estimated half-dollar hail. Several teenagers received bruises from the hail when they were on the shore of Lake Kookanusa. They estimated the thunderstorm wind gusts to 50 mph.
A right-moving supercell developed just southeast of Kila and tracked north and east across the Creston area. A local business sustained considerable damage due to the estimated quarter size hail.

A right-moving supercell developed just southeast of Kila and tracked north and east across the Creston area.  A local resident measured up to one inch hail in diameter that covered the ground to three inches deep.

A right-moving supercell developed just southeast of Kila and tracked north and east across the Creston area.  A farmer reported hail accumulation between 6 and 8 inches that dented vehicle hoods and damaged barley, spring wheat and canola crops. The half inch hail was estimated.

A right-moving supercell developed just southeast of Kila and tracked north and east across the Creston area. At least two different people from the Many Lakes residential area reported jagged edged-hail to the estimated size of golf balls. One person said the hail looked like it had marble sized pieces frozen together. Multiple homeowners reported hail damage to their vehicles.
A thunderstorm in its decaying stage unleashed strong gusty winds that blew over a 24 inch diameter tree onto a camper at the Wilderness Gateway Campground on the Lochsa River.
A right-moving supercell formed 30 miles southwest of Marion and tracked northeast around 40 mph to just north of Kila.  A trained spotter located 2 miles north of Kila measured penny sized hail.
A right-moving supercell that tracked from just southwest of Marion moved over Kila and Kalispell. A person from the public in Kalispell measured 1 inch hail.
A right-moving supercell moved across the Missoula International airport and brought penny sized hail.
A trained spotter on the east side of Flathead Lake reported an estimated 1 hail with no damage to cherry trees.

A long-lasting right-moving supercell that tracked over the Missoula International airport continued east-northeast between Seeley Lake and Woodworth. A person from the public estimated penny sized hail just northwest of Woodworth that lasted for 5 minutes. The Missoula Doppler radar observed a three body scatter spike between 12 and 18 thousand feet MSL with this storm which is indicative of large hail.

A very large right-moving supercell tracked east-northeast from Goldcreek to north of Avon bringing with it large hail, severe winds and heavy rain. A rancher 5 miles north of Avon reported a totaled barn, several trees that were either uprooted or broken in half. One of those trees uprooted was a 24 cottonwood.

A very large right-moving supercell unleashed up to ping pong sized hail that decimated a four to five foot tall hay crop. The hail covered the ground to a depth of 2 inches in spots. At least 10 windows were broken. Paint was chipped off from homes. Other damage included a greenhouse roof, vehicle windows and vegetation.

A very large right-moving supercell brought hail and wind damage to ranchers north of Avon. A rancher reported up to half dollar sized hail that brought considerable damage to their hay crop, and windows.
A very large supercell brought estimated 60 mph wind gusts that caused several trees to either uproot or break in half. Most of the trees fell in an easterly direction.

A member of the public in West Kootenai observed a strong and long-lived dust devil that caused roof damage to the Amish school and cut power momentarily at a warehouse. They said this was the strongest one they had ever experienced there in decades.

On July 17, 2013, a multicellular thunderstorm developed a gustnado causing a roof to be torn off of a closed garage and thrown into a power pole. The power pole broke off leaving live wires on the ground. Another shed immediately downstream was torn apart and thrown across the yard. The path of the damage was about 200 yards long and 50 to 100 feet wide. A neighbor watching the event occur from a few feet away, reported swirling debris for at least 10 to 15 seconds.
The Leadore Creek RAWS station at 6,150 ft., reported a 60 mph wind gust between 3:36 and 4:36 pm MDT thanks to a decaying thunderstorm cell that passed just to its north.

A very large right-moving & long-lived supercell developed across south-central Idaho and tracked north and east across northeastern Lemhi county. A trained spotter in Salmon, Idaho reported quarter size hail. Insurance companies reported at least 200 damage claims to both vehicles and homes from downtown, northwest Salmon and between Salmon and Carmen. An auto body reported fixing 15 passenger vehicles and 20 recreation vehicles caused by hail damage. The hail fell for at least 15 minutes damaging roofs, siding, stucco and windows. One person reported this was the worst storm she had seen in 42 years.

A person from the public estimated ping pong size hail as she was rafting on the Salmon River about 100 yards north of the Salmon River I-93 bridge about one mile south of Carmen, Idaho. Their floating party was unable to reach the beach due to strong southerly winds and proceeded to be pelted by large hail for at least five minutes. She reported vivid black and blue bruises on her arms and legs. Her garden located in Carmen was damaged extensively by the hail.
A trained spotter in Salmon, Idaho reported trees down over roadways, power lines down in three different areas with power outages and a  roof over a patio blew off.
A trained spotter north of Racetrack estimated penny sized hail.
A CoCoRaHS member reported penny size hail on the south side of Georgetown Lake.
A NWS employee measured penny sized hail across extreme southwestern Ravalli County.
The US forest service reported that a flash flood had washed out Nut Basin Rd. in the Sheep Fire Burn Area.

A flash flood occurred in the lower Colson Creek area in northwestern Lemhi County over part of the old 2012 Mustang fire burn scar. Colson Creek Rd. and Road 30 needed to be graded afterwards to permit safe vehicle passage. Up to one foot of debris deposited on roads in several places. Also the increased flow, up to 2 feet in Colson Creek, broke up a temporary earthen dam that emptied a pond.
A microburst with estimated 60 mph winds blew down 20+ trees around the crews at the Gold Pan wildfire. Trees blocked roads and crews had to use chainsaws to get out of the area.
A NWS employee reported an estimated 60 mph wind gust just north of Lolo, Montana.
The Ravalli County emergency manager reported that multiple power lines were down around Hamilton.

The Missoula International airport ASOS reported a gust to 54 mph from the south-southeast direction. An intense thunderstorm near Florence produced a strong outflow that traveled north into the Missoula Valley causing multiple trees to be uprooted, downed power lines, & damage to a tent at the Western Montana Fair. The Missoula 911 dispatch reported at least 13 calls related to either power outages or lines down.
A trained spotter two miles south of Clinton measured 1.05 of rainfall in 30 minutes.
A trained spotter in Bonner measured 0.85 of rainfall in 30 minutes.
A person from the public reported penny size hail in Drummond.

A slow moving wet thunderstorm dumped at least 1 of rainfall in one hour just southeast of Drummond. A rancher experienced a 5 foot wall of fast moving water that moved down their driveway. The fast flowing water laden with pea-sized hail and mud severely damaged grain & alfalfa crops, irrigation sprinklers and a fence. They said it was the worst flooding in at least 20 years.

A slow moving thunderstorm produced over an inch of rain in less than one hour during the evening of August 9, 2013 over the terrain southeast of Drummond, Montana. This triggered a flash flood up to four feet high that moved from small hillside gulches located north of Interstate 90 over the highway. One vehicle slid off the road and I-90 was shut down for a period of time until the water levels subsided.

A trained spotter northeast of Carmen estimated that most hail sizes ranged between 0.75 and 1 but there were a few that were up to ping pong size. The hail damaged several fruit trees and tomatoes. His neighbor's wood siding on his house was also damaged.

The Bert Mooney airport located four miles south-southeast of Butte reported a strong west wind gust of 53 mph due to a thunderstorm that moved through. Power companies reported six utility poles on a 50K transmission line down due to the storms in southwest Montana. This caused power outages in Silver Bow county that lasted through the night. The strong winds also caused downed trees in the Butte area.

A newspaper in Butte reported that the top of an approximately 40 foot Ponderosa Pine tree fell over onto Park Street near the Montana Tech hill. Looking at the photo, the tree apparently fell towards the east direction.
The Missoula 911 dispatch reported multiple trees and power lines down on Whitetail Dr and Dolly Varden Dr.
A trained spotter from Woods Bay reported power outages with at least one tree snapped in half.
A NWS employee reported trees bending with one large tree blown down. The waves on Flathead lake were the highest she had ever seen.
The Camels Hump lookout reported a measured wind gust to 58 mph during the early morning hours of August 26th.
A trained spotter reported that the power was out from 0230 to 0645 hrs MDT on August 26th.
A member of the public reported a strong thunderstorm with heavy rain, lightning gusty winds that moved through between 2 and 3 am MDT. They received 0.75 total rainfall measured.

A member of the public measured strong gusty winds that pushed over three large Ponderosa Pine trees and power outages.  A tree fell onto a transmission line that impacted two power substations causing power outages for the Many Lakes and Echo Lake area.

The Kalispell ASOS station measured a strong southerly wind gust to 55 mph.  The Flathead Valley power companies reported that around 5,000 customers lost power from 8pm MDT through the early morning hours on August 26. Multiple trees fell on power lines causing the outages.
An 80-foot-tall pine tree fell over on 5th Ave West in Kalispell crushing a Corvette and damaging a truck, car and a boat.
Downed power lines caused power outages and temporarily blocked U.S. 2 in Evergreen Sunday night.
A trained spotter northwest of Kila reported estimated penny sized hail and strong winds estimated at 50 mph that blew off patio furniture from their deck.
A trained spotter northwest of Kalispell reported strong winds with penny size hail.

The weather sensor at the Kalispell International airport reported a gust to 55 mph,  and heavy rain with reduced visibilities as low as one mile for at least 19 minutes. It reported 0.27 of rainfall in 23 minutes from 4:32 to 4:55 pm MDT. As the gust front moved through the Kalispell area, there were reports of a dust storm that brought visibilities down to near zero for several minutes before the rain began. The dust cloud moved through an open door of the Glacier High School setting off fire alarms and filling the school with dust. The school's custodial staff had to spend the night removing and cleaning the dust out. The strong wind caused large trees to fall, knocking down power lines and blocking roads. The power company reported approximately 2,500 people without power for a time that evening.
A trained spotter reported strong gusty winds that brought down power lines and trees of unknown size. They also reported pea size hail.
A trained spotter reported nickel size hail southwest of Columbia Falls.

A Glacier National Park official reported several cars damaged from downed trees. They also reported that there were several areas with rocks on the road partially blocking lanes, but no major landslide activity. Approximately 22 miles to the northwest in Polebridge, the RAWS sensor measured a wind gust to 50 mph at 4:50 pm MDT.

The Daily Inter Lake newspaper reported that a tree had fallen on a home on Kokanee Bend two miles southwest of Columbia Falls. The law enforcement scanner traffic indicated that the tree had cut the home in half trapping the people inside. They were uninjured and were eventually able to get out of the house.
The Kriley Creek RAWS, located at 5,200 ft MSL, reported 0.52 of rain in one hour. Radar data reveals that the rain could have fallen much quicker in approximately 30 minutes or less.
The Salmon RAWS, located at 5,100 ft. MSL, reported 0.58 of rainfall in one hour. According to radar storm echo trends, the rain could have fallen in less than 30 minutes time.

Although not under the main multicellular thunderstorm cores, the Indianola RAWS located at 3,529 ft MSL still reported 0.39 of rain in one hour. Considering what other weather stations in the area reported, this amount could have fallen in a much quicker timescale.

The Kriley Creek RAWS at 5,200 ft. MSL reported a hurricane force wind gust associated with a wet multicellular thunderstorm. It also reported a 69 mph gust during the 4:51 to 5:51 pm MDT hour. Doppler radar data shows that this gust probably occurred after 5:30 pm MDT. It also showed a wind shift from a west-southwest to a north-northeast direction as the storm passed to the northeast between the 5:51 and 6:51 pm MDT observations. This potentially could be classified as a wet microburst. Power and phone outages were reported in North Fork.

The Salmon RAWS  located 3 miles southwest of the city of Salmon at 5,100 feet reported a strong wind gust to 69 mph that occurred sometime between 5:36 and 6:00 pm MDT. Weather spotters reported trees down and a power outage in Salmon. A television news station reported on Facebook that over 5,000 people were affected. A person from the public in Salmon commented on this post that power was still out in parts of Salmon at 9 am MDT on September 6th.
A washout near Cramer Creek closed Salmon River Road/NF - 30 for a time. Nearby weather stations in Lemhi county reported anywhere from 0.39 up to 0.58 in less than 30 minutes with these storms.

Very wet thunderstorms triggered flash flooding in the Kriley Creek drainage. This debris flow traveled over the northbound lane of highway 93 shutting it down for a period. The BLM road Kriley Gulch Rd was closed in the Kriley Creek drainage due to another separate washout.
The Kalispell International airport tower observer estimated half dollar sized hail. Out of at least 5 vehicles damaged, one cost $5,600 to repair.
The Kalispell International Airport ASOS measured 0.38 of rain in 20 minutes with a west-southwest wind gust to 25 mph at 1:54 pm.
A person from the public that lives on the southeast side of Georgetown Lake at an elevation of 6,400 feet measured 10 inches of snow with trees down on the south side of the lake.
A person from the public located 6 miles south-southeast of Janney at an elevation around 7,100 feet, estimated that 18 inches fell with the storm.

The Basin Creek SNOTEL located at 7,180 ft. reported 14 inches of snow with 1.70 of snow water equivalent. The temperatures ranged from freezing to the middle 30s at this station located about 14 miles south of Butte.

A spotter located 7 miles south of Butte at 6,200 ft. estimated greater than 6 inches of heavy snow and measured 1.73 inches of precipitation during this event. They reported that the weight of the snow collapsed their carport and at least 6 aspen trees fell over. They were not home during the event, but at 6 am MDT on September 27th they measured 6 inches.  Using the Basin Creek 8:1 snow to liquid ratio for the event, this spotter could have potentially seen 10 to 14 inches total.

The MacDonald Pass weather station reported moderate to heavy snow between 9 pm MDT on the 25th and 12 am MDT on the 26th.  Road temperatures cooled to freezing at 9 pm and didn't warm up until 9 am MDT on the 26th. Montana DOT reported that chains were required on towing units and also that a semi-truck jack-knifed between 2 and 2:30 am MDT on Highway 12 near MacDonald Pass mile-marker 30 westbound.

The Warm Springs SNOTEL located 8 miles east-southeast of Philipsburg at 7,800 ft, reported 9 inches of snow that fell in 14 hours. It also reported a snow water equivalent of 0.70.  The sheriff in Philipsburg only reported a trace of slush for this event.
A trained spotter located 7.4 miles northwest of Anaconda at 6,000 ft. measured 1.2 of snow. They also reported 0.70 of precipitation that comprised of both rain and snow.

A person from the public 3 miles southeast of the city of Butte estimated that 5 inches of wet snow fell overnight. The Bert Mooney airport reported snow with visibilities from one mile to three-quarter mile from 9:53 pm to 11:53 pm MDT on the 25th. There were several reports of trees and tree limbs down in the area due to the heavy weight of the snow. A few trees were reported to have fallen onto power lines causing power outages. The Montana DOT reported that chains were required over Homestake Pass on I-90 and the east-bound lane closed for four hours due to a jack knifed semi 16 miles east of the pass.
A person from the public estimated 3 inches of snow fell in Walkersville at 6,300 ft. just two miles north of Butte.

A spotter located 10 miles south of Butte at 6,500 ft. measured 10 inches of very wet snow that caused several ponderosa pine and aspen trees to either fall down or break in half. Power was out from 3 am through 5:30 am MDT on the 26th.

Webcams from Lost Trail Pass (7,090 ft.) revealed snow-covered roads for much of the evening on the 25th through the morning hours of the 26th. The nearby Saddle Mountain SNOTEL located at 7,900 ft. measured 6 inches of snow with 0.90 of snow water equivalent. The pass had to be plowed often during the night which is a rare occurrence and quite possibly due to the unseasonable nature of this event.

Webcams from Lost Trail Pass (7,090 ft.) revealed snow-covered roads for much of the evening on the 25th through the morning hours of the 26th. The nearby Saddle Mountain SNOTEL located at 7,900 ft. measured 6 inches of snow with 0.90 of snow water equivalent. The pass had to be plowed often during the night which is a rare occurrence and quite possibly due to the unseasonable nature of this event.

A Glacier National Park service employee reported that the Going-to-the-Sun Road was closed from Big Bend up to Logan Pass from 11:28 am MDT on the 25th until 11:17 am MDT on the 26th. They reported that at least 3 inches fell at the pass and the road was very slick and icy.
The Morgan Creek SNOTEL located 30 miles southwest of Salmon at 7,600 ft. measured 5 inches of snow.
The Idaho Transportation Department estimated 5 inches of snow that fell at Gilmore Summit at 7,186 ft. Webcams revealed snow-covered roads at times during the event.
A person from the public 5 miles south-southeast of Leadore estimated that 6 inches of snow fell.
A person from the public in Leadore (5,900 ft.) estimated that 2 inches of snow fell during the storm.

The Flattop Mountain SNOTEL located at 6,300 ft or 9 miles north-northwest of Logan Pass reported 6 inches of snow. This SNOTEL reported a total of 4.20 of precipitation from the 28th through the 30th.

The Glacier National Park service reported more than 8 inches of snow fell at Logan Pass. The Going-to-the-Sun road closed at 7:19 am MDT on the 30th due to slush on the road and wind gusts to 40 mph.

A power pole in Florence had reportedly been snapped off by wind causing power outages for several hours. The local sheriff had to direct the morning commute. A NWS employee located in Lolo, estimated that the winds gusted to 50 mph at 8:14 am MDT with the passage of the cold front.

The Saddle Mountain SNOTEL at 7900 ft., located 1 mile west of Lost Trail Pass reported 3 inches of snow with temperatures near freezing. The ITD webcam at Lost Trail Pass showed slick conditions during this time-frame. An undetermined amount of light snow fell again on the morning of the 30th with the webcam showing slick roads at 8 am MDT.
The Basin Creek SNOTEL located at 7,180 ft. or 23 miles south of Butte reported 21 inches in 25 hours. It reported heavy snow from 7 am to 11 am MDT and from 8 pm to 11 pm MDT on Oct. 3rd.

A person from the public located 19 miles south-southeast of Butte at 6,600 ft., reported 17 inches of snow (estimated). A weather spotter located one mile to the north reported that power was out for several hours on Thursday morning October 3rd. They also confirmed the report of 17 inches of snow from this event.

The ASOS weather sensor at the Bert Mooney Airport (5,545 ft.), located 6 miles south-southeast of Butte, Montana reported rain that changed to snow during the early morning hours of Oct. 3rd. It reported moderate snow from 9 am to 12 pm MDT on the 3rd with winds gusting out of the northerly direction between 17 and 31 mph. One to two inches of total snow fell at the airport and in the city of Butte. The Montana DOT reported snow and slush at Homestake Pass on I-90. A 60-year-old woman and her 37-year-old-son from Washington State were killed in a roll-over accident on I-90 west of Butte (west of the Ramsay exit) at 6:45 am MDT on Friday Oct. 4th. A Montana Highway Patrol trooper reported the driver was going too fast for the slick road conditions.

A Butte news broadcast video showed blowing snow with limited visibilities on I-15 south of Butte specifically near the Feeley exit at mile marker 112 at 10:30 am MDT on Oct. 3rd. The roads appeared to be icy and slick as well. They said that traffic was only moving at 40 mph.

A trained spotter on the south end of Georgetown Lake at 6,386 ft. reported a storm total snowfall of 8 with temperatures near 29 degrees F. The Peterson Meadows SNOTEL located at 7,200 ft. or about 6 miles southwest of Georgetown Lake reported a storm total of 13 inches from 2 am to 4 pm MDT on Oct. 3rd. The Barker Lakes SNOTEL at 8,250 ft. or 15 miles west-southwest of Anaconda reported a storm total snow accumulation of 10 inches from 3 am to 1 pm MDT on Oct 3rd. The Warm Springs SNOTEL located 12 miles southeast of Philipsburg at 7,800 ft. reported 6 inches of snow from 5 to 10 am MDT.

A ranch near Painted Rocks Lake on the West Fork Rd., 21 miles southwest of Conner at 4,847 ft. estimated 6 inches of snow during this event. The snow covered the road, but melted within a few days. The Skalhaho Summit SNOTEL at 7,250 ft., located 36 miles west of Georgetown Lake in the Sapphire Range reported 5 inches of snow that ended at 8 pm MDT on Oct. 3rd.

The Idaho Transportation Department weather sensor at Lost Trail Pass on US-93 at 7,090 ft. reported visibilities less than one quarter mile from 1:45 am to 10:30 am MDT with heavy snow. Chains were required for towing vehicles over Lost Trail due to the conditions through 2:25 pm MDT on Oct. 3rd. The Saddle Mtn. SNOTEL at 7,900 ft., located 1.7 miles west of US-93 reported 9 inches of snow with temperatures ranging from 26 to 28 degrees F. SNOTEL stations located between 7,600 and 8,600 ft. in the Beaverhead and Bitterroot Mtns. reported 9 to 15 inches of total snowfall. A spotter from Salmon reported 10 inches of snowfall with this event at Williams Creek Summit.

Even though it started to snow in the early morning hours of October 3rd, the road temperatures at Gilmore Summit (7,018 ft.) on State Highway 28 didn't approach freezing until 6 pm MDT.  Winds picked up between 17 to 25 mph from the northwest with falling temperatures into the upper 20s. Blowing snow reduced visibilities to less than 1/2 mile at times and roads became slick. The Meadow Lake SNOTEL located at 9,150 ft., 6.5 miles west-southwest of Gilmore Summit reported 0.90 of precipitation which could have equated to at least a foot of snow with temperatures in the mid 20s.

The Flathead Lake Biological Station(FLBS) Mid-Lake buoy, located 8 miles east-southeast of Rollins, reported a peak wind of 65 mph from an easterly direction. A spokesperson from the FLBS reported that between 15 to 20 trees, consisting of both Tamarack & Fir, had fallen due to the winds. One of the trees fell onto a garage causing minor damage. The winds continued to gust over 50 mph through 7 am MDT on Oct. 28th. The FLBS Narrows buoy reported a peak wind gust to 50 mph at 7:33 pm MDT on Oct 27th from the northeast. According to the Mission Valley Power Company, more than 500 residences lost electrical service mostly along the eastern shore of Flathead Lake, with 350 of them located on Finley Point.  A 300-year-old ponderosa pine and root system crashed through electrical lines on the east side of North Finley Point Road at 7 pm MDT on Oct. 27th. A resident on the west side of Skidoo Bay reported 6 foot waves due to the persistent 40+ mph easterly winds. They also reported that they lost electricity for 14 hours.

A trained spotter 8 miles south of Woods Bay reported several fallen trees, one of which totaled their carport and another broke a utility light. A neighbor reported a fallen tree that damaged the metal roof of a tractor barn. The wind gust was recorded by a Heath anemometer and the spotter's location does have some tree coverage.

A person from the public in Columbia Falls reported a wind gust to 62 mph at 5:35 pm MDT on Oct. 27th according to their personal weather station. The Flathead Electric Cooperative reported nearly 800 power outages from the storm in the Columbia Falls and Marion areas.
