They reported approximately 5,000 co-op members lost power, most through the night, as trees or limbs hit power lines. The ASOS weather sensor at the Glacier Park International Airport measured a wind gust to 48 mph from the northeast at 4:44 pm MDT on Oct 27th.

The Montana road report for Marias Pass overnight showed snow, blowing and drifting snow. The DOT road crew estimated 3 to 4 inches at Marias Pass, although probably difficult to discern due to blowing snow. The nearby Pike Creek Snotel reported a total of 11 of snowfall with 0.30 of precipitation. The Marias Pass HADS sensor had reported 0.28 of precipitation. The Fielding RAWS station between Essex and Marias Pass reported easterly wind gusts between 20 and 33 mph.

The Montana Highway Patrol and Butte-Silver Bow County police responded to a combined total of almost 40 accidents Monday with most of them occurring on the morning of the 28th. The trained spotter at the Bert Mooney airport estimated 6 inches of snowfall.

The Idaho Transportation Department (ITD) weather sensor at Gilmore Summit reported gusty winds to 26 mph with visibilities that dropped below 1/2 mile at times due to blowing snow. The ITD had to close Highway 28 from Leadore south to the Lemhi County line for 11 hours from 7:51 pm MDT on the 28th to 6:56 am MDT on the 29th due to blowing & drifting snow and reduced visibilities.
MacDonald Pass experienced snow with gusty winds between 20 and 33 mph which caused periods of blowing snow and visibilities less than one half mile at times.
A person located at Montana Tech in Butte reported heavy snow that brought limited visibilities and impeded traffic.

The Montana DOT reported heavy snow Sunday afternoon Nov. 3rd through the morning hours of Monday Nov. 4th on US-2. The snowfall was especially heavy between Essex (mile-marker 180) and Stanton Creek (mile-marker 192) along US-2.  They estimated that up to 2 feet of snow fell during the storm in these areas. The Marias Pass HADS weather sensor at 5233 ft. reported 0.50 of precipitation with temperatures falling into the lower 20's. Using a 20:1 average snow to liquid ratio Marias Pass could have seen a foot of snow.

An avalanche forecaster measured 16 inches of total storm snowfall in Essex by Monday afternoon Nov. 4th, 12 hours after the snowfall ended. The BNSF Shed 4 weather sensor (4520 ft.) located approximately 10 miles southwest of Marias Pass just off of US-2, reported 12 of snow with 0.90 of precipitation 32 hours ending at 7 am MST on Monday Nov. 4th. It reported heavy snowfall rates between 1 to 1.8 per hour from 1 and 8 pm MST on Sunday Nov. 3rd. The Shed 7 weather station at 6363 ft. and 11.5 miles southwest of Marias Pass, reported 25 of snow from this storm. On Nov. 3rd, the arctic front pushed through Marias Pass by 3 pm MST and into Essex by 5:16 pm MST.

The Montana DOT at Lookout Pass on I-90 reported a storm total snowfall of 8 inches from Saturday evening Nov. 2nd through Monday morning the 4th. No accidents were reported, but road surfaces were reported to be slick especially by late evening on the 2nd when road temperatures cooled to freezing and below. The nearby Lookout SNOTEL reported 1.00 of total precipitation during the event. The COOP station 1 mile west of Haugan reported a storm total snowfall of  2 with 0.75 of precipitation.

A cold core upper level trough dropped out of British Columbia providing the necessary lift and instability to trigger showers across western Montana early on November 4th. The unstable atmosphere saw a 24 degree difference between Flathead Lake water temperatures(8.9 deg. C) and at 9,665 ft. MSL(700 millibars) -15 deg. C.  A convergent boundary set up southwest of Wood's Bay with cool northerly winds coming out of the Flathead Valley and relatively mild southerly winds moving across the lake. This boundary provided the vertical lift to develop the band of graupel and snow showers.  A waterspout was spotted by passers-by traveling on MT-83 near mile-marker 24.  Viewing the photos and video that Mike and Dana Marchetti took, it appears that there could have been multiple vortices based on darkened shadows in the vicinity of the main vortex. The waterspout remained over Flathead Lake and no damage was reported.

A local newspaper reporter tweeted at 7:57 am MST on November 4th that slick roads had caused several accidents from Frenchtown to just east of US-93 in Missoula, or between mile markers 92 and 98 on Interstate 90. The MT DOT Ninemile sensor reported snow falling continuously from 6 pm MST on Sunday evening Nov. 3rd through 11:45 am MST on Monday Nov. 4th with road temperatures ranging between 28 and 32 degrees F.  Nearby snowfall amounts include: 1.5 Evaro Hill, 1.3 2 mi. west of Bonner, 3 Arlee, 0.3 Missoula Int. Airport, and 1.5 Seeley Lake.

Snow showers developed on the back side of an exiting upper level trough across northwest Montana by Sunday afternoon November 3rd. With warm temperatures initially the showers were not much of an impact, but as they grew in size, visibilities dropped down to less than one half mile or less at times, air & road temperatures fell to near freezing and roads became snow-covered and slick. A weather spotter in Columbia Falls reported 4 of total snow with a majority of falling as moderate to heavy snow from 3:37 to 7:37 pm MST on the 3rd. Other snowfall amounts include: 2 5 miles north-northwest of Creston, 3 at the Glacier Park Int. Airport and 2.2 at Bigfork/Ferndale.

The COOP observer in West Glacier reported a storm total snowfall of 7.3 between Nov. 2nd and Nov. 4th with 0.85 of precipitation. The COOP observer at the Hungry Horse Dam reported 4 of snow with 1.07 of precipitation while a citizen in the town of Hungry Horse measured 6 of snow by 10:30 am MST on Monday, Nov. 4th. A person from the public located 1 mile southeast of Swan Lake estimated that 4 inches had fallen by 10:24 am MST on the 4th. They reported that MT-83 was snow-covered.  This snowfall was most likely connected with the snow band that developed over Flathead Lake just southwest of Wood's Bay.

Heavy mountain snowfall developed on Saturday Nov. 2nd across northwest Montana. The Hawkins Lake SNOTEL at 6,450 ft. located in extreme northwest Lincoln County reported 1 per hour snowfall rates on the 2nd from 2 to 11 pm MDT with 9 inches of snowfall. This sensor reported 13 total storm snowfall with 1.60 of precipitation through 4 am MST on Nov. 4th. The COOP observer located 9 miles north-northeast of Yaak reported a storm total snowfall of 2.4 with 1.04 of precipitation. On Sunday Nov. 3rd at 7:17 pm MST, a weather spotter reported moderate snow with visibilities less than one half mile from Marion to North Star Meadows and slick conditions on US-2.

The Pierce COOP observer at 3,185 ft., reported 7 of snow on Nov. 4th while their total precipitation from Nov. 3-4 was 0.93. The Elk Butte SNOTEL at 5,690 ft. located in northwestern Clearwater County reported a storm total snowfall of 11 with 1.20 of precipitation. The Cool Creek SNOTEL at 6,280 ft., located in northeastern Clearwater County reported a storm total snowfall of 19 with 1.90 of precipitation through 1 pm PST on Nov. 4th.  Other snow totals include: 8 Shanghi Summit SNOTEL (4,570 ft.), 14 Crater Meadows SNOTEL (5,960 ft.).

A weather spotter from Weippe at 3,022 ft. reported 2.5 of snowfall which accumulated on Highway 11 making for slick conditions. The ITD road sensor at Greer Grade at 3,112 ft. and 9 miles west of Weippe on Highway 11, reported snow on the road with grip levels suggesting that slippery conditions existed from 2 am through 7:45 am PST on Nov. 4th. Light snow also fell along across the Camas Prairie with ITD road sensors at both Frei Hill and the Concrete Section reporting slick roads Sunday evening Nov. 3rd through Monday morning Nov. 4th.

The Lolo Pass SNOTEL at 5,240 ft., reported a storm total snowfall of 6 with 1.00 of precipitation. The ITD sensors at Lolo Pass and at Elk City (3,939 ft.) reported slick roadways both Saturday (Nov. 2nd) and Sunday (Nov. 3rd) nights while improving during the daytime. The Savage Pass SNOTEL at 6,170 ft. reported 6 of snow with 0.60 of precipitation.

The ITD web cam at Lost Trail Pass at 7,090 ft. revealed off and on snow showers on Saturday Nov. 2nd and US-93 became snow covered by 7:16 pm MDT. There was a lull in the snow on Nov. 3rd before snow fell again by the early morning of the 4th. The Saddle Mountain SNOTEL at 7900 ft., located 1 mile west of Lost Trail Pass reported a three day storm total snowfall of 5.

events.cz_name: LOWER HELLS CANYON / SALMON RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Light snow fell at Whitebird Hill on US-95 at 4,222 ft. by 4:40 pm PST on Sunday Nov. 3rd. The ITD road sensor reported ice by 6:31 pm PST. By 2 am PST on Monday Nov. 4th, Whitebird Hill was snow covered and slippery. The snow tapered off by 7 am PST on Monday Nov. 4th, while road surfaces continued to be slick until around 10 am PST.
Broadcast media on Facebook reported an estimated 3.3 inches of snowfall in Eureka. Temperatures remained at 30 degrees F during the snowfall while roads became slick.
A person from the public in Essex reported an estimated 2 of snowfall that fell in 12 hours. The West Glacier COOP observer reported 2.1 of snow with 0.17 of precipitation on November 6th.

The Glacier Park International Airport reported 3 of snowfall through 5 am MST on Nov. 6th. Multiple vehicle slide-offs and accidents were reported in the Kalispell area. Other snow totals from this storm include: Kalispell 1.8, Whitefish 4, Bigfork/Ferndale 3.8, Creston 2.8, Lake Blaine 3.5, 1 mi. SW Columbia Falls 5, 4 mi. southeast Charlo 1.5, and Ronan 2.

Snow developed during the morning of Tuesday November 5th at Lookout Pass on Interstate 90, on the border of Idaho and Montana. It continued through much of the night and ended Wednesday morning. Web cams at the pass depicted slick road conditions especially during the night-time hours.

Showers brought 1 to 3 inches of snow from Tuesday November 5th through November 6th causing roadways to become slick. There were 7 vehicle accidents reported in Missoula between 6 pm MST Nov. 5th through 3 am MST Nov. 6th. Several of these wrecks occurred on the bridges along Reserve St. with no significant injuries reported. A NWS employee reported snow covered and slick roadways on US-93 from Florence north to Missoula between 5 and 7 am MST on November 6th. Snowfall totals include: 1.5 Missoula Int. Airport, 2 Missoula, 2.5 2 mi. northeast of Missoula, 3 Florence, Trace from Stevensville to Hamilton.

The Seeley Lake HADS sensor at 4,100 ft. reported 0.23 of total precipitation with temperatures around 29 degrees F between Nov. 5 and 6. A weather spotter located 1.6 miles east of Seeley Lake reported 2.8 of snowfall. They reported that the roads were slushy. The Greenough Hill MTDOT sensor reported road temperatures at freezing from 7 pm MST Nov 5 through 8:33 am MST on Nov 6. Other snowfall totals include: 6 1 mi. south of Condon, 5 Kraft Creek SNOTEL 7.5 mi. southwest of Condon, 5 Potomac, and 1.5 Bonner. The Missoula County dispatch reported a vehicle accident near mile marker 107 on I-90 east of Missoula on the morning of Nov. 6th.

Snow developed by 1:40 pm MST at Lolo Pass and by 5:30 pm MST at Lost Trail Pass. The snow ended around 7:30 am MST on November 6th. The highway sensor at Lolo Pass reported slick conditions from 3:38 pm MST on 11/5 through 8:24 am MST on 11/6. The highway sensor at Lost Trail Pass reported slick conditions from 8:30 pm MST on 11/5 through 6:30 am MST on 11/6. The Lolo Pass SNOTEL reported 3 of storm snowfall while the Saddle Mountain SNOTEL near Lost Trail received 2 of snow.

MacDonald Pass on US-12 at milepost 27.9 reported snow from the evening of Nov. 5th through the morning hours of Nov. 6th. Winds were steady 15 to 21 mph with gusts up to 33 mph. Visibility data is not available, but one web cam image from 7 am MST on Nov. 6th indicated blowing snow reducing visibility less than one mile while the roads appeared snow-covered. Media reported 2 inches of snowfall in Bearmouth and 3 inches by Divide (I-15 southwest of Butte).

Snow began just before rush hour on Thursday November 7th across portions of Lincoln County. MTDOT at Crystal Creek, about 20 miles south of Libby on US-2, reported an estimated 2.5 of snow before changing to snow by later Thursday morning. A weather spotter located 8 mi. north of Eureka reported 1.5 of snow. At 6:50 am MST on Nov. 7th, MTDOT reported that US-2 from Marion to Libby was slick and MT-56 was snow-packed.

The West Glacier COOP observer reported 2.7 of snowfall with 0.71 of precipitation for November 7th. The MTDOT road sensor at Essex reported steady snow for much of the day on the 7th and was intermittent on the 8th. The web cam at Essex depicted snow-covered conditions at 10:46 am on the 7th. The only period that saw above freezing road surface temperatures on US-2 at Essex was between 1 pm and 5:28 pm MST on the 7th.  Flattop Mountain SNOTEL (6,300 ft.), located 20 miles east-northeast of Polebridge reported a storm total precipitation of 1.30. The Pike Creek SNOTEL (5,930 ft.), located near Marias Pass reported 6 of snow from 6 pm MST on the 7th to 5 pm MST on the 8th.

Glacier Park International Airport reported 1 of snowfall with 0.40 of precipitation between Nov. 7-8. With ground temperatures at or just below freezing on the morning of November 7th, roads became slick with the light snowfall. There were 6 vehicle accidents and 4 slideoffs reported in the Flathead Valley from 7 am to 9:32 am MST on Nov. 7th. The Flathead County dispatch reported that many of the accidents were as a result of the slick conditions caused by the snow. The MTDOT road reports at 8:47 am MST on Nov. 7th indicated that MT-35 from Yellow Bay to S-206 Jct., and Kalispell to Whitefish had snowcover.

MTDOT reported freezing rain from Swamp Creek Hill (mile-marker 24 on MT-200) or 1 mile east-southeast of Tuscor at 6:50 am MST on Nov. 7th. On Nov. 7th, Lookout Pass on I-90 saw snow briefly change to freezing rain by 9:27 am MST before changing to all rain by 10 am.  Lookout Pass saw a change back to snow by 4:38 pm MST on the 7th and continued through 11:52 am MST on the 8th.

The ITD Lolo Pass sensor reported snow that changed to freezing rain by 5:38 am MST which continued until 9:40 am on Nov. 7th. When the cold front moved through around 7 pm, it reported heavy snow which changed to light snow by 7:53 pm. The Lolo Pass SNOTEL reported a precipitation total of 1.20, but its snow depth sensor was not working properly to be able to determine snowfall totals. Of that precipitation total, 0.50 fell after the cold front went through, so at least 5 of snowfall is possible at Lolo Pass. Lost Trail Pass reported periods of snow starting at 5:30 am MST and continued through 4:30 am MST on the 8th. The ITD sensor reported dense fog between 1:30 and 7:30 pm MST on the 7th. The Saddle Mountain SNOTEL located 1 mile west of Lost Trail reported a storm total snowfall of 6 inches.

The Little Rock Creek RAWS (5,507 ft. elevation) located 4.3 miles west-northwest of Darby reported a gust to 59 mph between 7:09 pm and 8:09 pm MST on November 7th. The Ravalli County sheriff reported power lines down in Darby (3,885 ft. elevation) due to strong winds. The Deer Mountain RAWS located 6 miles east of Darby at 7,282 ft., reported a wind gust to 57 mph between 8:06 pm and 9:06 pm MST on Nov. 7th.

The Anaconda AWOS located 4 miles east-northeast of the city of Anaconda reported a high wind gust of 60 mph associated with a cold front passage at 9 pm MST on Nov. 7th. The Deer Lodge County sheriff dispatch reported several trees and power lines down on the west side of Anaconda. A tree fell onto a power line near the intersection of Mt. Haggin Dr. and Theater Lane and started a fire. This location is approximately 2.5 miles west-northwest of Anaconda. There was a power outage which lasted for 2 hours and 20 minutes.

A cold front brought rain that changed to snow with strong gusty winds at MacDonald Pass on US-12 at milepost 27.9 around 9:14 pm MST on November 7th. Winds gusted as high as 42 mph with the frontal passage, but continued to be blustery between 20 and 41 mph through the night into the morning of November 8th. With the combination of relative humidity levels at one hundred percent and falling snow with strong winds, the visibility could have been near zero from 9:14 to 10:46 pm MST on Nov. 7th. Blowing snow was not an impact due to the wet snow, but road conditions remained slick through the morning of the 8th. Other locations affected by the cold front include Georgetown Lake, Butte and Homestake Pass. These areas saw light accumulation of snow on the road with strong gusty winds between 30 and 40 mph.

A person from the public in Essex reported 12 of snow as of 9:20 pm MST on Nov. 10th. They reported that US-2 was so bad that their boss had advised them not to travel. Earlier in the day they reported that roads were slick due to a layer of ice under the snow. The Pike Creek SNOTEL located 1.6 miles southeast of Marias Pass reported a total of 8 hours of heavy snow between 4 am and 5 pm MST on the 5th with a storm total snowfall of 11. The arctic front pushed through Marias Pass by 5:30 am MST on Nov. 10th which contributed to the heavy snowfall rates. The Shed 4 weather station (4,520 ft.) located 6 mi. southwest of Marias Pass measured 14.8 of snow with 0.75 of precipitation. The Summit HADS located at Marias Pass measured 0.60 of precipitation which could equate to 12 to 14 of snow(using a 20 to 1 snow to liquid ratio which matches Shed 4 observations).

A trained spotter reported that road conditions were terrible at 7:22 am MST Nov. 10th from West Glacier to Columbia Falls on US-2. The West Glacier COOP reported a storm total snowfall of 12 from Nov. 10-11 with 0.97 of precipitation. They also reported 0.67 of precipitation on Nov. 10th which was the 2nd highest amount since 1949. Other storm total snowfall amounts include: 7 Hungry Horse, 8-10 in Polebridge, and 7 Noisy Basin SNOTEL in the Swan Range at 6,040 ft.

The Olney COOP observer reported 3 of snow between Nov. 10-11 with 0.58 of precipitation. The COOP observer located 9 mi. north-northeast of Yaak reported 2.2 of snowfall with 0.24 of precipitation on Nov. 10th. There were reports of slushy conditions in Libby, Eureka, and Troy during the morning of Nov. 10th.

A weather spotter reported terrible road conditions on US-2 from West Glacier to Columbia Falls at 7:22 am MST on Nov. 10th. They reported light steady snow with up to 3.3 of snowfall through 10 am MST. The Glacier Park International Airport reported snowfall from midnight through 8:14 am MST on Nov. 10th with only 0.5 of accumulation. Glacier Park International Airport also reported 0.77 of precipitation on Nov. 10th which was the 2nd highest amount for the day.

MTDOT reported up 3 to 5 inches of storm total snowfall on US-2 between Libby and Happy's Inn with up to 8 inches that fell along a 5 mile stretch of US-2 between McGinnis Meadows to Loon Lake in a 36 hour period. This caused slick conditions at times due to snow and slush on the roads. The road sensor at Crystal Creek, about 19.6 miles south-southeast of Libby, reported snow with road temperatures at or below freezing during the evening and morning hours between the 15th and 17th. Other snow totals include: 4.8 9 mi. NNE of Yaak COOP, 6.1 30 mi. SSE of Libby COOP, 1.5 Libby 1 mi. NE RS COOP, 8 Olney COOP, and 2.9 1 mi. SE Marion.

A weather spotter that works as a ranger for Glacier National Park reported that up to 2 feet of snow had fallen on North Fork Rd., north of the park headquarters. The West Glacier COOP reported 9 of total storm snowfall while the Hungry Horse Dam COOP reported 11. The park ranger reported that several vehicles became stuck in the snow because of the snow depth. The Flattop Mountain SNOTEL, located 9.7 miles northwest of Logan Pass at 6,300 feet reported at storm total snowfall of 16 with 2.00 of total precipitation. The Emery Creek SNOTEL, located 5 miles south-southeast of West Glacier at 4,350 ft., reported 14 of total storm snowfall. A weather spotter from the Spotted Bear ranger station, located 40 miles southeast of Hungry Horse at 3,753 ft., reported a storm total snowfall of 8.

Numerous natural (slab) and human triggered avalanches were reported in the Jewel Basin in the Swan Range by the Flathead Avalanche Center on Saturday November 16th. The Noisy Basin SNOTEL located 8.8 mi. east-southeast of Creston at 6,040 ft. reported a storm total snowfall of 24 with 3.20 of precipitation.

The Glacier Park International Airport received 3 of total storm snowfall that mainly fell on November 17th. The temperatures on the morning of the 17th ranged from the upper 20s to near 30 degrees F. and road conditions were slick due to the snow in the Kalispell area. Other measured storm snowfall totals include: 3 Columbia Falls, 2.5 8 mi. north of Finley Point, 2 3 mi. east-northeast of Bigfork, 2 5 mi. north of Creston, and 1 4 mi. east-southeast Pablo.

A NWS employee reported that 2 inches of snow had already fallen on the road at mile marker 4 on Interstate 90 by 4:54 pm MST on Nov. 15th. By the time the storm cycle was over with, the Lookout Pass ski resort had reported 21 of total snowfall. Visibility was reduced with slick road conditions reported through much of the weekend. Power outages were reported at Lookout Pass during the morning of Nov. 16th, but the reasoning was not reported.

Highway 471 and Thompson Pass were closed for a time on Nov. 16th due to hazardous travel conditions and the Sanders County sheriff office advised people not to travel.  Numerous vehicle slide-offs were reported on I-90 due to snow and ice during the morning of Nov. 16th. The COOP observer located 2 mi. northwest of Heron reported 7.4 of snow with 0.94 of precipitation on Nov. 16th. Also the COOP observer located 1 mi. west of Haugan measured a total of 12 of total snow with 1.20 of precipitation between Nov. 16 and Nov. 18. A NWS employee driving on I-90 east of St. Regis at 6:49 pm MST on Nov. 16th reported less than 100 ft. visibility with heavy snow.

The COOP observer located in Olney reported 8 of total snowfall from Nov. 16 through Nov. 18. A person from the public reported that the falling snow on Nov. 16, was very heavy and dense with difficult driving conditions in the Olney area. The Hand Creek SNOTEL at 5,035 ft., located 20 miles southwest of Olney reported 16 of snowfall and 1.50 of precipitation from Nov 15-17. This sensor also reported periods of heavy snow during the morning and afternoon hours on the 16th.

The Seeley Lake ranger station COOP reported 10 of total storm snowfall from Nov. 16th through Nov 17. The Kraft Creek SNOTEL located 7.5 mi. southwest of Condon reported 16 of snow with 1.30 of precipitation from 5 pm MST Nov. 15 through 9 am MST Nov. 17. A weather spotter reported 11.5 of total storm snowfall with 8 of that falling on the evening of the 15th through the morning of the 16th.

The Lolo Pass SNOTEL located at 5,240 ft., reported a total of 19 of snow between Nov. 15-17. It reported 9 of heavy snow between 2 and 10 am MST on Nov. 16 and also from 5 to 7 am on Nov. 17. The ITD road sensor at Lolo Pass reported slick conditions for much of the weekend and only improving by Monday Nov. 18th. The Saddle Mountain SNOTEL at 7,900 ft., located one mile west of Lost Trail Pass reported 11 of total snowfall with 0.60 precipitation between Nov. 15-17. Other snowfall totals include: 14 Twelvemile Creek located 13.2 mi. west of Charlos Height at 5,600 ft. and 22 Twin Lakes SNOTEL located 16 mi. west of Charlos Height at 6,400 ft. The Twin Lakes sensor also reported 2.10 of total precipitation during the event.

The Bearmouth MTDOT web cam on Interstate 90 at milepost 145.8 indicated snow-covered road conditions for at least 3 hours during the morning hours on Nov. 16.  The MacDonald Pass road sensor located at milepost 27.9 on US-12 reported periods of snow between Nov. 16-17 with strong gusty winds to 35 mph. Web cams at MacDonald Pass indicated periods of blowing snow with limited visibility.

The Poorman Creek SNOTEL at 5,100 ft., located 18 miles south-southwest of Libby in the Cabinet Mountains, reported 18 of snowfall from Nov. 15-17. It reported heavy snow from 1 pm to 10 pm MST on Nov. 16 and from 10 am to 1 pm MST on Nov. 17. This  created dangerous conditions for hunters out in the higher terrain.

The Elk Butte SNOTEL at 5,690 ft., located 4.9 miles northeast of Elk River(elevation 2,856 ft.) reported 19 of snow with 2.50 of precipitation. It reported heavy snow from 5 pm on Nov. 15 through 2 am PST Nov. 16, and also from 3 to 5 am PST on Nov. 16. The heavy snow presented dangerous conditions in the higher elevations posing a threat to hunters and other back-country recreation.

A person from the public reported that 6 of heavy wet snow fell from the evening of Nov. 15 through 10:45 am PST Nov. 16. They reported that the heavy snow created difficult driving conditions. The Pierce RS SNOTEL at 3,080 ft., located 9.2 miles west of Pierce, measured 3 snow and 1.40 of precipitation from Nov. 15-17. The Shanghi Summit at 4,570 ft., located 3.5 mi. west-northwest of Cardiff reported 16 of snow with 2.40 of precipitation.

The Hemlock Butte SNOTEL at 5,810 ft., located 8.1 miles east-southeast of Pierce reported a storm total snowfall of 23 with 2.50 of precipitation. Other totals include: 21 snow with 2.40 of precipitation at the Crater Meadows SNOTEL (5,960 ft.) and 22 snow with 2.50 of precipitation at the Cool Creek SNOTEL(6,280 ft.). The heavy snowfall in the mountains created dangerous conditions for hunters driving forest service roads during this event.

The Dixie COOP observer at 5,740 ft. reported 15.3 of snow with 0.98 of precipitation between Nov. 15-18. A person from the public near Lowell reported that wet snow fell on back-country roads making travel miserable for hunters. The Mountain Meadows SNOTEL at 6,360 ft., located 13.2 miles southeast of Elk City reported 6 of snow with 0.50 of precipitation. The Savage Pass SNOTEL at 6,170 ft. located 5 miles southeast of Powell measured 16 of snow with 1.20 of precipitation. The web cam at Elk City showed snow on state highway 14 during the morning hours on Nov. 16.

The Idaho Transportation Department highway sensor located at 3,112 ft. at the top of Greer Grade, reported wet snow that fell between Nov. 15-16. A person from the public in Weippe reported 1.5 of snowfall at 9:12 am PST on Nov. 16.

events.cz_name: LOWER HELLS CANYON / SALMON RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: The Idaho Transportation Department highway sensor at Whitebird Hill at 4,222 ft. on US-95 reported snowfall between 5 pm PST Nov. 15 through 5:45 am PST on Nov 16 and from 11:45 pm on Nov. 16 through 8:45 am PST on Nov. 17. The road sensor reported very low grip values which indicated very slick conditions during this storm.

The Idaho Transportation Department sensor at Gilmore Summit reported light snow with slick roads between Nov. 16-17. The Saddle Mountain SNOTEL at 7,900 ft., located one mile west of Lost Trail Pass reported 11 of total snowfall with 0.60 precipitation between Nov. 15-17.
The trained weather spotter one mile south of Condon reported 1/8th of an inch of ice from freezing rain Friday evening, November 29 through Saturday morning, November 30.
A weather spotter in Troy reported freezing rain. They believed that the ice was forming on nearby roads making for slick conditions.

The MTDOT section between Kalispell and Whitefish, reported a layer of glaze that caused road surfaces to be slick during the early morning hours from 4 to 7 am MST on Nov. 29. A weather spotter from Columbia Falls reported freezing drizzle during the morning of Nov. 29 precipitating out of fog.  This spotter overheard multiple reports of vehicles spinning out due to the slick roads. A weather spotter located just west of Kalispell reported that mist developed during the early morning hours of Nov. 29 that caused sidewalks to become slick.  Light snow fell from 4 to 6:30 pm MST on Nov. 29 in the Kalispell area. The Flathead County 911 dispatch indicated that the combination of snow on top of icy conditions caused a few accidents and slide-offs. The Lake County 911 dispatch reported icy roads at Terrace Lake in the Ronan area at 9 am MST on Nov. 30. A spotter 8 mi. northwest of St. Ignatius reported freezing rain that caused the sidewalks to become icy during the late morning hours of Nov. 30. At 11:01 pm MST on Nov. 30, a spotter located in Columbia Falls tweeted that roads were solid sheets of ice due to freezing rain and were treacherous. They reportedly drove down East Tamarack Hill sideways.

The MTDOT reported freezing rain at Lookout Pass on Interstate 90 at 2:25 am MST on Nov. 30. The Mineral County sheriff office in Superior reported freezing rain, slick conditions on I-90 and multiple reports of accidents.

Periods of moderate snow fell at both Lolo and Lost Trail Passes especially associated with the warm front precipitation during the morning of Feb. 14th. Snow and rain bands had developed by the afternoon which brought brief periods of limited visibility. A rock slide occurred on Skalkaho highway 38 at mile-marker 7 around 5:53 pm MST blocking both lanes. It was subsequently cleared by 7 pm MST. The Lost Trail ski resort reported 8 of new snow 24 hours ending at 5:58 am MST Feb. 15. The Lolo Pass SNOTEL reported 4 of total snowfall.

A moist and strong warm front brought a relatively brief period of heavy snow to Lookout Pass on I-90 from 9 am to 12 pm on Feb. 14. This impacted travelers with low visibilities and slick, snow-covered roads. Throughout the day there were periods of snow and rain from bands that brought limited impacts. Two separate jack-knifed trucks were reported due to slick road conditions Friday evening, one at mile-marker 3 at 7:52 pm MST and another at mile-marker 24.5 at 4:54 pm MST.  By nightfall the skies cleared out and temperatures fell into the 20's helping to develop black ice. Another tractor trailer jack-knifed on the west bound lane at mile-marker 58 or 4.3 miles  north-northwest of Tarkio on I-90 at 1:15 am MST on Feb. 15. This incident blocked blocked both lanes until 2:36 am MST and was finally cleared by 3:22 am MST.

Snow began in the Kalispell area by 9:45 am MST on Feb. 14 and ended a little after 1 pm MST. The Glacier Park International Airport reported a period of heavy snow with 1 falling in a ten minute period ending 10:23 am MST. This sudden change brought very low visibilities and snow-covered roads to much of the Flathead Valley. The Flathead County 911 dispatch reported 6 motor vehicle accidents between 10 and 11 am MST with a few of those being slide-offs. MTDOT reported snow-covered roads through the afternoon hours from Yellow Bay to Creston on Highway 35 and on Highway 206 north to Columbia Falls. Snowfall amounts include: 1.4 at Glacier Park Int. Airport, 3 Columbia Falls and 1 near Blue Bay on the east side of Flathead Lake.
The ITD webcam and weather sensor at Greer Grade on highway 11 reported snow that covered the road for at 3 hours causing slick conditions.

The ITD sensors and webcams indicated snow that fell on US-12 near Kamiah, on US-95 from Ferdinand to Grangeville between 4:30 and 8:30 am PST. This caused road conditions to become slick impacting morning rush hour travel.

events.cz_name: LOWER HELLS CANYON / SALMON RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: The ITD sensor and webcams at Whitebird Grade on US-95 reported snow that made slick conditions on the morning of Feb. 14th.

A spotter in Salmon reported 2 of wet snow with the storm. They reported that US-93 became slick in spots between Salmon and Lost Trail Pass. The slush on the roads froze overnight and caused slick conditions. The Lemhi County dispatch reported at least one slide-off early Saturday morning Feb. 15. Another slide-off occurred 16 miles south of Salmon late Saturday morning in which a car went into the Salmon River, but its occupants escaped unharmed.

Slush and snow-covered roads were reported across much of Lincoln County during the morning into the afternoon hours on Feb. 14. A person from the public located in Olney reported 2 of heavy snow two hours ending at 10:49 MST. Whitefish Mountain Ski Resort reported a total of 3 at their base elevation 4,464 ft. 24 hours ending 5:50 am MST on Feb. 15.

Freezing rain was reported in Troy and along Highway 37 during the morning hours making untreated road surfaces slick. SNOTEL stations in the mountains reported anywhere from 5 to 12 inches of wet snow.
SNOTEL sites in the Swan, Whitefish and Mission mountains reported 8 to 10 inches of snow with over an inch of liquid equivalent.

A person from Columbia Falls tweeted that roads were icy and treacherous due to freezing rain at 12 am MST. Montana DOT reported freezing rain on MT-40 from US-93 to the junction of US-2 and also on S-424 between Lodgepole Road to the junction with US-93.

The Superior 911 dispatch reported freezing rain that brought a glaze of ice to the nearby roads from 9 am to 1 pm MST. Montana DOT reported freezing rain on Interstate 90 between St. Regis to Tarkio during the morning. Snow fell at Lookout Pass during the morning hours with up to 4 inches of wet snow reported. Web-cams indicated that the pass had snow-covered and slick road during the morning. The Hoodoo Basin SNOTEL at 6,050 ft., located 14 miles west-southwest of Tarkio, reported 13 inches of total snow with 1.70 inches of snow water equivalent.

The Saddle Mountain SNOTEL at 7,900 ft., located about 1.7 miles west-southwest of Lost Trail Pass on US-93 received 15 inches of snow with 1.80 inches of snow water equivalent. An intense period of heavy snow occurred between 4 and 8 pm MST when 9 inches fell. At 1:40 pm MST, the Montana DOT reported that chains were required on towing units for Lost Trail Pass. During the morning hours, freezing rain was reported near Sula on US-93 causing very slick conditions. Several vehicles had slid off the road from Sula towards Lost Trail Pass.

A railroad weather sensor at 4,520 ft., located 6.4 miles southwest of Marias Pass, measured 2 per hour snowfall rates between 6 and 8 am MST on Dec. 2. It also depicted a distinct wind shift with falling temperatures between 9 and 10 am MST, associated with an arctic cold front passage. It measured a total storm snowfall of 5.5 inches. A person from the public located in Essex, estimated that 12 inches of total snow fell during this event. They also reported that 6 inches of that fell as heavy snow with and behind the arctic front passage near 9:30 am MST. At 1 pm MST, the MT DOT reported that chains were required on towing units on US-2 from Essex to 7 miles west of Marias Pass.

A trained spotter located 2 miles west-southwest of Columbia Falls reported visibilities near zero from at least 1 to 3 pm MST due to blowing snow. During this time-frame the Glacier Park International Airport ASOS sensor reported frequent gusts between 32 and 38 mph. Based on this, wind speeds could have been reaching near 50 mph towards the Bad Rock Canyon on US-2. The Flathead County 911 dispatch reported that 15 vehicle slide-offs and accidents occurred during a time span of less than two hours inside and outside of the Kalispell city limits, some of which contained injuries. The Flathead Beacon tweeted at 3:31 pm MST, Terrible driving conditions currently-please drive with caution. Even though snowfall amounts were low and near 2 inches, the sudden change from dry roads to near whiteout conditions with dropping temperatures caused high impact to the Flathead Valley.

The Ronan Airport AWOS sensor reported northerly winds to 31 mph with the arctic front passage. Heavy snow, blowing snow reducing visibility, and slick conditions on US-93 from Ronan to Polson were reported by MT DOT at 6:50 pm MST. At 8:22 pm MST, MT DOT reported heavy snow with snow-covered roads from MT-200 west of Dixon to Ravalli and on Highway-212, 4 miles north of Dixon to Moise. Total snowfall ranged from 2 to 4 inches.
Rain fell during the early morning hours freezing to untreated secondary roads making for slippery travel in the Missoula and Bitterroot Valleys.

The arctic front passed through Missoula a little after 8 pm MST and brought 0.5 of snow, blowing snow with a few northerly wind gusts over 30 mph through 10 pm MST on Dec. 2. Visibilities fell down close to zero briefly with the combination of falling snow and blowing snow.  A person from the public reported strong winds, blowing snow and whiteout conditions on US-93 between Missoula and Lolo around 11:36 pm MST on Dec. 2. Half an inch of snow fell at the Missoula Airport, 1  to 2 fell in Lolo and 3 fell in the Grant Creek area 4 miles north-northwest of Missoula.

The Montana DOT reported heavy snow with snow-covered roads on MT-200 from Trout Creek to west of Plains at 6:18 pm MST on Dec. 2. By 7 pm MST, they reported heavy snow on MT-28 junction with MT-200 to 10 miles north. The MT DOT also reported heavy snow on US-93 at Evaro Hill. Rain had fallen earlier in the day on the 2nd and when the arctic front went through by 6 pm MST at Trout Creek, snow froze quickly to the road making for very slick conditions.  On Dec. 3, the MT DOT indicated that from 5:23 am to 7:11 am MST, there were severe driving conditions on MT-200 from Trout Creek to just west of Plains due to snow-pack and black ice.

The Saddle Mountain SNOTEL at 7,900 ft., located about 1.7 miles west-southwest of Lost Trail Pass on US-93 received 27 inches of total storm snow with 3.50 inches of snow water equivalent. An intense, 4 hour period of heavy snow amounting to 9 inches fell between 4 and 8 pm MST on Dec. 1. At 1:40 pm MST Dec. 1, the Montana DOT reported that chains were required on towing units for Lost Trail Pass. The heaviest snowfall, according to the SNOTEL, appeared to have stopped by 2 pm MST on Dec. 2.

A person from the public in Olney reported heavy snow with blowing snow creating whiteout conditions on US-93 near mile-marker 145. Although snow totals ranged between 2 to 3 inches across the area, this all fell within 2 to 3 hours ahead and with the arctic cold front passage. It was this sudden change with falling temperatures from above freezing to the teens, that caused roads to become very slick with several automobile slide-offs reported by the Flathead County dispatch between Olney and Whitefish. The Eureka Airport AWOS reported visibilities less than or equal to one-quarter mile from 11:56 am to 1:46 pm MST while the City of Eureka webcam indicated falling snow.

With arctic air entrenched over western Montana, convergent winds developed over a relatively warm Flathead Lake, allowing for lake effect snow (LES) to develop. Lake temperatures ranged from 32 to 36 degrees Fahrenheit during this event. Depending on where the convergent boundary set up, locations would receive anywhere from a dusting up to 10 inches of snow. During the morning of Dec. 5, a very intense west to east oriented LES band, 1 to 2 miles wide, formed north of Yellow Bay. An estimated 8 to 10 inches fell 1 mile south of Wood's Bay along Hwy-35, especially between mile-marker 18 and 22. An interesting note during this heavy snowfall is that the consistency of the snowflakes were observed to be large dendrites. As a secondary push of colder air moved in later on Dec. 5, the LES band shifted further south and light snow was reported between MM-3 and 5 on Hwy-35 just south of Finley Point. As indicated correctly by the high resolution WRF-ARW model forecast, the LES band became more north to south oriented. It brought up to 3 inches of snow from Polson to Big Arm between MM 57-69 on US-93 through 8:37 am MST on Dec. 6. The LES band continued to affect the Polson area through Dec. 7, bringing less than one inch of snow, which made roads slick. The Polson sheriff reported 2 accidents due to slick conditions at 12:51 pm on Dec. 7. They indicated that the snow was coming down as very fine grains and air temperatures ranged from 0 to -10 F. By the evening of Dec. 7, the LES band had shifted further to the east affecting the east and southeast side of Flathead Lake. A weather spotter located 8 miles north of Finley Point, measured 1 inch of snow between 6 and 6:30 pm MST on Dec. 7. An estimated 8 inches of heavy snow was reported near mile-markers 80-100 on US-93 near Rollins at 5 pm MST on Dec. 8. An estimated 8 inches of snow was reported by MT DOT, 2 miles north of Bigfork at 6:30 pm MST on Dec. 8.

The Georgetown Lake MT DOT sensor reported wind chill values between -20 and -31 F. The coldest air temperature reported was -22 F at 12:25 am MST on Dec. 8. The MT DOT sensor located 7 miles north-northwest of Avon on MT-141, reported wind chill values between -20 to -45 F from Dec. 3-9. The -45 F wind chill occurred at 1:59 am MST on Dec. 7, with a wind speed of 11 mph and air temperature was -22.7 F. The Bert Mooney Airport ASOS recorded its coldest wind chill of -35 F at 1:53 am MST on Dec. 7.

The Fielding RAWS, located 4.4 miles southwest of Marias Pass, reported air temperatures between -20 and -28 F during the mornings and evenings from 3:42 am MST on Dec. 6, through 2:42 am MST on Dec. 8. The HADS sensor at Marias Pass also measured very cold air temperatures: -27.5 F at 3 am MST Dec. 5, -30.9 F at 7:30 am MST Dec. 6, and -41.2 F at 7:45 am MST Dec. 7. A person from the public located 8 miles southwest of Marias Pass, reported frozen pipes on Dec. 6.

The Essex MT DOT sensor reported wind chill values between -20 and -33 F, with an average wind speed of 9 mph through 11:22 am MST Dec.5.  The peak wind during that time was 17 mph.  It also measured -20 to -32 F wind chill values from 9:16 pm MST Thursday Dec. 5 through 11:31 am MST Friday Dec. 6, with an average wind speed of 7 mph.  The peak wind was 18 mph.  It also reported -20 to -49 F wind chill values from 3:16 pm MST Dec. 6 through 12:20 pm MST Dec. 7, with an average wind speed of 10 mph.  The -49 F wind chill occurred at 7:58 am MST on Dec. 7 with a wind speed of 19 mph. It reported air temperatures between -20 and -22 F from 8:13 pm MST Dec. 7 through 2:16 am MST Dec. 8. The prevailing wind direction throughout this event was from the southeast.

The Pistol Creek RAWS at 6,043 ft., reported wind chill values between -20 and -39 F while wind speeds averaged around 7 mph. It measured the -39 F reading at 12:41 am MST on Dec. 7 with a speed of 11 mph. The Greenough Hill MT DOT sensor measured air temperatures from -20 to -22 F between 5 am and 9:08 am MST on Dec. 7. It also reported an air temperature of -20 F between 11:08 pm Dec. 7 and 2:32 am MST on Dec. 8. The Snowbowl ski resort cancelled their opening day, Friday, Dec. 6, and also Saturday, Dec. 7, due to the extreme cold.

The Mullan Pass sensor reported -20 to -34 wind chill values with an average wind speed of 8 mph. The -34 F value was observed at 6:53 MST on Dec. 7 when the air temperature was -13 F and the wind speed was 12.7 mph.

The Stillwater RAWS at 3,116 ft., located 1.1 mile southeast of Olney, reported air temperatures between -20 and -31 F mainly during the late evening and morning hours during this time period. The coldest value of -31 F occurred at 8 am MST on Dec. 7, which happens to be the same temperature recorded by the Olney COOP, and was a record minimum for the day. The Boorman RAWS at 3,963 ft., located 3 miles northwest of Marion reported air temperatures between -20 and -25 F between Dec. 6-8.

The Glacier Park International Airport ASOS reported wind chill values between -20 and -30 F, while north-northeast winds averaged around 15 mph. Both the City of Columbia Falls and Polson cancelled their Parade of Lights Dec. 6 due to the cold. The Bigfork Area Chamber of Commerce cancelled the Annual Magical Holiday Parade that was planned to occur on Dec. 7.

The Missoula International Airport reported wind chill values between -20 and -28 F with an average wind speed of 16 mph. During the morning of Dec. 7, the wind chill values could have ranged between -30 and -35 F across eastern Missoula, especially by Hellgate Canyon where wind speeds were a little stronger than by the airport. Thousands of people attended a championship football game at the University of Montana football stadium, while wind chill values possibly fluctuated between -15 and -20 F at times during the early afternoon on Dec. 7.

The Saddle Mountain SNOTEL at 7,900 ft. located about 1.7 miles west-southwest of Lost Trail Pass on US-93 received 27 inches of total storm snow with 3.50 inches of snow water equivalent. An intense, 4 hour period of heavy snow amounting to 9 inches fell between 4 and 8 pm MST on Dec. 1. At 1:40 pm MST Dec. 1, the Montana DOT reported that chains were required on towing units for Lost Trail Pass. The heaviest snowfall, according to the SNOTEL, appeared to have stopped by 2 pm MST on Dec. 2, but periods of light to moderate snow continued through the morning hours of Dec. 3.

An arctic cold front pushed through MacDonald Pass in the morning and brought periods of heavy snow and blowing snow reducing visibilities to near whiteout at times. The Deer Lodge AWOS reported visibilities less than one-quarter mile for 1.4 hours, while northerly winds gusting to 37 mph occurred as the arctic cold front passed through. A weather spotter at 6,200 ft., 2 miles southwest of Newcomb,  measured 5.5 inches of heavy snow, 5 hours ending at 3:50 pm MST. They also reported that 6 to 10 inches of snow fell across the higher elevations.

A trained weather spotter, located 1.5 miles south of Condon, reported 1.5 of snow. Both the North Fork Jocko SNOTEL at 6,330 ft. and Kraft Creek SNOTEL at 4,750 ft. measured 2 of total snowfall. Falling temperatures from the middle 30s to upper teens in the Condon area combined with the snowfall brought slick conditions on MT-83.

The Crater Meadows SNOTEL at 5,960 ft., located 24.8 miles east-northeast of Pierce, reported 17 of total storm snowfall with 4.10 of snow water equivalent. It reported heavy snow between 4 am through 9 am PST on Dec. 1 and also from 1 to 3 pm PST on Dec. 1.

The Lolo Pass SNOTEL, located 0.4 miles south of Lolo Pass at 5,240 ft., reported heavy wet snow from 4 am to 8 am PST and from 8 pm to 11 pm on Dec 1 with temperatures averaging around 34 deg. F. It also reported heavy snow from 8 to 11 am PST on Dec 2. The total storm snowfall accumulation was 16 with a snow water equivalent of 2.40. The Dixie COOP located at 5,740 ft., reported 11.8 of snow with 2.36 of liquid equivalent from Dec. 1-3. A person from Dixie reported several power brief power outages when the snow was the heaviest on Dec. 2. This heavy mountain snowfall event could have posed extreme danger to mountain lion hunters driving on forest service roads in the back-country.

A trained weather spotter, located 3 miles northeast of Orofino, measured 3.5 of snow that fell with the arctic cold front passage around 2 am PST. They reported that the roads were icy especially in shaded spots during the day on Dec 3.
The ITD sensor at Elk City reported 3.2 of snow during the day on December 3.

events.cz_name: LOWER HELLS CANYON / SALMON RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: The Whitebird Hill ITD sensor at 4,222 ft. on US-95, reported light snow that brought slick conditions during this period. It reported a very low grip level during this period which equates to very slick conditions.

The ITD sensor at Lost Trail Pass on US-93, recorded wind chill values between -20 and -26 F, with wind speeds ranging between 5 and 12 mph. The -26 F value occurred on Dec. 7 at 1:16 pm MST with a wind speed of 10 mph, and also on Dec. 8 at 5:46 am MST with a wind speed of 5 to 7 mph. The Lost Trail Ski Area closed down due to the cold on Dec. 8. The Leadore COOP station observed a low temperature of -29 F on both Dec. 5 and Dec. 6.  The value on Dec. 5 was the 2nd coldest minimum temperature for that day while back in 1972, the record was -38 F. The value on Dec. 6 was the coldest minimum for that day while 1972 was -15 F.

The Pike Creek SNOTEL located near Marias Pass reported a storm total snowfall of 15 while a mesonet sensor located 6 mi. southwest of the pass measured 12 of snow. The Essex web cam reported snow with periods of low visibility while the Montana DOT road reports stated that US-2 between Essex and Marias Pass experienced blowing snow and reduced visibility on the morning of the 16th. On November 16, an arctic cold front moved west through Marias Pass between 12:45 pm and 1:15 pm and through Essex between 2:46 pm and 3:46 pm MST. This front brought gusty winds between 20 and 30 mph for several hours, causing impacts of reduced visibility, snow and blowing snow to travel along the US-2 corridor.

As a NWS employee drove north on US-93 on Nov. 27, they encountered dense freezing fog with visibilities less than one quarter mile from the animal's bridge north for 5 miles and also from Ronan north to Pablo. In Ronan they interviewed a salesman at the Chevrolet dealer, who reported that a light dusting of snow fell when the fog moved in from the north earlier in the morning.  In Pablo, they reported light freezing drizzle creating a glaze on untreated surfaces near the People's Center museum. The Ronan Airport AWOS sensor, located 2.6 miles north of Ronan, reported visibility at or below one-half mile from the late evening of Nov. 26 through the afternoon on Nov. 27. The one-quarter mile visibility was observed from 8:55 am MST through 2:35 pm MST on Nov. 27.

A person from the public in Olney tweeted that they received 11 of fluffy snow as of 11:59 am MST on Dec. 10.  At 6:40 pm MST, they commented that US-93 near mile-marker 145 was plowed but slick with ice and snow. Other storm snowfall amounts COOP stations include: 1.9 Yaak 9 NNE, 1.8 Libby 30 SSE, 2.5 Libby 1 NE, and 2.5 at the Eureka Ranger Station. The common 24 hour snow to liquid ratios, as observed by these COOP stations, ranged between 20 and 30 to one.

The West Glacier Cooperative observer measured a storm total of 5.2 of snow with 0.22  liquid equivalent during this storm and temperatures ranged from the teens to lower 20's. The Hungry Horse Dam COOP reported 6.0 of total storm snowfall with 0.31 of liquid equivalent.

The Flathead and Mission Valleys saw the highest amount of snowfall in all of western Montana with this storm. Glacier Park International Airport reported a storm total snowfall of 10 with 0.41 liquid equivalent, while the ASOS reported mainly light snow intensities throughout the storm. A head-on automobile accident occurred near Moiese and the National Bison Range on MT Hwy-212 around 11 am MST on Dec 9. A 60 year old woman died as she lost control of her vehicle, and slid into the westbound lane striking an oncoming pickup truck injuring two people. Law enforcement reported that roads were icy at the time of the accident. A 5 vehicle accident occurred on US-93 near the Ninepipes Wildlife Refuge on Dec. 10. Law enforcement blamed the driver of a small U-Haul truck, for not stopping in time and rear-ending three other vehicles. Minor injuries were reported while road conditions were snow-covered and slick at the time of the accident. Several schools closed due to the weather on Dec. 10, including Salish Kootenai College located in Pablo, Polson, and Charlo schools. Two bus routes in the Ronan school district were canceled although schools stayed open. Other total snowfall amounts include: 13 Lake Blaine, 11.5 Polson Kerr DAM COOP, 11 4 SW Fort Connah, St. Ignatius, Creston and Columbia Falls, 10 Whitefish, and 8 at COOP station 13 S Bigfork.

A cooperative observer located one mile west of Haugan, measured a storm total snowfall of 9 with 0.30 of liquid equivalent. The Superior COOP didn't report snow, but did report a liquid equivalent of 0.42, which could have equated to near a foot of snow, using a 30 to 1 snow to liquid ratio. The St. Regis schools closed on Dec. 10 due to the weather. Other snowfall reports include: 10 Thompson Falls, 7 Belknap 2 WNW, 6.4 in Alberton, and 6 Evaro.

The official Missoula International Airport storm total snowfall measured was 5.8 with 0.19 of liquid during this storm. The snow fell lightly on Dec. 9 and wreaked havoc on area roads causing multiple accidents due to slick conditions. At 11:37 am on Dec. 9, a 2 car crash on US-93 south of Florence left a woman and teenage boy with serious injuries. US-93 was shut down for several hours and authorities said that conditions were very slick at the time when the first car went out of control. At 1:54 pm MST on Dec. 9, a SUV rolled over in the flats, just north of Lolo on US-93, causing 2 people to be injured. Law enforcement indicated that the road was snow covered and icy at the time.

The Seeley Lake RS COOP reported a three day storm total snowfall of 6.9 with 0.32 of liquid equivalent. The Kraft Creek SNOTEL, located 8 miles SSW of Condon measured 13 of snow by 7 am MST on Dec. 10.  There were multiple accidents and slide-offs reported during the storm. There was an injury reported with a crash that happened at 3:43 pm MST on Dec. 9, at the cross streets of MT-200 and Potomac Rd. Road conditions were snow-covered and icy at the time of the crash.

The Lolo Pass SNOTEL at 5,240 ft., reported a two day storm total snowfall of 12 with 0.50 of liquid equivalent. Temperatures started out at -1.5 deg. F and rose to 21 deg. by the end of the snowfall. The COOP located 14 miles northeast of Sula, reported 6.1 of snow with 0.23 of liquid equivalent.

The Pierce COOP measured a total storm snowfall of 4.8 with 0.10 of liquid equivalent. The Dworshak Fish Hatchery measured 3.5 of snow with 0.12 of liquid. Temperatures started off in the negative single digits and rose to near 20 degrees by the end of the event.
The Dixie COOP measured a total storm snowfall of 3.0 with 0.17 of liquid. The Fenn Ranger Station COOP reported 3 of snowfall. The Lolo Pass SNOTEL measured 12 of snow with 0.50 of liquid.

A trained spotter located 3 miles northeast of Orofino, measured 6.0 of total storm snowfall. Four inches of that fell on Monday, Dec. 9. The Grangeville COOP reported 1 of snow with 0.09 of liquid on Dec. 9.

MT DOT estimated that 8 to 10 inches of snow fell from West Glacier to Java East, which is located about 6 miles southwest of Marias Pass. They also reported that there was blowing and drifting snow, snow-pack and ice on US-2. They also indicated that the area south of Essex to Java East was particularly nasty. The Pike Creek SNOTEL at 5,930 ft., located about 1.6 miles southeast of Marias Pass, reported 6 of total snow with 0.20 of snow water equivalent, which gives an average snow to liquid ratio of 30 to 1. The HADS sensor at Marias Pass, reported 0.29 of liquid, which could equate to around 7.1 of snow, 6 of that fell between 4:45 and 7:45 pm MST on Dec. 18. The MT DOT sensor located at milepost 179.9 in Essex, reported gusty winds near 30 mph from 4 to 7:30 pm MST on Dec. 18, which corroborates the report of nasty conditions on US-2. An automobile accident with an injury was reported near West glacier at 4:24 pm MST on Dec. 18, while roads were reported to have snow-cover with slick conditions. Blowing snow with wind gusts near 50 mph were reported near Bad Rock canyon on the evening of Dec. 18. Other snow/liquid amounts: 7.0/0.20 Flattop Mtn. SNOTEL, 7.0/0.40 Emery Creek SNOTEL(5 SSE of West Glacier) & 4.4/0.41 West Glacier COOP.

A spotter located in Columbia Falls, reported 3 of total snowfall, flash-freezing to formerly wet road surfaces, and blowing snow with occasional strong gusts between 30 and 50 mph. They reported that visibility lowered to less than one-quarter mile at times due to blowing snow during the evening of Dec. 18. They also said that the drive from Whitefish to Columbia Falls around 11:30 pm MST on Dec. 18, was very slick due to ice, blowing and drifting snow. The arctic cold front made it through Glacier Park International Airport around 8:22 pm MST Dec. 18 and north-northeast winds were sustained between 30-33 mph with gusts up to 45 mph through 2:35 am MST Dec. 19. The airport only reported 1 of snow, and visibilities were only reduced to one-half mile between 11:24 and 11:55 pm MST Dec. 18. Five automobile crashes and 7 slide-offs were reported in the Flathead Valley on Dec. 18.

A trained spotter 7 miles south of Butte at 6,200 ft., reported a total storm snowfall of 3 inches that mainly fell after midnight on Dec. 19. A weather observer at the Bert Mooney Airport also reported an estimated 3 of snowfall during the event. The temperatures ranged from the single digits below zero to the teens in the Butte area through Dec. 20, which prevented the DOT to be able to mitigate the slick roads. Wind chill values ranged between 10 and 16 below zero F. from Avon to Deer Lodge from 4:30 to 10:21 am MST on Dec. 19. A trained spotter located near Georgetown Lake reported 4 of total storm snowfall.

The Olney COOP reported a total storm snowfall of 5 with 0.38 of precipitation for Dec. 19. A person from the public in Olney, tweeted that road conditions were snow-covered and snow intensities were heavy at 3:50 pm MST on Dec. 18.
The Lost Trail ski resort reported 3 of snow while Ski Lookout reported 2 of snow during this event.

Heavy snow was reported by MT DOT for I-90, especially from Alberton to Frenchtown and snow plows could barely keep up. The MT DOT also reported that US-93 at Evaro Hill experienced heavy snow for several hours during the afternoon and evening of Dec. 20. A weather spotter located in Alberton reported that conditions were severe on I-90, especially in the passing lane at 8:30 MST on Dec. 20. Snowfall amounts: 8 Evaro Hill, 6.7 Huson, 6.3 Frenchtown, and 5 lower Evaro Hill.

Snowfall was not as heavy in terms of sensible weather during this event, but because the timing occurred during high volume traffic, it became a high impact event. Steady snowfall continued during rush hour traffic on a weekend preceding the holidays, and this caused more people on the roads traveling to holiday parties etc. At 6:31 pm MST, the Missoula Sheriff's office issued an emergency alert asking people to stay off the roads, so that snow plows could efficiently mitigate poor road conditions. Several accidents were reported in the City of Missoula and along US-93 south to Victor.  In the immediate Missoula Valley, snowfall amounts ranged from 4.7 at the Missoula International Airport to 6 on the South Hills of Missoula. In the Bitterroot Valley from Lolo to Stevensville, snowfall amounts ranged from 6 to 8.

Two different accidents involving multiple vehicles occurred on I-90 near Turah and also east of Clinton. The accident near Turah closed both lanes near 6:15 pm MST on Dec. 20. Road conditions at the time of the accidents were moderate to heavy snowfall, snow-covered and icy. Several accidents were also reported on Highway 83 from Seeley Lake to Condon. Snowfall reports: 8 Potomac, 7 Condon, 5 in Bonner and 2 in Seeley Lake.
A person from the public in Eureka reported 5 of total snowfall with this event. A person from 5 miles north of Fortine measured 4.5 of total snowfall.

The Glacier Park International Airport reported 5.4 of snow with 0.21 of liquid equivalent. A weather spotter in Columbia Falls tweeted that the powdery snow had fallen over icy roads, which made for slick driving at 12:26 pm MST and at 4:07 pm MST. This spotter measured a total of 8 of snow at 11:30 pm MST and reported that secondary roads had deep snow. Someone from Kalispell tweeted at 2:50 pm MST that the roads in Kalispell were nasty and suggested that people stay home. At 10:30 pm, a weather spotter located 2 miles NNW of Kalispell reported 8.3 of snow. The MT road incidents reported 10 automobile crashes with no injuries, 3 crashes with injuries and 8 slide-offs in the Flathead and Mission Valleys on Dec. 20.

The Idaho County highway reported white-out conditions from Whitebird Grade to Grangeville and from Grangeville to Cottonwood due to blowing snow and snow. They also reported that they received over 30 automobile accident calls. Southerly winds between 20 to 25 mph developed around 2:45 pm PST across the Camas Prairie, as observed by an ITD road sensor located 3.8 miles south-southeast of Cottonwood. The sensors at the Grangeville Idaho County Airport, reported southerly winds sustained between 25-30 mph with gusts to 41 mph between 6:24 pm and 9:44 pm PST. Weather spotters reported 2 per hour snowfall rates in Woodland and in Kamiah around 3:55 pm PST. Other snowfall amounts: 6.5 E Kooskia, 6 1 mi. ENE Woodland, and 4.5 3 mi. NE Orofino.

A trained spotter in Elk City measured 8.5 of snow that mainly fell during the afternoon and evening on Dec. 20. The Lowell ASOS reported around 0.10 of precipitation each hour from 4 to 8 pm PST which could equate to over 1 per hour snowfall rates, and temperatures ranged between 29-30 deg. F during the event. It recorded a total precipitation amount of 0.69 which could be converted to around 8 of snowfall. Other snowfall amounts: 12.4 Dixie COOP, 9 Mountain Meadows SNOTEL, and 8 2 miles north of Elk City.
The COOP observer located in Pierce, measured 5.0 of total snowfall with 0.62 of liquid equivalent during the storm. Other snowfall amounts include: 6 Elk Butte SNOTEL and 4 Shanghi Summit SNOTEL.

events.cz_name: LOWER HELLS CANYON / SALMON RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: The ITD road sensor at Whitebird Hill on US-95 reported 0.25 of precipitation which could equate to around 3 of snowfall.  It reported visibilities below one-half mile at times between 1:46 and 11:16 pm PST, and web-cams indicated blowing snow and snow. The winds were southerly between 10 and 20 mph during the event.
A trained spotter located 1 mile east-southeast of Salmon estimated 5.5 of snowfall. The Saddle Mountain SNOTEL recorded 4 of snowfall with 0.50 of snow water equivalent during the storm.
The Lolo Pass SNOTEL measured 6 of snow with 0.50 of snow water equivalent with this storm. The COOP located at Lolo Hot Springs measured 2 of snow with 0.12 of precipitation.

The COOP observer in Olney reported 4 of snow with 0.39 of precipitation. Freezing rain was reported in the Libby area during the morning of Jan. 3, causing slick and slushy roads. Behind the cold front, precipitation changed to moderate and heavy snow for a period between Whitefish and Olney during the afternoon on Jan. 3. Other snow amounts: 6.0 Hand Creek SNOTEL (20 mi. SW of Olney at 5,035 ft.).

The Shed 4 weather sensor located 6.4 miles southwest of Marias Pass near US-2 at 4,520 ft., reported heavy snow and 1-2.6 per hour snowfall rates during the afternoon on Jan. 3. It measured a storm total of 9.0 with 0.51 snow water equivalent. Other totals include: 16 at the summit(6,817 ft.) of Whitefish Ski Resort, 9 of snow in Essex, 7.8 of snow (1.18 precipitation) West Glacier COOP and 5 snow (0.46 precipitation) Whitefish COOP.
Moderate to heavy snow bands brought 1 to 2 inches of snow from Clinton north to Seeley Lake. The MT DOT reported snow and ice on I-90 east of Missoula to 15 miles west of Drummond.

The Pacific cold front moved through in the morning of Jan. 3. Snow showers with the front brought gusty winds to 35 mph and reduced visibility to the Missoula Valley from 7:30 to 9 am MST. A NWS employee reported that roads were very icy north of Mullan Road at 10:20 am MST. Snow bands brought less than an inch of snow to the area in the afternoon.

The Glacier Park International Airport measured 5 of heavy snow in 5 hours 35 minutes during the afternoon and evening of Jan. 3. The Flathead County 911 dispatch at 7:33 pm MST, reported that the roads were icy and 10 automobile slide-offs had occurred that evening. A weather spotter from Columbia Falls tweeted at 9:10 pm MST that the secondary roads had deep snow over ice and had not been plowed yet. Other total snow amounts: 8.4 Columbia Falls and 4 Creston COOP. There was a report of freezing rain in Columbia Falls during the morning of Jan. 3.

Strong gusty winds near 50 mph accompanied a cold front during the morning of Jan. 3, which caused snow and blowing snow at times at MacDonald Pass, Homestake Pass and portions of southwest Montana. The MacDonald Pass sensor reported moderate to heavy snowfall from 5:15 to 7:48 pm MST associated with snow bands in the area. The snow continued at MacDonald through much of the day on Jan. 4 and the MT DOT required towing units to use chains. Snow amounts include: 5.5 Discovery Ski Resort and 4 Georgetown Lake.
Both Lolo Pass on US-12 and Lost Trail pass on US-93 received around 6 of total storm snowfall.

The MT DOT road sensor located at milepost 8.1 on MT-141, reported extreme wind chill values between -20 and -31 deg. F. Wind speeds varied from 10 to 19 mph during the morning of Jan. 5. Other wind chills observed(all in degrees F): -25 Helmville, -25 Garrison Junction, -20 MacDonald Pass and -19 at Bert Mooney Airport ASOS. Along the wind chills a few locations including MacDonald Pass saw snow, blowing and drifting snow at times. Deer Lodge reported snow, blowing snow and wind gusts to 23 mph between midnight and 3 am MST on Jan. 5 as the arctic cold front passed through. The Elliston COOP measured 7 of snow with 0.31 of precipitation between Jan. 4-5.
The MT DOT sensor located at milepost 179.9 on US-2 reported extreme wind chills between -20 and -25 F on the morning of Jan. 5.
The storm total snowfall for Olney was 5 with 0.55 of precipitation. Two inches fell at 32 miles SSE of Libby.

The COOP observer located in West Glacier measured a 3-day storm total snowfall of 10.5 with 0.77 of precipitation. MT DOT reported that US-2 was snow covered with slick conditions throughout this period.

The Glacier Park Airport reported a 4 day storm total snowfall of 4.1 with 0.37 of precipitation. It also reported freezing rain during the early morning of Jan. 9. Other snowfall amounts include: 6 Whitefish, 5.3 Creston, and 3 Polson.
The COOP observer located 1 mile west of Haugan measured 12 of snow with 1.44 of precipitation. Other snowfall amounts include: 16 Lookout Pass Ski Resort and 6.3 Heron 2 mi. NW.

The Missoula International Airport experienced freezing rain between 1:04 am and 3:46 am MST, and from 6 to 8 am MST on Jan. 9. There was a coating of glaze/ice observed on sidewalks and on side roads from Frenchtown south to Florence. On Jan. 10, intense snow bands brought up to 4 of snow to Stevensville.
The COOP observer measured a total snowfall of 6.1 with 0.33 precipitation. Road surfaces from Bonner to Seeley Lake were slick at times through this event.

The Lolo Pass SNOTEL measured 3-day snow total of 15. During the early morning hours of Jan. 10, the MT DOT required chains on towing units on Lolo Pass.  Other snowfall amounts include: 6.8 Sula 14 NE and 4 Lolo Hot Springs.

The COOP observer in Elliston recorded 3 of snow on Jan 10. Interstate 90 experienced slick travel from Bearmouth to Butte at times during this period. Both MacDonald and Homestake Pass showed periods of snow with some blowing snow as well.
The Pierce COOP reported 5.5 of snow and 1.28 of precipitation during this event. The Elk Butte SNOTEL at 5,690 ft., located 5 miles northeast of Elk River measured 15 of snow from Jan 7-10.

The COOP observer located 1 mile north of Dixie measured 8.8 of total storm snowfall with 0.71 of precipitation. The Savage Pass SNOTEL at 6,170 ft., located 5 miles southeast of Powell, recorded 9 of snowfall with 1.10 of snow water equivalent.

The Grangeville COOP observer reported 1 of total snowfall while the observer located 2 miles west-southwest of Cottonwood recorded 1.2. Web cams at Greer Grade indicated slick conditions at times during the morning of Jan. 9.
The total Jan. 9-10 snowfall for Leadore was 6.5 with 0.37 of precipitation. A person from the public in Salmon reported 4 of snowfall.

After the cold front passed through, air temperatures remained warm in the 30's and 40's and this aided the development of rain & snow showers. After sunset, weather spotters from Libby southward reported freezing rain that formed a glaze of ice on untreated surfaces. Snow covered US-2 from Happy's Inn to Marion, and there were reports of periods of heavy snow and wind gusts to 40 mph associated the showers. A weather spotter reported a foot of standing water on the Champion Haul Road near US-2 in Libby at 9:38 pm MST on Jan. 11. Total snowfall amounts include: 8 Blacktail Ski Resort, 6 at MacGregor Pass Rd. or 10 miles WSW of Marion, 2 5 miles SW of Marion.

As the strong cold front passed through around 1 pm MST on Jan. 11, wind gusts between 45 and 52 mph were felt near populations centers such as Kila and Libby. At 3:06 pm MST, the Zonolite RAWS sensor located at 4,204 ft., 8 miles east-northeast of Libby, recorded a wind gust to 65 mph. The Blacktail Ski Area reported very strong winds that blew down trees across power lines on their access road. Fire personnel responded to several downed trees on power lines between Marion and Kila by 4 pm. MST.

The HADS sensor at Marias Pass reported a total storm precipitation of 0.67 which could have equated to around 6 inches of snow, matching the nearby SNOTEL measurements. A NWS employee reported blowing snow with approximately 5 of snow on the ground as they drove through Marias Pass around 1 pm MST on Jan. 12. An avalanche forecaster reported just under an inch of precipitation mostly in the form of rain. They also reported two avalanches that occurred from natural triggers, but did not affect US-2. The Fielding RAWS sensor recorded a wind gust of 51 mph at 2:42 pm MST on Jan. 11. Other precipitation amounts include: 1.27 Hungry Horse Dam COOP and 0.42 West Glacier COOP.

The Lookout Pass Ski area reported 10 of snow that fell in 11 hours through 6:25 am MST Jan. 12. The MT DOT sensor at Lookout Pass reported wind gusts between 25 and 39 mph from 8 pm to 11:26 pm Jan. 11. The strong winds combined with moderate to heavy snow, most likely caused blowing snow which worsened visibilities. An automobile accident occurred at Lookout Pass around 7:35 pm MST and closed all lanes in both directions on Interstate 90 for some time.

A cold front pushed south and east across the Stevensville area around 2 pm MST and wind gusts were close to 30 mph. Radar echoes revealed showers behind the front which affected the area for an hour afterwards. A National Weather Service employee observed a mountain wave developing behind the cold front across the northern Bitterroot Valley. A person from the public located 6 miles south of Lolo, recorded 88 mph on their home anemometer sometime between 2:30 and 3:15 pm MST. They reported roof shingles blown off their roof and a tree limb fell on their house. Three other homes in that area also saw shingle damage and a few trees were blown down. A weather spotter located 2 miles west-northwest of Stevensville estimated that a 60 mph wind gust occurred at 2:57 pm MST. They reported shingle damage and the top of a tree blew off. The wind gust occurred simultaneously with a rain and snow shower.

A NWS employee observed a small stream that had ran over the Old East Highway northwest of Florence. The combination of rain and snow melt and a cold ground, created conditions for the overland flooding.
The sheriff in Hamilton reported up to 2 of snow fell associated with snow bands. Other reports include: 1.5 Florence and 4 in Grantsdale.

The MT DOT sensor located at milepost 47 on Highway 83 measured a gust to 51 mph at 1:59 pm. The Missoula 911 dispatch reported that there were trees down along Highway 200 and 83 due to the wind. The Snowbowl Ski Resort has to shut down two ski lifts due to the strong winds.

The Lost Trail Ski Resort measured a storm total snowfall of 13.5 in 13 hours and 34 minutes. The MT DOT required chains on towing vehicles at Lolo pass Saturday evening, Jan. 11 through the morning of Jan. 12. From 8 pm MST to 12 am MST Jan. 12, the Lolo Pass SNOTEL reported 4 of heavy snow. Lolo Pass received 14 inches of snow with 2.20 of snow water equivalent from Jan. 10-12.

A person from the public located in Hall reported strong gusty winds near 60 mph. There were a few trees down, mainly dead Lodgepole Pine with diameters around 16 inches at the base. The MT DOT sensor located 8 miles north of Avon on Highway 141, recorded a peak wind gust to 59 mph while its highest sustained wind speed was 45 mph. Other wind reports include: 58 mph 3 miles NNW Racetrack and 53 mph 2 miles WSW of Deer Lodge. The combination of the recent rains and high winds helped to dislodge several rocks onto MT-1 at Flint Creek Hill by the late afternoon.

When the cold front passed through Deer Lodge Airport around 3:20 pm MST, visibility dropped to one-quarter mile due to snow and blowing snow while winds gusted up to 53 mph. These similar conditions were reciprocated at MacDonald Pass by 4:05 pm and at Homestake Pass by 5:10 pm MST with the front. Snow and blowing snow was reported by a spotter in Anaconda from 4:45 pm to 6 pm MST, and they measured 3.5 of snow in 4 hours. Other snowfall amounts include: 7.5 Georgetown Lake, 6 Discovery Ski Resort and 1.5 7 miles south of Butte.
The Lost Trail Ski Resort measured a storm total snowfall of 13.5 in 13 hours and 34 minutes.

There was one tree of unknown size that fell partly onto a house and gutters were knocked partially off of homes in Grangeville. The peak wind gust measured was from the NWS handar located one mile north of Grangeville, at the Grangeville Airport. Strong gusty winds caused a downed power line and started a fire in the Clearwater area of Idaho County around 5:12 am PST.

The first of two avalanches near mile-marker 345 on US-93 that crossed the highway located just south of Lost Trail Pass, was 900 feet in length, 24 feet wide and 6 to 8 feet deep. A second avalanche occurred approximately 18 minutes later at 7:30 am MST at the same location and was 100 feet in length, 12 feet side, and 6 to 8 feet deep. One lane of US-93 was opened up by 8:30 am MST and by 10 am MST all lanes were open. No injuries or vehicle damage was reported.

The MT DOT required that towing vehicles wear chains at Lolo pass Saturday evening, Jan. 11 through the morning of Jan. 12. From 8 pm MST to 12 am MST Jan. 12, the Lolo Pass SNOTEL reported 4 of heavy snow. This sensor recorded 14 total storm snowfall with 2.20 of snow water equivalent from 8 pm PST Jan. 10 through 5 am PST Jan. 12.

The MT DOT sensor located 8.1 miles north-northwest of Avon on MT-141 reported multiple wind gusts over 60 mph. When the peak wind of 75 mph occurred at 8:11 am MST, the sustained wind was 54 mph from the west. The peak wind gust at the Bert Mooney Airport was 61 mph at 10:22 am MST from the west or 270 degrees. Other wind gusts include: 51 mph Anaconda at 10:26 am, 50 mph 2 miles southwest Newcomb at 10:23 am and 48 mph 2 miles south-southeast of Warm Springs at 7:34 am MST.

The MT DOT reported fog in the Kalispell area with temperatures near 20 degrees F. They reported that roads became icy and continued to have ice or black ice through the early afternoon on Jan. 19. A 42 year old male died and another 22 year old male was taken to the hospital for minor injuries after their pickup hit black ice on secondary highway 209, went out of control and ended up in the Swan River. According to the Montana Highway Patrol, the fatality was a combination of driver error and weather: going to fast, not wearing a seat belt and slipping on black ice. The Kalispell International Airport reported dense freezing fog with visibility reduced to one half mile or less beginning at 11:55 pm MST Jan. 18 through 4 am MST on Jan 19. It also reported dense freezing fog from 7:55 am through 11:55 am MST on Jan. 19. The Flathead County dispatch reported that the Kalispell City streets were a sheet of ice before daybreak on Jan 19, but said the impacts were not as great due to it being a Sunday morning.

The MT DOT reported that US-2 had fog and icy conditions from Columbia Falls to Marias Pass. A weather spotter reported a glaze of ice on US-2 between Hungry Horse and Bad Rock Canyon with freezing drizzle at 9:29 am MST on Jan. 19.
The MT DOT reported fog and ice/black ice on Highway 200 and Highway 56 to Bull Lake. They also reported black ice on I-90 from Lookout Pass to St. Regis.

Light freezing rain was reported around 12:25 pm MST on Jan. 29 by a trained spotter located 9.1 miles north-northwest of Noxon at 2,400 ft. They had reported 2.5 of snow that morning before the freezing rain began. The rain changed to all snow by the morning of Jan. 30 as colder arctic air pushed south and west through the area. Total storm snowfall amounts include: 11 Blacktail Mountain SNOTEL, 9.6 30 miles south-southeast of Libby COOP, 6 Olney COOP, and 4.8 one mile northeast of Libby COOP.

A person from the public located 1 mile northwest of West Glacier reported 12 inches of snow that fell in 12 hours ending at 6:15 pm Jan. 29. They also reported whiteout conditions at times. An arctic cold front pushed west through Marias Pass between 7 and 8 pm MST Jan. 29 and then through Bad Rock Canyon by 11:30 pm MST. Between 6 and 12 inches of snow fell before the influx of much colder air, and this caused blowing and drifting of snow along portions of US-2 through the early morning hours of Jan. 30. Snowfall totals include: 9 Hungry Horse Dam COOP, 9 Essex, 6 Pike Creek SNOTEL located 1.6 miles SE of Marias Pass, and 5.6 West Glacier COOP.

Steady snow from the Pacific moisture influx continued through the afternoon of Jan. 29. A few places reported heavy snow including a weather spotter located 4 miles south-southeast of of Creston. This spotter measured 11 of snow through 8 pm MST on Jan. 29. Also a person from the public reported heavy snow in Whitefish between 5 to 8 pm an. 29. Once the arctic cold front made its way into the Flathead Valley around 11 pm MST, strong gusty winds to 36 mph caused blowing and drifting snow especially near Bad Rock Canyon. The MT DOT reported blowing and drifting snow on US-93 in the Mission Valley between 1 and 5 am MST Jan. 30 where 4 to 6 of transportable snow had fallen earlier. Total snowfall amounts include: 10 Bigfork, 10.5 13 miles south of Bigfork, 8.5 Kalispell, 8 Polson & Creston, 7 Somers, 5 Ronan and 4.3 at Kalispell International Airport. There were 11 automobile slide-offs and 16 crashes with several injuries reported between Jan. 29-30.

The MT DOT reported blowing and drifting snow on US-93 from Wye to Arlee during the morning hours of Jan 30. A person from the public reported 7.3 of heavy snow one mile north-northwest of Evaro at 5 am MST on Jan. 30. The MT DOT reported moderate to heavy snowfall on I-90 between St. Regis and Tarkio at 6:16 pm MST on Jan. 30. Consistent snow between 4 to 6 inches fell along Highway 200 near Noxon. An automobile accident with injuries occurred on I-90 1.5 miles east of Alberton, blocking an eastbound lane for 2.5 hours during the evening of Jan. 30. Conditions at the time of the accident were snow-covered and icy roads with light to moderate snowfall. Other total three day snowfall amounts from COOP observers include: 11.8 2 miles northwest of Heron, 10 one west of Haugan, 9 Thompson Falls PH, 7.3 Alberton and 6.6 at Superior.

A person from the public reported whiteout conditions due to blowing snow near Hellgate Canyon with estimated winds gusting near 40 mph around 6:23 am MST on Jan. 30.
