Wind gusts ranged between 45 and 56 mph, which caused a tree to fall onto a house and vehicle in Martin City, and multiple trees down along US-2 between West Glacier and Essex.

High winds across the area led to a few thousand power outages. Additionally, there were a couple reports of trees blown down, part of a roof ripped off in the Upper Miller Creek area, and transmission line damage in the Missoula area.
Strong winds led to 400 to 500 power outages.
A downed tree in the Old Ahsanka Grade area led to 1100 customers losing power, according to Clearwater Power.
Multiple accidents and car slide offs occurred within 1 hour of snow squalls affecting both the I-90 and US-93 highways from Missoula south through Stevensville.
Snow squalls led to multiple accidents and slide offs, mainly along I-90 from Drummond to Deer Lodge.

Moderate to heavy snow fell during the morning commute. The emergency manager stated that the school buses were delayed on their morning routes. Additionally, a spotter reported multiple cases of vehicle slide offs. Snow amounts ranged from 1 to 2 inches at Orofino to as high as 4.6 inches at Woodland, ID.
Strong winds caused power outages along both I-90 and the MT-200 corridors.
There was a report of roof damage and blown over trees near Skalkaho Pass.
A local utility company reported multiple trees on power lines leading to many outages across the region. Some of those power outages lasted up to 48 hours.

Southwesterly wind gusts of 40 mph or higher were observed at Marias Pass from midnight to 600 am on December 1st. A peak gust of 59 mph was observed at midnight. The Montana Department of Transportation reported a large tree blocking the eastbound lane of US Highway 2 at milepost 176. Flathead Electric COOP reported 353 residents without power in the vicinity of Essex, with power being restored by 619 am.

Wind gusts of 30 to 50 mph were observed in the Kootenai/Cabinet region during the morning and afternoon hours of December 1st. The Flathead Electric COOP reported two power outages associated with tree damage, totaling 298 residents.
Freezing rain impacted US Highway 93 from Stryker to Whitefish. The public reported slick conditions and slow travel times.
Freezing rain was reported in Libby during the morning commute of December 8th. Residents reported slick roads and sidewalks.

Freezing rain was reported in the Flathead Valley during the morning commute of December 7th. Impacts were observed at Glacier Park International Airport, as officials noted a ton of deicer was needed. A trained spotter reported a glaze of ice on windshields in Columbia Falls.
A light glaze of ice from freezing rain impacted travel in the Flathead Valley from Kalispell to Bigfork.

Wind gusts in excess of 40 mph were observed in Grangeville from the morning to late evening hours of December 11th. The Idaho County Sheriff's Office reported several cable lines, trees, and a power pole fell down due to strong winds, leading to multiple traffic hazards.

Heavy snow, with rates in excess of one inch per hour, was observed in Elk River, Grangemont, Headquarters, and in higher elevations areas of the northern Clearwater Mountains. One to two feet of snow was measured by area SNOTEL sites, with nine inches of snow being reported in Elk River. 264 residents in Elk River lost power, likely due to snow loading.
A mix of rain and wet snow was observed across valley locations, with generally three to six inches of snow being reported. Mountain area SNOTEL sites measured around one foot of new snow.

Montana Department of Transportation officials reported eight to ten inches of snow impacted US Highway 2 from Essex to Devils Creek on Saturday, with another eight to twelve inches falling by Sunday morning. Mesonet sites from Essex to Marias Pass measured an eight to twelve inch snow depth increase. Southwest wind gusts up to 33 mph were observed at Marias Pass.

A foot or more of snow was measured in Grangeville, leading to power outages and school closures. Avista Utilities reported 4,504 customers without power. The Idaho County Sherriff's office received numerous calls for vehicle slide offs and 20 calls involving downed power lines and power poles.

Heavy snow, wind gusts to 30 mph, and falling temperatures led the Montana Department of Transportation to close I-90 over Homestake Pass between 424 pm and 550 pm. Two inches of snow was measured along the I-90 corridor from Deer Lodge to Butte during a 30 minute period as the front passed.

Heavy snow led Montana Department of Transportation officials to declare severe driving conditions on I-90 over Lookout Pass from milepost 0.0 to 5.0 during the morning hours of December 12th. Numerous accidents occurred, leading to travel delays across Lookout Pass. The Mullan Pass ASOS measured 2.59 inches of precipitation during this event; suggesting at least 18 inches of snow fell for nearby Lookout Pass.

Heavy snow led Montana Department of Transportation officials to declare severe driving conditions on US Highway 12 over Lolo Pass from milepost 0.0 to 4.0 during the morning hours of December 12th. The Lolo Pass Snotel measured 0.40 inches of precipitation between 800 am and noon, suggesting snowfall rates of one inch per hour.
Six to twelve inches of wet heavy snow was observed across valley areas, with one to two feet of snow impacting mountain areas above 5,000 feet.

One to three inches of snow was measured across the Flathead Valley, with little to any accumulation across the Mission Valley. Snow changed to freezing rain by the early morning hours of December 19th. Trained spotters reported a light glaze of ice on area roadways.

Heavy snow, followed by a period of freezing rain was observed along the Highway 200 corridor near the Idaho border. Valley locations near the Idaho border received five to eight inches of snow, with 15 inches at Lookout Pass.
A wintry mix of snow and freezing rain was observed across the Missoula and Bitterroot valleys. One to three inches of snow along with a light glaze of ice made for slick travel conditions.
Heavy snow during the morning commute led to numerous accidents, especially across the Missoula Valley. Dangerous travel conditions led to a two hour delay for Ravalli County school districts.
Snowfall rates around one inch per hour led the Montana Department of Transportation to declare severe driving conditions on US Highway 12 from mile markers 0.0 to 4.0 over Lolo Pass.
Periods of moderate snow led to travel impacts. Two to five inches of snow was observed across valley areas. Finally, a light glaze of ice was observed along the I-90 corridor near Clinton.
Periods of moderate snow led to travel delays along the I-90 corridor. Two to five inches of snow was observed across valley areas.

South wind gusts in excess of 50 mph led to widespread blowing snow across the Camas Prairie in the vicinity of Grangeville. US-95 was closed from 617 pm on December 18th through the morning hours of December 19th. A period of moderate to heavy snow impacted Frei Hill and Greer Grade during the December 19th morning commute.

A snow squall closed travel on US 95 between Grangeville and the Ferdinand County line from 300 pm to 625 pm. A flash freeze was observed on roadways due to the combination of heavy snow, falling temperatures, and wind gusts up to 45 mph. The Idaho County Sheriff's Office responded to multiple vehicle slide offs on US 95.
A peak wind gust of 54 mph was observed Hamilton. Isolated power outages impacted the Bitterroot Valley.
The Idaho Department of Transportation closed US 95 from Whitebird Hill to Cottonwood due to drifting snow and poor visibility. The closure went through the morning commute, lifting around 1000 am.

Wind gusts of 15-25 miles per hour and well below zero air temperatures resulted in extended periods of wind chills of -30F to -50F. The coldest observed wind chill was -52F at the Snowslip sensor above US Highway 2.
A series of heavy snow showers with snowfall rates around one inch per hour impacted Lookout Pass Christmas Eve. A crash closed I-90 westbound on the Idaho side of Lookout Pass.

A period of heavy snow was observed across the West Glacier region Christmas Eve, with snowfall rates around two inches per hour. Temperatures quickly dropped into the single digits as an arctic front moved over the Divide early Christmas morning. Snow and blowing snow was observed on US 2, with wind chills of -10 to -20.

SNOW SQUALL. Snow showers produced gusty winds to 40 miles per hour and low visibility to 1/4 mile near the mouth of Bad Rock Canyon to West Glacier during the evening commute. Dangerous driving conditions were noted.

SNOW SQUALL. Periods of snow and gusty winds occurred during the evening commute. A strong snow shower between 4:30 pm and 6:00 pm resulted in low visibility of less than 1/4 mile and a peak wind gust of 48 miles per hour at Glacier Park International Airport. Both road crews and the public reported very difficult travel conditions during peak snowfall intensity.

Snow showers, wind gusts to 40 miles per hour, and a sharp temperature drop along an advancing arctic front resulted in severe driving conditions on Interstate 90 from near Drummond to Butte. Similar road conditions were observed on US Highway 12 from MacDonald Pass to Elliston.
